# Loco.exe subsystem reference

Current-state map of `Loco.exe`'s subsystems, classes, and globals, as recovered in Ghidra.
This is a **reference organized by subsystem, not a session log** — when new facts land, merge
them into the relevant section (and correct anything they refute) instead of appending
chronology. The session-by-session history lives in `git log` and `docs/PICKUPS_PRIOR.md`.

Conventions: addresses are PE vaddrs (image base 0x400000, identical to Ghidra addresses).
Names follow CLAUDE.md's uncertainty ladder — a `Maybe` suffix means behavior is clear but
purpose is hypothesized. `DAT_XXXXXXXX` means the global is still unnamed in Ghidra. Struct
sizes are pinned from `operator new(N)` call sites unless noted. Known original-engine bugs
are catalogued in `docs/engine-bugs.md`; parked byte-match residuals in `docs/PARKED.md`.

## Memory map and CRT boundary

Single clean app/CRT cutpoint, matching the Yoda-project pattern:

- **App code:** `0x401000`–`~0x465fd0` (~404 KB, ~86% of `.text`).
- **CRT crossover ~`0x466050`**: `__global_unwind2`, `__local_unwind2`,
  `__abnormal_termination`, `__NLG_Notify1`, `__fpmath`, `_strncpy`, `__ftol` (0x466d30),
  `_strchr`/`_strpbrk`/`_strncat`/`_strrchr`/`_strstr`, `__exit` (0x4684f0),
  `WinMainCRTStartup` (0x4689e0), `__amsg_exit`, `__CallSettingFrame@12`, `_abort`,
  `__setdefaultprecision`, `__allmul`, `__seh_longjmp_unwind@4`, `__isindst`,
  `__aulldiv`/`__aullrem`/`__allshl`, `_strcspn`, `_strncmp`, `RtlUnwind` thunk (0x474c60).
- **Tail `0x474df0`–`0x4767c0`**: ~700 auto-labeled `Unwind@<addr>` SEH scope-table funclets
  for the statically-linked CRT's internal `__try`/`__finally`.

### CRT facts that matter to app RE

- **One heap, not two — CORRECTED 2026-07-21 (v319).** `0x465ce0` = `operator new` (retry loop
  + new-handler `0x46ce80`, wraps the alloc helper `0x4673e0` = `__nh_malloc`); `0x465cd0` =
  `operator delete` (wraps `0x466c70`). `0x4673c0`/`0x466c70` were previously modeled as a
  "dedicated resource heap" (`Rf_AllocFromResourceHeap`/`Rf_FreeResourceBuffer`,
  `DAT_004ff268` treated as a distinct heap handle) — **this was wrong.** Byte-diffed against
  `toolchain/vc50/LIB/LIBCMT.LIB`'s `malloc.obj`/`free.obj`, `0x4673c0` is byte-identical to
  the real CRT `_malloc()` (it pushes `DAT_004ff268`, the ordinary new-handler flag global —
  not a heap handle — and tail-calls `__nh_malloc`) and `0x466c70` is byte-identical to the
  real CRT `_free()`. Renamed to `_malloc`/`_free` throughout Ghidra + `src/`
  (`DSoundChannel.h`'s shared extern block + every consumer TU: `Wav.cpp`, `SoundBank.cpp`,
  `LocoBitmap.cpp`, `DPlaySessionMgr.cpp`, `EditCardWnd.cpp`, `CreditsWnd.cpp`) — a pure
  identifier rename, verified zero-byte-diff across every affected TU via `tools/progress.py`
  before/after. So there is genuinely only ONE general-purpose heap in this binary (the
  process default heap via the CRT's small-block allocator, see the `__sbh_*`/`__heap_alloc`
  cluster below) — `operator new`/`malloc`/`free`/`realloc` (the last confirmed as `0x46ee80`,
  byte-identical to `realloc.obj`'s `_realloc`, also v319) all route through it. Some GameNet
  payloads are additionally `HeapAlloc`'d and freed via raw `HeapFree` on the SEPARATE Win32
  process heap (`DAT_004ff7a8`, see the local message queue below) — that one's still real, a
  second allocator to keep straight, just not the one `Rf_Alloc...`/`Rf_Free...` used to imply.
- **File I/O plumbing:** `0x468480` → `fopen` (wraps `0x468440`; `0x40` = `_SH_DENYNO`),
  `0x4681d0` → `fclose`, `0x468610`/`0x468790` → lock-wrapped `fread`/`fseek`.
- **iostream.lib is statically linked and ACTIVELY USED** (the RTTI type-descriptor strings
  at 0x481920–0x481a38 are dead, but the classes are live — constructed for real file I/O,
  just never through RTTI). Named so they aren't re-investigated as app classes:
  `ifstream_DefaultCtor`/`OpenCtor`/`Dtor` (0x463890/0x463970/0x463a80),
  `istrstream_BufferCtor`/`Dtor` (0x464490/0x464550), `ofstream_OpenCtor`/`Dtor`
  (0x465090/0x465180), `filebuf_Open` (0x4652d0), `streambuf_AllocateDefaultBuffer`
  (0x4656f0), `streambuf_SetBuffer` (0x465730, = `streambuf::setb`),
  `strstreambuf_GrowBuffer` (0x464120). The classic MSVC virtual-base-adjusted vtable-store
  idiom (`*(int*)this+4` vbase lookup) marks the `ios`/`istream`/`ostream` diamond. All
  low-priority for transcription — comes free from the real library at Phase 4 link time.
- **ctype internals** `0x469810`/`0x469840`/`0x469870` (locale check + `_pctype`-style table
  at `0x481ea0`) — CRT, not app code. `0x469870` itself remains an unnamed wrapper (calls
  `_isctype(c, 8)`, i.e. an `isspace`-shaped predicate) — not resolved to a real LIBCMT.LIB
  symbol as of 2026-07-21; a good `--symbol`-path candidate for a future session (see below).
- **More CRT internals identified 2026-07-21 (v314) via `tools/extract_lib_member.py` +
  byte-diff against `toolchain/vc50/LIB/LIBCMT.LIB`** (extends the `sprintf`/`_output`/
  `_flsbuf` v313 finding — none of these are referenced from `src/`, all Ghidra-only):
  `_input`/0x46cea0 (the scanf-family parsing engine) plus its own small static helpers
  `_hextodec`/0x46dbe0, `_inc`/0x46dc20, `_un_inc`/0x46dc50, `_whiteout`/0x46dc70 (all four
  bundled in the same `input.obj`, placed contiguously right after `_input`'s own body in the
  final link); `_isctype`/0x46b0c0 (the shared ctype-mask helper `_hextodec`/`_whiteout` both
  call); `_strgtold12`/0x4730e0 (decimal-string → 12-byte extended-float parser, the scanf-side
  counterpart — Ghidra's own function body was 305 bytes too short, not extended over its
  trailing jump-table/case-constant data; the real size is 1936 bytes, confirmed by the next
  function starting exactly there); `_I10_OUTPUT`/0x473870 (`$I10_OUTPUT`, extended-float →
  decimal-string, the sprintf-side counterpart, builds "1#SNAN"/"1#QNAN"/"1#INF" special-value
  text).
- **v314's `0x471cf0`/881B locale-info loader — RESOLVED 2026-07-21 (v315).** It's
  `__get_lc_time` (`inittime.obj`), the CRT's day/month/AM-PM/currency-sign bulk loader for
  `setlocale(LC_TIME, ...)`; its 44×-called per-field helper (`FUN_00473cc0`) is
  `__getlocaleinfo` (`inithelp.obj`, wraps `___crtGetLocaleInfoA`/`GetACP` fallback + a
  `malloc`), and its own trailing "final call" (`FUN_004722b0`) is `_storeTimeFmt` (also
  `inittime.obj`, builds the `"H"`/`"h"` 24-vs-12-hour format-string prefix from 3 more
  `LCTYPE` queries: `LOCALE_STIMEFORMAT`/`LOCALE_ITIME`/`LOCALE_INEGCURR`). Their shared caller,
  `___init_time` itself, was a genuine **Ghidra-missed function gap** — Ghidra had never
  boundaried `0x471c40`–`0x471ced` (174 bytes) as a function at all (the preceding function
  `FUN_00471bb0` ends at `0x471c3d`, then 2 NOPs, then this one starts cold) — `create_function`
  fixed it, matching `inittime.obj`'s own `___init_time` byte-for-byte. Found via the
  `getqloc.obj`/`setlocal.obj` symbol trail: `_setlocale` calls `___init_time`/`___init_numeric`/
  `___init_monetary`/`___init_ctype`/`___init_collate` as externs, each defined in its own
  `init*.obj` (`inittime.obj`/`initnum.obj`/`initmon.obj`/`initctyp.obj`/`initcoll.obj`) — a
  reusable next-step template for the still-unresolved locale bulk-loader at `0x471cf0`'s
  siblings (numeric/monetary/ctype/collate categories weren't chased this session, only time).
- **The C++ EH internals cluster gained its first 2 real identifications 2026-07-21 (v315),
  found via `frame.obj`'s `___InternalCxxFrameHandler` module** (the actual runtime dispatcher
  behind the tiny `___CxxFrameHandler` SEH-handler shim that `/GX` installs per-function —
  `___CxxFrameHandler` itself is a 54-byte wrapper too small to match anything currently opaque
  in this binary, so it's presumably already inlined/shared under one of the ~160 SEH-prologue
  functions rather than sitting as its own opaque `FUN_`): **`FindHandler`**/0x469e60 (mangled
  `?FindHandler@@YAXPAUEHExceptionRecord@@PAUEHRegistrationNode@@PAU_CONTEXT@@PAXPBU_s_FuncInfo@
  @EH1@Z` — `___InternalCxxFrameHandler`'s own static helper, walks a function's `TryBlockMap`
  looking for a matching catch for the exception code/state, checking the `0xe06d7363`
  MSC-exception magic and the `0x19930520` EH-version constant that CLAUDE.md's `/GX` lesson
  bullet already documents) and **`__getptd`**/0x46a870 (`tidtable.obj` — fetches the calling
  thread's per-thread-data block, `FindHandler` reads the cached current-exception pointer from
  it at `+0x6c`/`+0x70`).
- **v315's `FUN_0046aa30` lead RESOLVED 2026-07-21 (v316) — it's `_inconsistency`, NOT
  `terminate`.** v315 flagged it as "close to `hooks.obj`'s `terminate` but diverges at +0x2d"
  and left it unrenamed. `hooks.obj` (the same archive member) actually defines THREE separate
  functions across 3 distinct `.text` sections: `terminate` (144B), `unexpected` (32B), and
  **`_inconsistency`** (110B) — a sibling nobody had extracted yet. `_inconsistency`'s own
  disasm matches `FUN_0046aa30` instruction-for-instruction, including the exact reloc that
  broke the `terminate` hypothesis: `mov eax,ds:0x0` → `?__pInconsistency@@3P6AXXZA` (a
  `.data`-resident global function pointer) at the identical offset where `FUN_0046aa30` reads
  `ds:0x481e84` — `terminate`'s own body reads `__getptd()+0x60` at that point instead, a
  genuinely different instruction sequence. Renamed. `FindHandler`'s other 2 previously-unchased
  callees also resolved this session, both exact byte-for-byte matches (masked relocs only):
  **`_ValidateRead`**/0x4706f0 (`validate.obj`, 32B — wraps `IsBadReadPtr`) and
  **`_GetRangeOfTrysToCheck`**/0x465fd0 (`trnsctrl.obj`, 128B — walks a `TryBlockMapEntry`
  array by nesting depth; both its own internal "index out of range" checks are calls to the
  now-identified `_inconsistency`, a 3rd independent confirmation of that rename).
  `trnsctrl.obj` itself is a goldmine for this cluster, NOT yet fully mined: it also DEFINES
  `_JumpToContinuation`, `_CallMemberFunction0/1/2`, `_UnwindNestedFrames`, `__CxxFrameHandler`
  (64B — does NOT match the still-unidentified 0x46cda8 gap below), `__CxxLongjmpUnwind@4`,
  `_CallCatchBlock2`, `CatchGuardHandler`, `_CallSETranslator`, `TranslatorGuardHandler` — none
  of these were byte-matched against opaque `FUN_`s this session (only `_GetRangeOfTrysToCheck`
  was chased down), a strong next-session lead.
- **v316's `0x46cda8` mystery RESOLVED 2026-07-21 (v317) — it's `_except_handler3`, not
  `__CxxFrameHandler`/`___InternalCxxFrameHandler`.** v316 correctly identified the SEH-frame
  shape (walks a -1-terminated scopetable at `[registrationFrame+0xc]`/`[+8]`, 12-byte
  `{enclosingLevel, filter, handler}` entries) but ruled out the wrong symbol family — this is
  the classic Win32 SEH `__try`/`__except` scope-table walker, not a C++-typed-exception
  dispatcher. `libcmt.lib`'s symbol index has NO `_except_handler3` entry (it's exported with an
  extra leading underscore per MS C name decoration: `__except_handler3`) — `--symbol
  __except_handler3` found it in `exsup3.obj` (not `exsup.obj`, a different member), **189
  bytes, exact size match**, and the disasm is structurally identical instruction-for-
  instruction (same `test [eax+4],0x6` early-out, same `lea ecx,[esi+esi*2]` ×12-byte-stride
  indexing, same filter-then-unwind-then-handler call sequence). Bonus confirmation: Ghidra's
  own signature-matcher had ALREADY independently recognized `__seh_longjmp_unwind@4` as a
  "Library Function - Single Match" starting at exactly `0x46ce65` = `0x46cda8 + 189` — the
  precise byte boundary our size match predicts, and the same two functions sit contiguously
  in `exsup3.obj` too. Renamed `0x46cda8` → `_except_handler3`; `0x46cd90` (13B,
  `SetUnhandledExceptionFilter` wrapper) stays unnamed (too small/generic to symbol-match, low
  priority). Also resolved from the same `trnsctrl.obj` cluster this session: **`
  _CallSETranslator`**/0x465e70 (204B exact — the `_set_se_translator` invocation shim, calls
  `__getptd()[0x1a]`/offset 0x68 exactly matching the `.obj`'s `call [eax+0x68]`) and
  **`_UnwindNestedFrames`**/0x465d40 (86B exact — `RtlUnwind` + clears the
  `EXCEPTION_UNWINDING` bit, `ExceptionFlags &= ~2`). Separately, while chasing
  `__NLG_Notify` (non-local-goto notify, called from `__local_unwind2`): **`__NLG_Notify`**/
  0x466126 (confirmed via the literal absolute reloc `mov ebx,0x481a08` matching `exsup.obj`'s
  own `mov ebx,IMM32` entry — writes `[ebx+8]`/`[ebx+4]`/`[ebx+0xc]` from ecx/eax/ebp, using the
  CALLER's register state with no prologue of its own, the textbook NLG_Notify shape).
  `_JumpToContinuation`/`_CallCatchBlock2`/`CatchGuardHandler`/`TranslatorGuardHandler`
  (96/48/129-byte targets) have NO size-matching candidates anywhere in a fresh full gap-list
  sweep — likely genuinely absent from this binary (the game may never trigger the
  exception-specification/`set_se_translator`-guard-funclet compiler paths that emit them);
  don't keep searching for these three without a new angle. **Bonus finding: `0x465d30` (7B) is
  where the linker FOLDED `_CallMemberFunction0`/`_CallMemberFunction1`/`_CallMemberFunction2`
  into one physical body** — all three source symbols compile byte-identical (`pop eax; pop
  ecx; xchg [esp],eax; jmp eax`), and REAL call sites prove the fold: `0x46a690`/`0x46a6ad` push
  3 args before calling it (matches `_CallMemberFunction1`'s signature) while `0x46a733` pushes
  only 2 (matches `_CallMemberFunction0`'s) — same target address, genuinely different original
  symbols. Left unrenamed (any single one of the 3 names would be confidently wrong) with a
  plate comment documenting the fold; a new lesson for identical-COMDAT-folding worth
  generalizing if it recurs elsewhere in the CRT region.
- **`memmove` identified 2026-07-21 (v316): `FUN_00466ea0`/0x466ea0, 820 bytes.** Found by eye
  (not the symbol trail) — its decompile is the textbook overlap-direction check
  (`if (dest > src && dest < src+n) copy-backward else copy-forward`) — confirmed exact
  byte-for-byte (masked relocs) against `memmove.obj`'s `_memmove`. Renamed.
- **Two more large past-`TOTAL_APP_END` gaps were INVESTIGATED but NOT confirmed this session
  (v316) — do not re-attempt without a new angle:** `FUN_004698a0` (848B) is textbook CRT
  `_sopen`/`_open`-shaped (CreateFileA + oflag/pmode bit-decoding + a `DAT_005007e0`
  `_iob`-style fd table with 0x24-byte stride) but its extracted candidate, `open.obj`'s
  `__sopen` (928B, found via `--symbol __sopen`), has a DIFFERENT prologue shape (`sub esp,0x14`
  stack-frame, no `push ebp`) and a different share-mode dispatch (`cmp eax,0x30;ja` vs. our
  function's `switch` on 0x10/0x20/0x30/0x40) — likely a different source revision of the same
  logical function, not a match; needs a differently-versioned `.lib` or hand-transcription
  instead of extraction. `FUN_00466590` (831B) looks like a `_fullpath`/`_searchenv`-shaped
  path-search helper (`FindFirstFileA`/`FindClose` shapes) but was not symbol-matched at all.
  `FUN_0046dd00` (728B, void/void) was decompiled but not investigated for identity.
- **21 more CRT internals identified 2026-07-21 (v319), plus the malloc/free/realloc identity
  correction documented above.** All via `tools/extract_lib_member.py` byte-diff, none
  referenced from `src/` except the malloc/free/realloc trio (Ghidra-only otherwise, so this
  doesn't move `progress.py`'s EXACT/PARTIAL totals — verified by a full re-run,
  bit-identical). **Extended-precision (80-bit long double) arithmetic cluster**
  (`tenpow.obj`/`mantold.obj`, feeds the already-known `_strgtold12`/`_I10_OUTPUT`
  scanf/sprintf converters): `__ld12mul`/0x473f80 (696B, the software 80-bit multiply used for
  decimal-exponent scaling), its callees `__addl`/0x472ee0 (34B), `__shl_12`/0x472f80 (45B),
  `__shr_12`/0x472fb0 (44B), and its own caller `__multtenpow12`/0x474240 (137B, walks the
  `__pow10pos`/`__pow10neg` lookup tables applying `__ld12mul` per set bit of the power-of-ten
  exponent). **`strtol`/`strtoul` family** (`strtol.obj`): the shared internal engine
  `_strtoxl`/0x469560 (640B) plus its two public 32-byte cdecl wrappers `_strtol`/0x469540 and
  `_strtoul`/0x4697f0 (differ only in the literal radix-signedness flag pushed before the
  shared call). **Small-block-heap (`__sbh_*`) allocator internals** (`sbheap.obj`, the guts of
  `malloc`/`free`/`realloc` — see the "one heap, not two" correction above): `__sbh_alloc_block`/
  0x46c880 (562B, scans a heap region's page array for a big-enough free run),
  `__sbh_alloc_block_from_page`/0x46cac0 (369B, carves a block out of one found page),
  `__sbh_find_block`/0x46c7c0 (88B, locates which region+page owns a given pointer for
  free/realloc), `__sbh_free_block`/0x46c820 (82B), `__sbh_resize_block`/0x46cc40 (196B,
  in-place grow/shrink before falling back to alloc+copy+free) — plus the CRT-level wrappers
  around them: `__heap_alloc`/0x467430 (84B, threshold check + `__lock`/`__sbh_alloc_block`/
  `__unlock` + `HeapAlloc` fallback), `__nh_malloc`/0x4673e0 (the new-handler retry loop
  `operator new` and `_malloc` both tail into), and the primitive lock/unlock pair
  `__lock`/0x46b770 + `__unlock`/0x46b7f0 (`mlock.obj`, lock-id-indexed critical sections; id 9
  = the heap lock, id 0x19 = the MBCS-codepage-table lock below). **Locale time cluster
  closeout**: `__free_lc_time`/0x472070 (562B, `inittime.obj` — the `setlocale(LC_TIME,...)`
  teardown counterpart to v315's `__get_lc_time`, frees each of its ~20 allocated day/month/
  AM-PM strings via `_free`); its sibling helpers `_storeTimeFmt`/`__getlocaleinfo` turned out
  to already be named from v315, nothing left to do in this cluster. **MBCS codepage setup**

  table for a new multibyte codepage, lock id 0x19) and its callee `_getSystemCP`/0x46ea00 (34B,
  resolves the `_MB_CP_ANSI`/`_MB_CP_OEM`/`_MB_CP_LOCALE` pseudo-codepage constants to a real
  `GetACP`/`GetOEMCP`/registry-LCID value). Two of `__setmbcp`'s own callees on its
  codepage-lookup-miss path, `_setSBCS`/0x46eab0 (49B, zeroes the `_mbctype` table; v320
  byte-match) and `_setSBUpLow`/0x46eaf0 (473B, the real `GetCPInfo`-driven table rebuild;
  resolved v321 — see below).

## App bootstrap, config, and the app state machine

**Before `LocoWinMain` runs at all: the CRT constructs 13 global objects.** `WinMainCRTStartup`
(0x4689e0) calls `__cinit` (0x4684a0), which makes two `_initterm` calls — `__xi_a/__xi_z` =
(0x47e03c, 0x47e04c), the C initializers, then `__xc_a/__xc_z` = (0x47e000, 0x47e038), the C++
dynamic initializers. That second table is the **complete, ordered list of every global object in
the game with a constructor**: 13 entries, each pointing at a `mov ecx,<object>; call <ctor>;
push <atexit thunk>; call atexit` thunk, with the matching `mov ecx,<object>; jmp <dtor>` thunk
0x20 bytes later. Recovered in v561 (see `docs/CODEGEN.md` #178) — all 13 ctors are transcribed:

| # | thunk | object | ctor / dtor | class (home TU) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0x45c530 | 0x4a9910 `g_screenSaver` | 0x448040 / 0x448080 | `ScreenSaver` (`src/ScreenSaver.cpp`) |
| 2 | 0x45c560 | 0x4855e8 `g_UIResources` | 0x445f70 / 0x445fe0 | `UIResources` (`src/UIResources.cpp`) |
| 3 | 0x45c590 | 0x4a98b0 `g_PeerTrainSlotQueue` | 0x44d800 / 0x44d860 | `PeerTrainSlotQueueMaybe` |
| 4 | 0x45c5c0 | 0x4854c8 `PlacementCursorMaybe_004854c8` | 0x410510 / 0x410680 | `PlacementCursorMaybe` |
| 5 | 0x45c5f0 | 0x485448 `DecorObjMgrMaybe_00485448` | 0x434500 / 0x4345f0 | `DecorObjMgrMaybe` (`src/DecorActor.cpp`) |
| 6 | 0x45c620 | 0x4a9990 `g_NetSessionEventQueue` | 0x41d250 / 0x41d2d0 | `NetSessionEventQueue` |
| 7 | 0x45c650 | 0x4a99b0 (`g_easterEggMgrMaybe`'s bytes) | 0x41f480 / 0x41f4d0 | `ScriptEventLoader` |
| 8 | 0x45c680 | 0x4fd220 `DAT_004fd220` | 0x4238c0 / 0x4239e0 | `EffectSpawner` |
| 9 | 0x45c6b0 | 0x4aa5b8 `g_BuildToolButton` | 0x449430 / 0x4494e0 | `BuildToolButton` |

The port build reproduces this list explicitly (`port/PortGlobalCtors.h` +
`link/init_globals.cpp`), because its globals come from a zero-filled `.bss` mirror that has no
initializers of its own. #13 is the only one a `src/` TU defines for real, so it is the only one
our own CRT constructs.

**Bootstrap order** (`LocoWinMain` 0x462e90, confirmed): splash dialog → App-object ctor
(`0x4061e0`, singleton `DAT_004aa4a0`; `+8` = main app HWND) → `CoInitializeEx` →
`Config_LoadDirectories` (0x4068d0) → `Locale_DetectLanguage` (0x4463c0) → fatal-exit if
config failed → command-line parser (0x406790) → startup sound (0x4480c0) →
`0x406480`/`0x406680` (window-rect/balancing/color-depth checks) → `0x406ba0` "Run" (mouse
ini, PostBag dirs, client identity, `CreateEventA("GameLoop")`,
`Bootstrap_ConstructSingletonWindows`, `Ddraw_InitTileGridExtent`, `DPlaySessionMgr` ctor at
call site 0x406c9d, `NetSettings` ctor) → message pump.

#### `Main::AppWndProc` (0x4618c0) — the main window procedure

`LRESULT CALLBACK(HWND, UINT, WPARAM, LPARAM)`, **5351 bytes of code (5584 including its five
jump tables) — the single largest function in the app region**, and it was invisible to Ghidra
until v367's `tools/find_unanalyzed.py` sweep created it. Its only reference in the whole binary
is the DATA store at 0x406ef4, where `FUN_00406ed0_CallsCreateWindowExA` puts it in the
`WNDCLASS`; no `call` or `jmp` anywhere targets it, which is why every previous call-graph sweep
missed it. **Transcribed v368** into `src/Main.cpp` (PARTIAL, parked — 1740 instructions to the
original's 1739; see `docs/PARKED.md`).

⚠ **It is NOT an `AppWindow` TU member — it lives in Main.obj.** v367 named it
`AppWindow::AppWindow_WndProc` on subject-matter grounds, but `.text` contiguity settles it:
0x4618c0 runs straight into `Main::LocoWinMain` (0x462e90) and then the rest of the `Main::`
cluster (0x463430, 0x4634f0, 0x463600, 0x463670) before the import thunks at 0x4637c0, while the
preceding run is `ThreadWrapper`'s. Renamed **`Main::AppWndProc`** in v368; WinMain + WndProc in
one file is the classic Win32 layout.

Three layers, in order:
1. `hWnd != g_pApp->hwndOwner` ⇒ straight to `DefWindowProcA`.
2. The screen-saver intercept: `if (g_screenSaver.bScreenSaverMode == 1)`, `ScreenSaver::
   FilterMessage` gets first refusal and the caller switches on its ACTION CODE (0 ⇒ fall
   through to normal handling, 2 ⇒ `return 0`, 3 ⇒ `return 1`, anything else ⇒ `DefWindowProcA`).
3. `WM_DISPLAYCHANGE` (0x7e) is handled before everything else — if the new (width, height,
   bpp) triple differs from `g_dwScreenWidth`/`g_dwScreenHeight`/`g_dwScreenBpp` it hides the
   window, puts up locale string 0x14b behind a re-entrancy guard, and exits.
4. Then TWO switches over the same message: a small **front-end** one used while the app state
   is 0, 1 or 2, and the full **in-game** one for every other state. Both fall through to one
   shared `DefWindowProcA` tail — which is why the app-state test is evaluated twice
   (`if (P()) {front-end}` then `if (!P()) {game}`).

`ScreenSaver::PostQuitRequest`'s WM_USER+5 (0x405) is answered in the front-end switch
(`Sleep(0x14)` + the quit routine at 0x45e400).

The in-game switch's own notable cases:

| msg | behaviour |
|---|---|
| `WM_SIZE` (5) | parks `g_bAppMinimizedMaybe` (0x4851f0) — 1 on SIZE_MINIMIZED, 0 on SIZE_RESTORED, `(state == 0)` on SIZE_MAXIMIZED — plays UI sound 0x5465/0x5467 unless the net subsystem is shutting down, and on SIZE_MAXIMIZED bounces SC_RESTORE/SC_SIZE back at itself |
| `WM_CLOSE` (0x10) | quits when shutting down or in saver mode, else `BuildToolCursorWnd::ShowTool(0, 0)` |
| `WM_NCHITTEST` (0x84) | toggles the software placement cursor's capture on entering/leaving the client area — suppressed while `g_bSizeMoveInProgressMaybe` (0x4ff13c) is set |
| `WM_KEYDOWN` (0x100) | non-printable keys only. VK_RETURN opens build mode (`SetDescriptorMaybe(0x2400,…)` + UI mode 4); **VK_ESCAPE or `'VK_Q'`** posts WM_CLOSE. ⚠ `'VK_Q'` is a FOUR-CHARACTER LITERAL (0x564b5f51), not a virtual-key code — dead by construction, reproduced with `// sic:` |
| `WM_CHAR` (0x102) | printable keys, upper-cased via the CRT's `_toupper`; offers them to `g_pActiveTabWidgetMaybe`'s vtable slot 16 first, then 'Q' = quit, 'W' = 0x407d00 |
| `WM_HSCROLL`/`WM_VSCROLL` | `g_pApp->FUN_00407ae0/bf0_CallsSetScrollRangePos(lParam, delta)` with ±4 / ±0x100 / an absolute thumb position relative to `g_worldBoard.dwScrollX/Y` |
| `WM_MOUSEMOVE` (0x200) | forwarded wholesale to the tutorial window while app state is 8; otherwise latched into the placement cursor, which ticks immediately in state 4 unless the held kind's category is 5 |
| 0x201–0x206 | each latches one of the placement cursor's four (pending, packed pos) mouse-action quartets and falls through to `DefWindowProcA` |
| `WM_SIZING` (0x214) | the live drag-resize clamp — bounds the client area to the board extent and to 0x80 board pixels per axis (via `AdjustWindowRect` on `GWL_STYLE` + `SM_CXFRAME`/`SM_CYFRAME`), re-anchors both scrollers, then dirties the four strips the resize exposed and repaints |
| 0x231 / 0x232 | `WM_ENTERSIZEMOVE`/`WM_EXITSIZEMOVE`: raise/lower `g_bSizeMoveInProgressMaybe`; on exit re-cache `g_rectAppWindowBounds`/`g_rectAppClientBounds`, recentre the viewport and redraw the whole board |
| `WM_USER+1` (0x401) | a `switch (wParam)` command port: 0 = leave multiplayer/return to front end, 5/6/7 = the savegame picker's load/save/(0x429dd0), 8 = raise `g_pMailWnd->bMailPendingMaybe` and switch to UI mode 5, 9 = checkpoint `_curr` → reload another slot → re-link, 0xa = purge duplicate album cards, 0xb = detach the train hanging off the board object in lParam. **Its jump-table bodies are emitted in SOURCE order and the original's starts at case 8** |
| `WM_USER+2/3/4/6/8` | per-frame object dispatch, each gated on "not shutting down" and each bumping its own counter (`DAT_004ff12c`/`118`/`128`): +2 and +8 call vtable slots 15/18 on the object in wParam, +3 goes to the decor-object manager (0x485448), +4 to `g_easterEggMgrMaybe` (0x4a99b0), +6 to `UIResources::TickStationClockChimeMaybe(wParam, 0)` |

Globals this function pinned down (all renamed in Ghidra v368): **`g_dwScreenBpp`** (0x48521c,
`GetDeviceCaps(hdc, BITSPIXEL)`, written by 0x406680), **`g_bAppMinimizedMaybe`** (0x4851f0,
ex-`DAT_004851f0` — `WorldBoardMaybe::UpdateDirtyTiles` reads it as its "== 1 suppresses the
update" gate), **`g_rectAppWindowBounds`** (0x485200, ex-`tagRECT_00485200`) and
**`g_rectAppClientBounds`** (0x485220, ex-`tagRECT_00485220`) — the cached `GetWindowRect` and
`GetClientRect` of `hwndOwner`. It also proved **0x407ae0/0x407bf0 are `AppWindow` MEMBERS**
(every call site loads ecx = g_pApp) and that **`BuildToolButton::nButtonStateMaybe` (+0x740) is
2 bytes wide**, not the int the widget-family gap arithmetic had implied — this function's
`mov WORD PTR ds:0x4aacf8,1` is its only WRITE anywhere in `.text`. ⚠ Corrected 2026-07-31
(v525): it is not the only ACCESS. `BuildToolButton::OnKeyDownMaybe` (0x44adf0) READS it, gating
its entire body on `== 3` — so this field and the button assembly's open/close animation states
1/2/3 are one enum, the same one `AdvanceAnimFrameMaybe`'s slide and `BlitAllRegionsMaybe`'s
"only in state 3" icon blit are keyed on.

### The head of the AppWindow .obj (0x4061e0–0x4068c4), transcribed v488

The `.obj` does NOT start at 0x4068d0. The six functions from **0x4061e0 to 0x4068c4** sit
immediately before it and belong to the same translation unit — they were simply never opened,
because nothing in `src/` referenced them except two file-local `extern` declarations. All six are
now in `src/AppWindow.cpp`; four are EXACT.

| addr | name | size | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0x4061e0 | `AppWindow::AppWindow(HINSTANCE)` | 190 | EXACT first compile |
| 0x4062a0 | `??_GAppWindow` (scalar deleting dtor) | 57 | EXACT — see the polymorphism note below |
| 0x4062e0 | `AppWindow::ReadOwnFileVersion` | 416 | PARTIAL, `docs/PARKED.md`; ex-`FUN_004062e0_DplayRelated` |
| 0x406480 | `AppWindow::LoadWindowAndBalancing` | 500 | PARTIAL, `docs/PARKED.md` |
| 0x406680 | `AppWindow::CheckMinimumDisplaySpec` | 265 | EXACT; ex-`FUN_00406680_ChecksHighResModeRelated` |
| 0x406790 | `AppWindow_ParseCommandLine` | 308 | EXACT first compile; `__cdecl` free function |

⭐ **`AppWindow` IS A POLYMORPHIC CLASS, and its vtable (0x4774c4) has exactly ONE slot** — the
scalar deleting destructor at 0x4062a0. The class is now modelled with a real
`virtual ~AppWindow()` instead of the `char padVtbl[4]` that had held offset 0 open; this is
layout-neutral (`sizeof` stays 0x28, every field offset unchanged) and it retired both of
`src/Main.cpp`'s TU-local look-alike views. The dtor's body must be defined IN-CLASS — the
original inlines it into the `??_G` thunk and emits no separate `??1` anywhere in the image.

⭐ **The four `dwFileVersion*` fields are PINNED.** They were recorded for many sessions as four
opaque dwords of unknown purpose, known only from `GameNetThreadState::GameNet_DispatchMessage`
copying them verbatim into the 0x3e9 "who are you" handshake reply. `ReadOwnFileVersion` is where
they come from: it pulls the app's own `\StringFileInfo\080904B0\FileVersion` string out of its
VERSIONINFO resource and splits the comma-separated "a, b, c, d" form with `strtok`. They are the
build version a multiplayer peer is told about. (The strtok continuation is hand-rolled — each
subsequent call restarts explicitly at `pszTok + strlen(pszTok) + 1` rather than passing `NULL`.)

**`AppWindow::CheckMinimumDisplaySpec` (0x406680)** is the minimum-spec gate shown once at
startup. The display must be a non-palette device (`GetDeviceCaps(NUMCOLORS)` returns −1 above
8bpp) of at most 16bpp, a mouse must be present (`SM_MOUSEPRESENT`), and the desktop must be
between 800 and 1280 pixels wide. Any failure puts up localized string 0x7a (display) or 0x7b
(no mouse) in a `MessageBoxA` titled "LEGO LOCO" and returns 0, which aborts the launch.

**`AppWindow_ParseCommandLine` (0x406790)** takes two things off the command line: the `-s`
screen-saver switch (what the Windows control panel passes when launching a `.scr`) and an
optional season-name override — `Easter`/`Desert`/`Halloween`/`Winter`/`XMas` map to
`g_forcedSeason` (0x485230) 1..5, overriding the calendar-derived season the easter-egg manager
would otherwise pick. `sic:` the delimiter set is `" /"`, so `/` is consumed as a separator and no
token can ever begin with it — which makes the `"/s"` comparison, tested first of the three,
permanently dead. `-s` and a bare `s` both work.

⚠ **The ini section name is `"WINDOW_ATTRIBUTES"` with an UNDERSCORE** (byte 0x5f, read out of the
image at 0x47e1a0). `src/AppWindow.cpp` carried `"WINDOW ATTRIBUTES"` with a SPACE at four sites
for many sessions — the v395 Ghidra-label-mangling trap, and invisible to every check we have
because string CONTENT is never compared (only the relocation to it, which is masked). Fixed v488.

⚠ **`g_dwScreenWidth`/`g_dwScreenHeight`/`g_dwScreenBpp` are SIGNED `int`**, not `unsigned` as two
TUs had declared them — pinned by `LoadWindowAndBalancing`'s signed `/2` (`cdq; sub; sar`) and by
`CheckMinimumDisplaySpec`'s `jle`/`jge`/`jg` bounds tests. The full geometry set this TU owns:
`g_dwScreenWidth` 0x4851d8, `g_dwScreenHeight` 0x485214, `g_dwScreenHalfWidth` 0x4851f8,
`g_dwScreenHalfHeight` 0x4851fc, `g_dwScreenBpp` 0x48521c, and **`g_rectScreenBounds` 0x4851e0**
(ex-`tagRECT_004851e0`), the whole desktop as a rect.

### The display-mode cluster (0x407ae0–0x407d20), transcribed v421

`src/Bootstrap.cpp` was renamed **`src/AppWindow.cpp`** in v421 — the TU's real identity is the
app singleton (the `.text` run from 0x4061e0 to 0x408a30 is the Ghidra `AppWindow` namespace),
and `src/AppWindow.h` was already its header. Twenty-two of its functions are now transcribed;
seventeen are EXACT.

**`AppWindow::ApplyDisplayModeMaybe` (0x407d20, ex-`FUN_00407d20_SetsWindowPos_ScrollBarIdk`,
`__cdecl(char bFullscreen)`)** is the windowed/fullscreen switch. `bFullscreen == 0` installs
`WS_POPUP|WS_VISIBLE|WS_CLIPCHILDREN|WS_OVERLAPPEDWINDOW|WS_VSCROLL|WS_HSCROLL` (0x92ff0000),
raises `g_bBoardScrollFlag`, restores the window to `g_rectAppWindowBounds` and then shrinks the
frame back to the board if the client area now exceeds the whole viewport. `bFullscreen != 0`
returns immediately unless the viewport is at least as wide as the screen, then installs
`WS_POPUP|WS_VISIBLE|WS_CLIPCHILDREN|WS_MAXIMIZE` (0x93000000, plus both scroll-bar bits when the
board is wider than the screen and we are NOT in screen-saver mode), clears `g_bBoardScrollFlag`,
and sizes the window to `g_dwScreenWidth`×`g_dwScreenHeight` — `HWND_TOPMOST` in saver mode,
`SWP_NOZORDER` otherwise. Both paths bracket themselves with a full-viewport `MarkRectDirty`, and
the shared tail re-caches `g_rectAppClientBounds`, recentres the viewport, and — when the scroll
bars are hidden but the board still overflows the screen in attract mode — parks the scroll offset
in the middle, since nothing can scroll it. Still PARTIAL (asmscore 229933), see `docs/PARKED.md`.

**`AppWindow::ToggleWindowedModeMaybe` (0x407d00, ex-`FUN_00407d00`)** is the 'W' key: it reads
`g_bBoardScrollFlag` (which therefore doubles as "we are currently windowed") and calls the above
with the opposite mode. EXACT.

**`AppWindow::ScrollBoardHorizontal` / `ScrollBoardVertical` (0x407ae0 / 0x407bf0,
ex-`FUN_00407ae0_CallsSetScrollRangePos` / `FUN_00407bf0_...`)** are an exact mirror-image pair,
both EXACT. Each takes the originating WM_HSCROLL/WM_VSCROLL `lParam` (never read) and a signed
pixel delta, clamps `g_worldBoard.dwScrollX`/`dwScrollY` into `[0, nMaxPos]` — where `nMaxPos` is
how much of the viewport does not fit in the client area — recentres and repaints, and mirrors the
new offset into the real scroll bar via `SetScrollRange`/`SetScrollPos`, but only when
`g_bScrollBarsVisible`. A viewport that already fits (`nMaxPos <= 0`) returns early WITHOUT
repainting.

**`AppWindow::BuildTool_SetAutoCurveConnectModeMaybe` (0x4089d0)** is the build-tool mode setter
for `DAT_00485234` (0 = no tool, 1 = bulldoze, 2 = place). A no-op when the mode is unchanged;
otherwise it stores it and fixes up `PlacementCursorMaybe_004854c8.nTypeIdMaybe` and the still
unnamed companion byte `DAT_004aa7dc`, and dirties the board
(`g_worldBoard.bBoardDirtyNeedsRebuildFlag`) when entering either live tool mode. EXACT.

**`AppWindow::ReadHklmValue` (0x408a30)** — EXACT, and behaves as `src/AppWindow.h` already
described it.

New global named in Ghidra: **`g_bScrollBarsVisible`** (0x485238, ex-`DAT_00485238`) — "the board
scroll bars are currently shown". Every write is paired with a `ShowScrollBar` of matching
polarity; the two scrollers above read it as their "there is a scroll bar to update" gate; also
written by the app ctor (0x406247) and the config loader (0x4064f1).

Sibling found by the same sweep: **`AppWindow::App_LoadWorldThreadProcMaybe` (0x45de40, 591 B)**,
the world-load THREAD procedure (`ThreadWrapper::Start(0x45de40, 0)` at 0x4084a5, also a

failure — then spins on app-state `g_nScreenState` until it reads 1 or 10, and finally loads the
board layout: `ScreenSaver::GetLayoutFileName` in saver mode, `Layouts\<provider long name>` when
`g_pDPlaySessionMgr->connectionMode == 2`, else `_curr`. Ends with `ScreenSaver::PostQuitRequest`.

### The AppWindow window/session cluster (0x406e80–0x406ed0, 0x4085e0, 0x4086f0), transcribed v422–v423

**`AppWindow::CreateMainWindow` (0x406ed0)** registers the app's one window class, `"LEGO LOCO"`
(`CS_HREDRAW|CS_VREDRAW|CS_DBLCLKS`, icon resource 101, no class cursor or background brush, window
proc = `Main::AppWndProc`) and creates the app's single top-level window — `WS_POPUP|WS_CLIPCHILDREN`
at the screen origin, `g_dwScreenWidth` × `g_dwScreenHeight`, class name reused verbatim as the
window title. **`WS_EX_TOPMOST` is added only when `g_screenSaver.bScreenSaverMode == 1`**, so
nothing can draw over attract mode. Stores the HWND into `hwndOwner`, caches `GetClientRect` into
`g_rectAppClientBounds`, and returns 0 if `CreateWindowExA` failed. PARKED at 64/64 instructions —
one register, see docs/PARKED.md.

**`AppWindow::AbortMultiplayerSession` (0x406e80)** is the multiplayer-abort / return-to-front-end
path, reached from `src/DPlaySessionMgr.cpp` after a "connection lost"-shaped `MessageBoxA`. Tears
the DirectPlay session down via **`GameNet::TeardownAllSessionState` (0x43f7b0**, newly named — the
full teardown: posts the provider-teardown notification, drains both pending-node lists through each
node's own virtual dtor, walks the 9 layout slots freeing each one's node chain and display buffer,
resets the providers, drops the mode to 0, and posts the teardown notification again; its ONLY caller
in the binary is this function), raises the still-unmodeled `g_pApp+0x10` flag, ducks the sound
manager, resets the board's tiles and the peer train-slot registry, then hands the app to screen
state 2. EXACT. **0x43f7b0 itself is transcribed as of v519** (`src/DPlaySessionMgr.cpp`,
EFFECTIVE-parked DIFF(4) at the exact 204 B, insns 68/68 — the whole residual is one
push-vs-ecx-load scheduling swap at the `SetMode(0)` call): the head-of-list loads hoist
BEFORE the queueSourceId/searchProviderId zero pair, both node-list drains re-load the walk
variable from the head field after each delete, and the 9-slot result-chain + layout-blob
cleanup is the hoisted-pointer form (esi anchors at `pLayoutData`), NOT `ResetProviders`'
direct-subscript form.

**`AppWindow::DrainQueuedMouseInput` (0x4085e0)** drains the run of mouse input at the head of the
message queue, stopping at the first message that is not `WM_SETCURSOR`, `WM_MOUSEMOVE` or one of the
left/right button up/down pair. Its `bDiscard` argument selects between throwing the input away
(forcing the cursor off rather than letting the window proc choose one) and translating+dispatching
each message on the way past. Called wherever a blocking animation has held the main pump and the
clicks that piled up behind it must not fire against UI that has since changed — the transition
sequencer `FUN_00408350_PlaysSound` (0x408350) does it at five points and
`AnimateDecalPickerPageWipe` (0x41923a) once. EXACT.
Two details worth keeping: **`WM_LBUTTONDBLCLK` (0x203) is deliberately absent** from the button
run, so a double-click ENDS the drain instead of being eaten (the jump table routes 0x203 to the
default arm); and the `WM_SETCURSOR`+`bDiscard` arm is the one arm that does NOT remove the message,
which would spin forever if `WM_SETCURSOR` could ever be *posted* — it cannot, it is only ever sent,
so the path is dead by construction and is reproduced with a `// sic:`.

**`ConstructSingletonWindows` (0x406f90) takes a real `AppWindow *` as of v422.** Its parameter had
been modeled as a separate `BootstrapAppContext` struct, which was a partial view of AppWindow itself
under another name (its `+0x8` "hwndParent" IS `AppWindow::hwndOwner`, `+0xc` IS `hInstance`) — the
same duplicate-struct hazard `src/AppWindow.h`'s header note records cleaning up twice before. So the
eight singleton windows are created as children of the app's OWN window, not of some other parent.
Still EXACT at 2052 B after the retype.

**`AppWindow_LoadConfigDirectories` (0x4068d0, 712 B) — transcribed v426, PARTIAL at asmscore 21**
(every one of its 242 instructions matches, at the original's exact length; see `docs/PARKED.md`).
The lowest-addressed function in the TU and the app's install-path bootstrap. It opens HKLM
`SOFTWARE\Intelligent Games\LEGO LOCO\Path` for its default value; if either the open or the query
fails it **self-heals** — `_getcwd` into the same buffer and `RegCreateKeyExA`/`RegSetValueExA` the
result back so the next run finds it. Then it appends `\` + `lego.ini`, constructs the `IniFile`
singleton (`g_pIniFile`, `new_alloc(0x10c)`) on that path, and reads the two directory settings:
`[DIRECTORIES] Res` (default `.\`) into `g_pInstallPathPrefix` and `[DIRECTORIES] RemoteRes`
(default `""`) into `g_szRemoteResPath` (ex-`DAT_004a97a8`, named v426 — its only reader or writer
in the whole binary is this function). Attract mode forces `RemoteRes` empty. Both paths are
normalised to end in `\`, but the install prefix is `_stat`ed **without** its separator first —
the return value, which gates a hard startup failure in `LocoWinMain`, is
`_stat(prefix) == 0 && strlen(prefix) > 2` (unsigned; a bare drive root fails it like an empty
setting does). `sizeof(IniFile)` is 0x10c and `src/IniFile.h` now carries its real fields
(`char iniPath[260]` at +0x4, `int Unk0x108`), transcribed from Ghidra's own struct DB — modelling
it as an opaque view had silently made `sizeof` 4 and compiled the allocation as `push 4`.

**`AppWindow::EnterBuildMode` (0x4086f0, 732 B incl. its trailing jump table) — EXACT (v423).**
Screen state 3's arm of `AppWindow_SetScreenState`, i.e. "get the player back onto the live
world board". Its only caller passes the state being **left**, not entered, which is why the switch
runs over values the dispatcher itself treats as destinations — each arm is the teardown for one
departing screen and the shared tail is the world resuming:

- **case 1 (start game)** — the world has just finished loading: settle the display mode against the
  board's viewport (`AppWindow_ApplyDisplayModeMaybe`), retire the loading timer, publish the layout
  bitmap, kick the game tick (`WM_APP+6` / 0x406 carrying `g_dwGameTick`), honour
  `[ScreenSaver] Sound` from `lego.ini` while in screen-saver mode, force one board rebuild, and let
  the tutorial fire its stage-5 notification. **Falls through into case 4**, which does the rest.
- **case 4 (auto-curve connect)** — kick the tick, publish the layout, take the placement cursor
  back, drive the easter-egg manager, and rebuild the board if anything dirtied it while the tool
  was up.
- **case 2 (front end)** — refuses the transition: parks the state selector back on 2 and returns
  WITHOUT running the shared tail.
- **cases 5/6/7 (mail, album, edit card)** — close all three card-family windows (they share a
  screen), un-duck the sound manager, take the cursor back, and dirty the whole viewport.
- **case 9 (map)** — the same, for the map window alone.

The shared tail resumes both decor-object registries (`DecorObjMgrMaybe::FUN_00434800(1)`), both
effect collections (`EffectSpawner::BroadcastToAllEffectsMaybe(1)`) and the four board train slots
(`PeerTrainSlotQueueMaybe::DispatchActiveSlotsMaybe(1)`), restarts the world idle pump on
`g_worldLoadThread`, clears the pending build-tool selection if `DAT_00485234` is up, and refreshes
the cursor for the new app state.

### LoadingScreen — the cold-start "please wait" overlay (`src/LoadingScreen.cpp`, 0x45de40..0x45e484)

A whole small TU found v435, invisible to both forms of the unclaimed-function sweep because it is
bracketed by two DIFFERENT TUs (`src/TrackGraph.cpp`'s run ends at 0x45de39, `src/GameNet.cpp`'s
`GNetManager` block starts at 0x45e490). Five functions, four byte-matched.

The screen is one global `AnimDescRefObj0x477488` on resource id 0x402 (`DAT_004fd3d8`), centred a
quarter of the way across the display and vertically on its own art's native height.
`AppWindow_StartGame` raises it with `LoadingScreen_Show` (0x45e090: stop sound, whiten the client
area through the DirectDraw work surface's GDI DC, build and place the animation), pumps it between
each window's backdrop realization via `LoadingScreen_Pump` (0x45e1e0 → `WM_USER+7`) →
`LoadingScreen_Animate` (0x45e210), and `AppWndProc` tears it down on `WM_USER+5` with
`LoadingScreen_Hide` (0x45e400). `LoadingScreen_Animate`'s non-zero argument runs a four-frame
flourish by hand (75 ms beats, holding the last 250 ms) rather than the ordinary one-frame tick.
⚠ `DAT_004fd3d4` is a never-constructed twin: nothing in `.text` ever assigns it a non-NULL value,
yet both this TU and `AppWindow::SaveWindowAndCleanExit` still delete it. Vestigial; reproduced.

`App_LoadWorldThreadProcMaybe` (0x45de40) is the off-thread world load `AppWindow_StartGame` hands
to `g_worldLoadThread`. It brings up the subsystems too slow for the UI thread — placement sounds,
the seasonal `ee.ini` `[TimeEvents]` table, the build-tool and train-coupling menu icons, the
category icon toolbox — each failure closing the app with its own numbered `WM_CLOSE` code (1, 3, 5,
6, 7). It then spins until the UI thread settles on screen state 1 and picks the board layout: the
screen saver's randomly-chosen one, else the connected provider's `Layouts\<name>`, else the
`"~curr"` checkpoint — the last only if the previous run set `[PROCESS] CleanExit`. (sic: it also
`sprintf`s the install path into a 256-byte local that nothing ever reads.)

### ScreenSaver — the attract-mode / Windows-screen-saver controller (`g_screenSaver`, 0x4a9910)

**LEGO LOCO ships as a dual-personality executable.** Launched with `-s` / `/s` / `s` on the
command line (`AppWindow::ParseCommandLine`, 0x406790) it runs as a genuine Win32 screen saver:
full-screen demo session, no multiplayer setup wizard, dismissed by the first key press or mouse
button (or the third mouse move), optionally gated behind the system screen-saver password.
Identified and modelled v366, completed v367 (`src/ScreenSaver.h` / `src/ScreenSaver.cpp`,
**7/9 EXACT** — every member transcribed; only `FilterMessage` and `EnterDemoSession` are
non-exact, both parked).

⚠ **The flag long modelled as a free global `g_bCmdlineSFlagSet` (0x4a9918) is member +0x08 of
this object**, and `DAT_004a991c` / `DAT_004a9920` are +0x0c / +0x10. The ctor at 0x448040 is
reached with `mov ecx,0x4a9910` and writes all of them through `this`. The ~24 sites across the
binary that read 0x4a9918 absolutely are ordinary `g_screenSaver.bScreenSaverMode` accesses on a
statically-known global — a member access on a global object compiles to an absolute address, so
"read as a bare `DAT_`" was never evidence of a separate variable. Cross-check any other
"newly discovered singleton" the same way before assuming a global is standalone.

`FilterMessage`'s return value is an ACTION CODE, not an LRESULT — the caller at 0x461955 does
`sub eax,0 / je`, `sub eax,2 / je`, `dec eax / je`: 0 = not handled, 2 and 3 = two distinct
caller-side epilogues, anything else (i.e. 1) = fall through to `DefWindowProcA`. It intercepts
`SC_CLOSE` and `SC_TASKLIST` (logging `sc_close intercepted` / `sc_tasklist intercepted` via
`OutputDebugStringA`) so Alt+F4 and the task list cannot escape the saver.

### FrameDriver — the per-frame pump pair (`src/FrameDriver.cpp`, v495)

**`FrameDriver_TickMaybe`** (0x45c3c0, EXACT, 339 B — long mislabeled `LocoBitmap::FUN_0045c3c0`
in Ghidra, and mis-described in old notes as an "app shutdown fn") is THE frame driver: the
in-game message loop (src/Main.cpp) calls it once per presented frame, gated on the
`DAT_00485444` latch, and it clears that latch on entry. **`GameLoopTimerProcMaybe`**
(0x45c520, EXACT, 10 B) is the 28 ms `timeSetEvent` callback the bootstrap arms
(src/AppWindow.cpp) whose entire body is raising that latch — the pump itself runs on the
main thread. Per frame the tick: re-stamps `g_dwGameTick` from the wall clock (`time()` —
this is the "timer proc ... re-_time()s it" the ScriptEventLoader singleton notes refer to),
drains the net event queue (`GameNet_DrainEventQueue`, when `g_pDPlaySessionMgr` exists),
ticks `g_screenSaver`, then — unless the app is front-end (states 1..2) or quitting (10) —
runs every per-frame subsystem: the peer-train sound suspend/resume refresh (the two
`SetSoundStateMaybe(2)/(0)` sweeps over `g_PeerTrainSlotQueue.aSlots`, gated on the
`DAT_004ff124`/`DAT_004ff11c` latch pair) bracketing `DrainPendingSlotsMaybe`, the
`EffectSpawner` tick (0x423d70), the placement cursor and build-toolbar anim ticks, and — in
states 3/9 only — the selection widget (0x42d1a0), `g_worldActionCursor`, the session event
queue (0x41dd40) and `DecorObjMgrMaybe::TickCategory7And8Maybe`, finishing with
`g_worldBoard.UpdateDirtyTiles(0)`. The original .obj also OWNED the 13 app-wide singleton
definitions whose CRT static-init/atexit thunk pairs run 0x45c530..0x45c790 (including
`g_worldLoadThread`, which src/FrameDriver.cpp therefore defines) — the thunk region stays
unclaimed; the .obj bracket is `GetDSoundErrorString` (0x45c2e0, unclaimed) above and
GeomUtil's pair (0x45c7a0/0x45c7c0) below.

### Top-level app state machine

**`AppWindow_SetScreenState`** dispatches over the global app state **`g_nScreenState`**
(25+ xrefs — a general app/game-state global, not net-specific). `param_1` is the NEW state;
the prior value of `g_nScreenState` (old state) is passed on to a couple of per-state handlers
(see state 3 below). Known states: 1 = start game (`FUN_00408350_PlaysSound`), 2 = main
menu(?), **3 = build/tile-placement mode**, **4 = auto-curve track connect tool** (RESOLVED
2026-07-13, see below), 5 = `MailWnd`, 6 = `AlbumCardWnd`, 7 = `EditCardWnd`, 8 = `TutorialWnd`,
9 = `MapWnd`, 0xa = quit/cleanup. Value **10** reads as "tearing down" everywhere it appears
(both GameNet queues stop enqueueing at 10). This is one level above each window's own
internal `state` field. States 2/3 bodies still mostly unread.

**RESOLVED 2026-07-13: state 4 = "auto-curve track connect" tool, a build-mode sub-tool.**
Entered by pressing a build-toolbar toggle button, handled by
`BuildToolButton::OnPressReleaseMaybe` (class identified 2026-07-13 — see "The
`BuildToolButton` widget family" below): on press it calls
`AppWindow_SetScreenState(4)` directly and plays a click effect (id `0x3879`) at the
button position; on release it calls the new `BuildTool_SetAutoCurveConnectModeMaybe(0)`
(ex-`FUN_004089d0`) but does NOT itself transition back to state 3 (that happens elsewhere, not
yet traced). `BuildTool_SetAutoCurveConnectModeMaybe` (`DAT_00485234`, 0/1/2) is a companion
mode flag: 1 = single-tile auto-connect, 2 = footprint/area auto-connect — both mark
`DAT_004aad08.bBoardDirtyNeedsRebuildFlag` (`WorldBoardMaybe+0x52491`; **CORRECTED 2026-07-20** —
formerly misnamed `bTrackGraphsBuiltMaybe`/`bTrackGraphsBuiltFlag` here, but it is a SEPARATE
byte from the real track-graphs-built flag at `+0x52490`; see `WorldBoardMaybe`'s field list
below) dirty — a "board dirty, needs rebuild+autosave" flag, also read by
`BuildToolButton::OnPressReleaseMaybe` on button-release to decide whether to autosave and
cleared by `AppWindow_SetScreenState`'s big switch case 4. While in state 4: `PlacementCursorMaybe::UpdateCursorForAppStateMaybe`
picks `SelectCursorTypeAutoCurveMaybe`, which auto-orients the cursor's curved-track id based on
which `WorldBoardMaybe` viewport edge the cursor is near; and the per-tick
`PlacementCursorMaybe::RefreshFootprintHighlightMaybe` (0x410d20, ex-`FUN_00410d20`; gated on
`g_nScreenState==4` and `DAT_00485234`) highlights the plane-A slots under the cursor footprint
(single tile vs multi-tile area per the mode flag) by setting their `nBlitFlags` to the `0x400`
highlight-overlay id. Entering state 4 (`AppWindow_SetScreenState` case 4)
cancels any active drag (`FUN_004113a0(&PlacementCursorMaybe, NULL)`), deactivates
`DecorObjMgrMaybe`/peer-train-slot dispatch, and invalidates the track graphs; returning to
state 3 from state 1 or state 4 (`FUN_004086f0_BigSwitch` cases 1/4, shared tail) re-enables
both and — if the graphs were already built — calls
`DecorObjMgrMaybe::RestoreEntryPositionsMaybe`. Open: the exact trigger that transitions back
from 4 to 3; no dedicated "owner" class was found for the button (it's invoked flatly from
message-dispatch code around `0x462a00`, not through an OOP container).

**2026-07-25/26 (v393-v395) — the class is FULLY TRANSCRIBED (`src/BuildToolButton.cpp`,
9+5/14 exact, 1547 B byte-identical). NO member is unclaimed.** The unclaimed functions in the
`0x449430`-`0x44a9d0` block were all `BuildToolButton` members; `0x4497a0` (1113 B) was the
largest unclaimed gap in the app region and is content-complete (insns 353/352).

v395 closed the last two: `0x44a9d0` `OnPressReleaseMaybe` (432 B incl. its jump table) is an
EXACT MATCH, and `0x449600` `InitMenuIconsMaybe` (413 B) is content-complete at DIFF(311).
The class's remaining non-exact members (`0x4497a0`, `0x449600`, `0x449dc0`, `0x449d00`, and
the long-parked `0x44a250` `DispatchMenuItemClickMaybe`) are all autopsied in
`docs/PARKED.md`'s v393/v394 and v395 sections; every one is an intrinsic VC5 tie-break, not
missing body. Corrections and new findings from reading them:

- **Slot 2 and slot 21 are two DIFFERENT hit tests, and the older model conflated them.**
  `0x449d80`, modeled as `Contains` since v322, is a NEW slot 21 testing the button's own hit
  area; the real slot-2 override is the 18-byte `0x449ce0`, which does nothing but tail-call
  `RectFlagObj0x477820::Contains` — deliberately skipping the `AnimDescRefObj`/`WidgetBaseObj`
  overrides in between. Renamed `ContainsHitAreaMaybe` in src and Ghidra. Slot 22 (`0x449d00`,
  `ContainsAnyRegionMaybe`) composes slot 2, slot 21 and each active sub-region's own slot 2 —
  it is the vtable's last real entry, confirming the documented 24-slot/null-slot-23 shape.
- **`WidgetBaseObj0x4784c8` +0x90/+0x94/+0x98 are a DRAG triple**, not the "selection-lifetime
  flag" +0x90 was recorded as. `HitTestMaybe` (`0x44a0c0`) GRABS: on a slot-21 hit it stores
  `cursor.resolvedPosA{X,Y} - rect.{left,top}` into +0x94/+0x98 and sets +0x90.
  `AdvanceAnimFrameMaybe` (`0x4497a0`) MOVES: while +0x90 is set it repositions to
  `cursor.lastResolvedPos{X,Y} - +0x94/+0x98` every frame. So the pair is the grab point's
  offset within the widget's own rect, and `WorldActionCursor::SelectDecorObjAndDispatchMode
  Maybe`'s clearing of +0x90 is cancelling an in-flight drag. Named `bDraggingMaybe` /
  `nDragGrabOffsetXMaybe` / `nDragGrabOffsetYMaybe`; they were carved out of the existing
  `pad0x91[11]`, so the layout is unchanged.
- **+0x168 is a RECT** (`rectHitAreaMaybe`), not four loose ints: `RepositionWithHotspot`
  builds it with `SetRect` while the toolbar is closed and copies `iconBMaybe.rect` into it
  wholesale once open. Ghidra's struct was updated to match; size unchanged at 0x74c.
- **Slot 3 (`0x449dc0`) is the assembly-wide reposition**, and `bSuppressRectBMaybe` (+0xad)
  selects which viewport edge clamps it — i.e. whether the tool menu hangs off the button's
  RIGHT (limits become viewport width minus the menu's own width) or its LEFT (the button may
  not travel left of the menu it carries). When a drag is in flight and the clamp actually
  moved the button, it warps the OS cursor (`ClientToScreen` + `SetCursorPos`) and re-drives
  `PlacementCursorMaybe`'s own position resolve, so the pointer stays pinned to the grab point.
- **Slot 10 (`0x4497a0`) is the per-frame tick**, chaining `AnimDescRefObj0x477488::Advance
  AnimFrameMaybe` explicitly. States: 0 = closed, 1 = opening, 2 = closing, 3 = open. In states
  1/2 it runs a SLIDE animation whose progress fraction is
  `nAnimValueCache / pKindDesc->paFrameEntries[1].nEndFrame` — the button is nudged back into
  view by `pos - (int)(pos * progress) - 1` on whichever viewport edge it has crossed. Reaching
  `paFrameEntries[2].nEndFrame` ends the open (state → 0, `BigSwitchStatement(3)`); reaching
  `[1].nEndFrame` completes it (state → 3, every menu node gets slot-8'd, tutorial event 6
  fires unless `g_pDPlaySessionMgr[0x7c4] == 2`).
- **⭐ SLOT 13 (+0x34) OF `AnimDescRefObj0x477488` IS `SetCategoryIfPrintable` (`0x405e20`),
  identified v537** — it was carried as an unidentified `_v13()` placeholder while the SAME
  function was separately modeled as an "ordinary (non-virtual) member" a few lines above it in
  `src/WidgetBase.h`. One function, two names, two signatures: CLAUDE.md's "a vtable slot and a
  named method at the same address are ONE function" hazard, second sighting after v477's
  `CarNetObj`. `DecorActorBase` OVERRIDES the slot at `0x4344a0` — all three actor-family vtables
  (`0x477eb8`, `0x477f18`, `0x4780b8`) carry `0x4344a0` at +0x34 where the two non-actor tables
  (`0x477488`, `0x4784c8`) carry `0x405e20`. Nothing caught it for so long because every caller of
  the base spelling is a CONSTRUCTOR (`TilePlacedObj`'s `0x4580a0`, `DecorActorBase`'s `0x433a20`)
  and MSVC emits a direct `call 0x405e20` for a virtual called from inside one, so both models
  emit identical bytes. ⚖ The split model is nonetheless what `src/` still carries, deliberately:
  unifying the two declarations is measured at −1005 B and the override's own declaration at a

      is `LocoBitmap::RestoreOverlapBlt`'s dispatch case for `ShadowBlit` — so a "simple" effect
      is by construction a shadow, and the sprites backing these ids are PURE SHADOW MASKS: a
      live dump of effect `0x3887` (the build-toolbar button's own shadow, spawned at
      `rect.left + 0x32, rect.top + 0x32` from `BuildToolButton.cpp`) histogrammed 280 index-0
      and 3998 index-1 pixels over its 69x62 frame and **zero pixels indexing >= 2**. Since
      `ShadowBlit` maps index 0 -> untouched dest and index 1 -> the 50%-darkened dest, the

      defect). The sheet is two frames wide — `rectViewport` came back `(69,0,138,62)` on a
      138x62 bitmap, i.e. the second 69x62 frame, matching the dest rect 1:1. The two known
      producers are that toolbar button and `AnimEffectObj0x477a90`'s ctor tail, which spawns
      one whenever its descriptor carries `nShadowId > 0`. See CODEGEN #208.

  silently makes every menu/palette item unavailable rather than erroring. On success it also

**Confirmed via read-only raw-disasm analysis (agent-assisted): the 4 sorted-position search
blocks embedded in cases 2/3/4/5 are byte-for-byte IDENTICAL compiled code** (same 124
instructions, same bytes modulo relative-branch-displacement operands — cases 2/3/4 are
literally 359 bytes each with zero non-branch-target diffs; case 5's copy is 8 bytes shorter only
because its physical position lets 2 of its exit jumps assemble as short-form rel8 instead of
near-form rel32, pure branch-encoding, not a real difference). Best explanation: each block does
2 manual byte-pair string compares that match MSVC's own `strcmp` intrinsic-substitution shape
exactly (`/O2` implies `/Oi`) — an intrinsic substitution is deterministic regardless of
call-site context, unlike a genuine shared-helper inline (which would be expected to show at
least some register-allocation drift by call-site position per Yoda lesson #7). Transcribed as
`strcmp(...)` calls plus a small hand-written 2-phase (forward-scan via `pPrev`,
backward-scan via `pNext`) search loop, written out literally once per case rather than
factored into a shared method — matches the original's own structure, not a missed idiom
opportunity.

Two structural fixes were needed beyond the field retypes, both now folded into the "KEY VC++
x86 byte-matching lessons" list in CLAUDE.md: hoisting a scratch buffer local to unconditional
function-entry scope when the original zeroes it on every call regardless of which branch runs,
and preferring `> 0` over the logically-equivalent `>= 1` when comparing a tri-state -1/0/1
strcmp-style sign result (comparisons against a literal constant are emitted literally per Yoda
lesson #2, extended here to the "which constant" choice, not just the operator).

**v118: `WidgetPickerObj0x477cc8::HandleTabSwitchMenuNode` (0x428af0, vtable slot 21)
transcribed into `src/WidgetPicker.cpp` — EFFECTIVE MATCH (DIFF 46/168 bytes).** Small click
handler for the tab-switch command nodes: guards on the clicked node's own `wSelIndexMaybe`,
toggles its hover state, then maps its `pIconDesc->resourceId` onto an `ActivateTab`
category — `0x2c02`/`0x2c03`/`0x2c05` → categories 2/3/4 (re-invoked with the base's own
`pLastActivatedNode`, not the clicked node itself), while `0x2c04` instead resets straight
to category 0 (passing the clicked node), skipping the trailing `BuildToolButton`
reposition call. Structure fully confirmed against raw disasm (jump-table entries read via a
manual VA→file-offset dword decode, same technique as the FPU-constant/GUID recipes already
documented). New in Ghidra: `BuildToolButton::ClampDragPositionMaybe` (0x449dc0, a large
drag/placement-clamp method) is confirmed already `this`-typed but not yet transcribed/renamed
— only its call signature was needed here, modeled via a same-address `BuildToolButtonPartial`
partial-view struct (this file's established pattern for not-yet-transcribed singletons).
`DAT_004aa5c0`/`DAT_004aa5c4` (read once, here, never written anywhere in `.text`, always
zero-initialized BSS) left at their literal names pending a future writer/purpose. Residual is
two intrinsic register-choice tie-breaks (the `pLastActivatedNode` reload kept in one
register across the whole switch here vs. re-read twice in the original; the 2 `DAT_004aa5c0/c4`
loads picking swapped registers) plus expected switch-jump-table/inter-function-padding noise —
see the in-source comment and `docs/PARKED.md` for the full tried-and-failed writeup (a
duplicate-call-per-case rewrite, meant to match the original's literal 2-read count, scored
WORSE under `asmscore.py`'s alignment metric since the 3 duplicated reload sites picked 3
different registers, blocking the cross-jump merge needed to match).

**CORRECTED 2026-07-13 (v54): the prior "vtable lengths for all 6 classes confirmed" claim
(and every "N slots beyond base's 23" claim derived from it) was wrong — `WidgetBaseObj0x4784c8`
is genuinely 21 slots (0x54 bytes), not 23.** The earlier confirmation method (reading a run of
raw dwords until hitting a zero/float/"looks like an address boundary") is NOT sufficient in
this codebase: `.rdata` packs many small, wholly UNRELATED classes' vtables contiguously with no
padding, and two of them (`ResourceRef` at `0x47851c`, `WorldBoardMaybe` at `0x478520`)
happen to sit immediately after `WidgetBaseObj0x4784c8`'s real 21st slot, reading as plausible
"slots 21/22" if you don't check who else claims that address. Ground truth this session: (1)
`get_xrefs_to(0x4784c8)` returns exactly 2 hits — `WidgetBaseObj0x4784c8`'s own ctor/dtor, no
more; (2) raw dword at `0x47851c` = `0x454b70`, which independently decompiles as
`ResourceRef`'s own dtor storing `this->pVtable = &0x47851c` — i.e. `0x47851c` is
`ResourceRef`'s OWN vtable address, not `WidgetBaseObj0x4784c8`'s slot 21; (3) raw dword at
`0x478520` = `0x454db0`, independently decompiled as `WorldBoardMaybe`'s own dtor doing the same
self-store. **The fix, generalized: a vtable's true length can only be trusted by finding where
the NEXT class's own ctor/dtor claims ownership of the boundary address (via `get_xrefs_to`), or
by an unambiguous non-code terminator (a float constant, as seen for `WorldActionCursor`) — never
by "the dwords still look plausible."** This is the same `.rdata`-packing trap already documented
for `LocoBitmap`/`SavedFileEntry`, now shown to also break naive vtable-LENGTH inference, not
just "what class does this address belong to."

**RESOLVED 2026-07-13: `WidgetPickerObj0x477cc8` vs. `SaveGamePicker` is composition, NOT
inheritance.** The two ctors have unrelated shapes: `WidgetPickerObj0x477cc8::WidgetPickerObj0x477cc8`
(`0x427370`) is a `__thiscall` chaining `WidgetBaseObj0x4784c8`'s base ctor + an embedded
`AnimDescRefObj0x477488`; `SaveGamePicker`'s destructor (`0x429820` — see correction below)
sets a wholly different vtable (`0x477d24`, unrelated to `0x477cc8`) and tears down an
embedded `ThumbnailBmp` at +0x50. **`SaveGamePicker` was a wrong name — it isn't a picker
widget at all, it's a single enumerated file record.** Renamed the class to
`SavedFileEntry` (0x230 bytes: `vftableMaybe`/+0, `szShortName[11]`/+4,
`szFileName[0x41]`/+0xf, embedded `ThumbnailBmp`/+0x50, `pPrev`/`pNext` list
links at +0x228/+0x22c — confirmed via the allocation site, `new_alloc(0x230)` in the function
below). The real relationship: `WidgetPickerObj0x477cc8` (the file-picker widget) owns a sorted
doubly-linked list of these `SavedFileEntry` nodes through its own `pLinkedListHead`
(+0x4d8). The function that builds that list — previously misnamed
`SaveGamePicker_EnumerateFilesMaybe` — was retyped/moved/renamed to
`WidgetPickerObj0x477cc8::EnumerateFiles`: its body reads `this->pLinkedListHead` and
`this->nCategory` (ex-`Unk0x49c`, also resolved this session: `5` = backdrop `.bmp`
category, else savegame `.sav`) directly and idiomatically once typed as
`WidgetPickerObj0x477cc8*` — proof it was always this class's own method, not
`SaveGamePicker`'s.

**`EnumerateFiles` transcribed 2026-07-16 (v122), EFFECTIVE MATCH.** Clears the existing
list (the same `delete`-loop pattern as this class's own destructor), then rebuilds it: glob
`g_pInstallPathPrefix + ("backdrop\*.bmp" or "savegame\*.sav")` via `_findfirst`/`_findnext`/
`_findclose` (confirmed genuine CRT calls, not custom code — `FUN_00467a20`/`FUN_00467b50`/
`FUN_00467c70`'s own decompiled bodies are textbook `_findfirst`/`_findnext`/`_findclose`
wrapping `FindFirstFileA`/`FindNextFileA`/`FindClose` with `GetLastError`-to-errno translation).
Falls back to `CreateDirectoryA(installPath + "savegame")` if the glob finds nothing (fresh
install). Each non-dotfile match is `_splitpath`'d (confirmed CRT, `_splitpath`) to get its
filename-without-extension; if that fits in `szShortName`'s 10 usable chars, a new
`SavedFileEntry` is inserted into the list via a **stack-local sentinel-head insertion
sort**: a `SavedFileEntry dummyMaybe;` local (default-constructed, not heap-allocated) acts
as the list head for the whole build, walked/compared case-insensitively (`_stricmp`, confirmed
CRT) by `szShortName`; at the end `pLinkedListHead = dummyMaybe.pNext` detaches
the real list from the sentinel. Two real structural fixes were needed to match: (1) the
category-selected string literal ("backdrop..." vs "savegame...") must be computed into a
`const char *` local via an `if` BEFORE the `strcpy`/`strcat` call, never as a ternary argument
in-place — a ternary makes the compiler duplicate the entire `strcpy`/`strcat` intrinsic
expansion once per branch instead of sharing one runtime-selected-pointer expansion; (2) that
computation must be interleaved in the same order as the original's instruction stream
(`strcpy` first, then the category pick, then `strcat`) or the whole function's block layout
shifts. Residual: the documented symmetric-register-swap class (`this` in EBX in the original
vs EBP here, propagating through most of the function) — see the function's own EFFECTIVE MATCH
comment in `src/WidgetPicker.cpp` and `docs/PARKED.md`.

real vtable slot (`0x477d24`, a single dword — the immediately-following dword at `0x477d28` is
a wholly unrelated class's (`LocoBitmap`'s) own vtable, just coincidentally adjacent in

and `ThumbnailBmp`'s own ctor/dtor pair (`0x447b20`/`0x447b90`):

    embedded object at +0x50. Proven a destructor because it calls `0x447b90`, which is
    `ThumbnailBmp`'s DESTRUCTOR (calls `ThumbnailBmp::ThumbnailBmp_CloseStreamsMaybe`) — a
    constructor would never call another object's destructor.
  - **`SavedFileEntry::ScalarDeletingDestructorMaybe`** (`0x429830`, vtable slot 0):
    calls `~SavedFileEntry` then conditionally `operator delete`s based on `param_1&1` — the

    one's vtable slot 0 with `param_1=1` (delete), matching `ScalarDeletingDestructorMaybe`
    exactly.

    renamed into the (pre-existing but previously member-less) `ThumbnailBmp` namespace; no

    `PlaySoundAtScreenPos`'s prologue only ever touches `[esp+...]` stack args, never `ecx`) — same
    class as this file's `Widget::TestAndToggleMenuNodeHoverMaybe` precedent. Calling them as
    plain free functions leaves the caller-side `mov ecx, 0x4855e8` this-load unexplained (a
    real byte-diff); modeling them as members of a `UIResourcesFxPartial` partial-view struct
    (mirroring `src/DSound.cpp`'s own `UIResourcesPartial`, but separately named per-TU to dodge
    the idiom lint's duplicate-class-definition class E) closed it and also improved
    `ActivateTab`'s own match (DIFF 2234→2145) since it shares the `PlayUiSound` call
    site.
  - **v472 — the sound-lookup trio, and why two of the three are parked.**
    `UIResources::SoundBank_LookupEntryById` (0x4472b0, 127 B) is TRANSCRIBED AND EXACT
    (`src/UIResources.cpp`): it resolves a WAV id in the `0x5000..0x6060` band through
    `m_apSoundBankEntries[id - 0x5000]`, loading on first use via `SoundBank_PreloadWavRange`,
    and latches the `(SoundBankEntry *)-1` poison value into the slot when the WAV cannot be
    loaded so the load is attempted exactly once. Out-of-band → `errno = EPERM`; poisoned or
    failed → `errno = ENOENT`. ⚠ The upper bound is written `>= 0x6060` in the source, not
    `> 0x605f` — that was its only residual.
    `PlayUiSound` (0x447930) and `PlaySoundAtScreenPos` (0x4479d0) both INLINE that helper in
    the original and are PARKED for a toolchain reason rather than a source-shape one — see
    docs/PARKED.md and CODEGEN.md's `/Ob1` bullet. They differ only in where the sound is
    positioned: `PlayUiSound` uses the world board's own centre
    (`g_worldBoard.dwHalfWidth`/`dwHalfHeight`) and category 4, `PlaySoundAtScreenPos` takes
    both from parameters. `PlaySoundAtScreenPos` omits the former's `pEntry != NULL` re-check;
    that is NOT an engine bug — `DSound::AcquireChannelForSound` (0x413210) tests its own
    descriptor argument and bails.
    `SoundBank_PreloadWavRange` (0x446cc0) is now declared on `src/UIResources.h` proper,
    retiring one use of the TU-local `UIResourcesTuLocalView` shim; v340's warning that any new
    declaration there rotates `DPlaySessionMgr.cpp` did NOT reproduce when measured.
- Many `Unk0xNN` fields across all 6 structs are purpose-unread (size/offset only, per the
  uncertainty ladder) — see the Ghidra struct definitions for the full field list.

**State 3's world-click handling** (found via `WorldBoardMaybe::ResolveWorldClickMaybe`,
2026-07-13): clicking a placed **world kiosk object** (a `TilePlacedObj` whose kind id
matches one of a fixed set) triggers the matching front-end screen transition through this
same `AppWindow_SetScreenState` dispatcher — kind `0x818` → state 7 (`EditCardWnd`,
"postbox"-shaped), `0x848` → state 6 (`AlbumCardWnd`, "trader"-shaped), `0xc5c`/`0xc5e`/`0xc60`
→ state 5 (`MailWnd`, "mailbox"-shaped), `0x3011`/`0xc42`/`0xc44`/`0xc46`/`0xc48`/`0x3013`/
`0x3015`/`0x3017`/`0x3019`/`0x301b` → state 9 (`MapWnd`, "map kiosk"-shaped, additionally
gated on `g_pDPlaySessionMgr->connectionMode == 2`). Confirms state 3 is the primary in-game/build mode
and these front-end screens are reached by clicking their in-world building, not just via
`MailWnd`'s menu buttons.

**Completed 2026-07-26 (v420) when `ResolveWorldClickMaybe` was transcribed.** Two corrections
and one addition to the list above. (1) Kind **`0x820`** is a 15th special kind that goes
nowhere through `AppWindow_SetScreenState` at all — it calls `g_pCreditsWnd->Show()`
(vtable slot 8) directly, i.e. it is the in-world **credits sign**. (2) The map-kiosk group is
really TWO groups sharing one body: the `0xc42..0xc48` map-edge connectors and the
`0x3011..0x301b` station family both fall into the same `connectionMode == 2` test, and when
that test FAILS they do not open anything — they fall into the ordinary "select this object"
path (`SelectedObjWidgetMaybe::SelectObjMaybe`), which is also the default for every kind not
in the list. (3) The whole dispatch is gated twice on `PlacementCursorMaybe`'s
`bPendingActionBMaybe`, once before the object's own `OnPlacedObjEventMaybe` (vtable slot 0x44,
whose return value becomes the handler's) and again on the default path — the object's virtual
can clear the flag, and the original re-reads it.

**State 4 is BUILD mode**, and there the build-tool mode global `DAT_00485234` decides: mode 1
bulldozes (the single object under the cursor, or -- if `WorldBoardPartial::bFlag0x3cMaybe` says
a previous bulldoze click is still anchored and the new click is more than 16 px away in either
axis -- everything on the segment between the two, via `WorldBoardMaybe::
EraseAlongDragSegmentMaybe`/`0x455960`, which walks a unit vector between the endpoints
flushing whatever plane-A slot each step lands on). Mode 2 places
`PlacementCursorMaybe.nTypeIdMaybe` and plays the accept (`0x501a`) or reject (`0x501b`) sound.
Both are additionally gated on `bPendingActionAMaybe` and on `DAT_004aa648` being 0 -- the same
global input lock that makes `PlacementCursorMaybe` (0x4117b0) force cursor kind `0x1404`. The
bulldoze anchor itself is `WorldBoardPartial+0x34/+0x38` (`dwLastBulldozeXMaybe`/`Y`), written on
every bulldoze click and invalidated by `ResetFlag0x3c` (0x456140) when the button comes up.

## Window system

### WindowBase

**⚠ VTABLE AUDIT (v543): `PopupWndBase` is modelled ~15 slots SHORT — `WindowBase` itself is
clean.** `tools/vtable_audit.py` diffs every emitted `??_7Class@@6B@` COMDAT against the image's
own vtable. `WindowBase` (0x477c30) and its direct derivatives agree; `PopupWndBase` (0x477898)
emits 21 slots where the image runs to at least 36, so `CreditsWnd`'s `OnClose`/`OnKillFocus`
sit at slots 21/22 instead of 31/24. The image's `PopupWndBase` table is structurally PARALLEL
to `WindowBase`'s, shifted by exactly one slot (WB `OnMouseMove` 20 ↔ PB 19 … WB `OnClose` 32 ↔
PB 31) — siblings over a shared message-handler block, not one deriving from the other. The full
slot 21–35 map is in the **`docs/PARKED.md` v543 section**, ready to transcribe. Same audit found
`WidgetBaseObj0x4784c8` slots 17–20 are `__purecall` (= pure virtual) in the image and ~40 missing
override declarations repo-wide; see CODEGEN #129/#130.

**Full vtable modeled 2026-07-22 (v323):** every slot 0x00-0x90 is now a real virtual
declaration on the class in `src/WindowBase.h` (declaration order = vtable order), ground-
truthed from the vtable at `0x477c30` itself. Newly identified: slot 0x14 = `NoOpVirtualMaybe`
(`0x426130`, a no-op body also installed at slot 0x20), slot 0x18 = **`Create` itself**
(`0x425b70` is a virtual — `EditCardWnd`/`MailWnd` hide it with their own same-named
non-virtual `Create(HWND)`, a different signature, not overrides), slot 0x24 = bare-ret no-op
`0x4661a0` (stays a `_v24` dummy), slot 0x28 = `RouteMessage` (NOT a real virtual — stays a
`_v28` dummy; `WindowBaseVtableView` remains its dispatch model). The whole 0x2c-0x90 message
block is declared with the probe's names (`OnCreate`/`OnLButtonDown`/... per the WM_*-to-slot
table below); DefWindowProcStub-default slots are declared-only. The 4 shared named bodies

`0x426ad0`) moved from non-virtual members into the virtual block (the two `*NoOp` names were

`OnClose`=`0x426a90` (all declared-only, Ghidra renamed to match); slot 0x6c

(`AlbumCardWnd::OnLButtonDown`/`OnRButtonDown`/`OnKeyDown`/`OnMouseMove`,

method (`FullscreenPopupWndPartial::CreateFullscreenPopupWnd`'s `Create`) was qualified

⚠ **A Ghidra handler name that says `…SetCursor…` is worth re-checking against the class's own
vtable before believing it (v420).** `0x41ce50` was `EditCardWnd_HandleSetCursorMaybe` for many
sessions; the vtable at `0x477930` puts it at slot **0x50**, i.e. `WM_MOUSEMOVE` — `WM_SETCURSOR`

does nothing but set cursors) and it is exactly the failure mode the "pinning a message handler's

names the handler. Renamed `EditCardWnd::OnMouseMove` and given its real 4-parameter prototype
(it had been typed 0-param); transcribed EXACT the same session, 1020 bytes.

**Ctor `0x425870`** (transcribed v176, **EXACT match, first attempt**, 128 bytes, sizeof 0xe8) —
a flat, branch-free sequence of field zero-inits (`hwndSelf`, `hwndOwner`,

`pEraserCursorDesc`, `bSuppressCursorRedraw`, `pCursorBitmap`,

+ `CreateWindowExA`, stores the new HWND at `+0x08 hwndSelf`; the passed-in "owner" HWND at
`+0x0c hwndOwner` is used **only to steal its window TEXT as the new window's title** — an
unusual pattern, not a real parent link. Real param count is **11**, confirmed via `ret 0x2c`
(Ghidra's own auto-analysis had only inferred 9): `nShowCmd`, `hwndOwnerParam`, `xParam`,
`yParam`, `width`, `height`, `hMenu`, `hIcon`, `nClassStyle` (overrides
the registered `WNDCLASSA`'s own `style`, defaults to `CS_HREDRAW|CS_VREDRAW`=3 when 0 — a
prior session's guess that this was a resource id was wrong), and a trailing

`WindowBase::WndProc`, `0x4272f0`, **transcribed, EXACT match, first attempt**,

then forwards to the recovered object's own `RouteMessageMaybe` (vtable slot 0x28; falls back
to `DefWindowProcA` if no object can be recovered at all). Known fields: `vtable`, `hInstance`,
`hwndSelf`, `hwndOwner`, `resourceId`, `className[0x32]`, `bCreated`, `x`/`y`/`width`/`height`,
plus the cursor-system fields below; the rest are `Unk0xNN` placeholders.

**`WindowBase::RouteMessageMaybe` (`0x426140`, named + namespaced v172, NOT this-typed — see
the "Shared vtable slot conventions" section above for why — transcribed v173,
`src/WindowBase.cpp`, **EFFECTIVE MATCH**: every real instruction plus the compiler-emitted
jump-table data trailing the code is byte-identical; only a 3-byte alignment-NOP encoding tie-
break survives before the jump table, see the plate comment/`docs/PARKED.md`)** is
`WndProc`'s slot-0x28 target: the master WM_*-to-vtable-slot router shared by every

case order in source is NOT WM_* numeric order — it's the TRUE physical case-body order
ground-truthed instruction-by-instruction from the raw disasm (Yoda lesson #33); notably
`default:` is declared BEFORE `case WM_HOTKEY:` in the switch. **`WindowBase::
DefWindowProcStub` (`0x422ea0`, named v172, transcribed this session — **EXACT match**,
first attempt, `src/WindowBase.cpp`)** is the shared `{ DefWindowProcA(...); }` default
installed at nearly every unoverridden per-message slot; plain `__stdcall` 4-param forward, no
implicit `this` touched despite living in the vtable array (same "state-pointer free function"
convention as `RouteMessageMaybe` itself).

**`WindowBase::RefreshClientClipRect` (`0x425d30`, named v137)** — the class's own vtable
slot **0x1c** default body (every `WindowBase`-derived singleton but `EditCardWnd` inherits it
unoverridden; `EditCardWnd` overrides slot 0x1c with its own `0x417180`
(`EditCardWnd::RefreshClientClipRect`, named + fully transcribed; content-complete at
`insns 940/938`, residual now a pure `edi`/`ebp` coin-flip. **Its long-standing
"whole-function register-pressure" verdict was REFUTED in v371** — the apparent spilling was a
single address-taken local `RECT rect` written per block and whole-struct-assigned to each
button (`pBtn->rect = rect;`); restoring that shape plus three others cut the residual 86%
(2885608 → 391073). See `src/EditCardWnd.cpp`'s plate comment and `docs/CODEGEN.md`) —
called e.g. from
`EditCardWnd::BeginEdit`, see that class's section). Gated on
