confirmed via cross-check with `RedrawCustomCursor`'s own direct `RECT*` cast at the same
offset), refreshes `width`/`height` (`+0xb4`/`+0xb8`) from it, snapshots it into
`rectClipBounds` (`+0xd4`, another real `RECT`), then derives
`nClipWidth`/`nClipHeight` (`+0xbc`/`+0xc0`) from the snapshot. `rectClipBounds`
is the clamp-bounds source `RedrawCustomCursor` reads at `+0xd4..+0xe0` to keep the drawn
cursor inside the client area. `RedrawCustomCursor` and `BeginModalCapture` are both
named + transcribed now (`BeginModalCapture` EXACT since v141, `RedrawCustomCursor`
still PARKED — see above and CLAUDE.md's pickup).

**Window class names are recoverable directly from the binary.** The ctor resolves its
`resourceId` param through `FUN_00447330` → `LoadStringA(GetModuleHandleA(0), id, ...)` and
the loaded string becomes `WNDCLASSA.lpszClassName`. Ids above the locale-remap range
(~100–500) load the literal `RT_STRING` entry — extracting the raw `RT_STRING` block from
`.rsrc` gives authoritative class names (see CLAUDE.md recipe). This is the FIRST thing to
check for any future unnamed `WindowBase`/`PopupWndBase`-derived window.

### PopupWndBase

A second, independent base class (ctor `0x413ab0`, `Create` `0x413de0`, sizeof 0x118, shared
`WndProc` `0x415900`, vtable `0x477898`) — genuinely separate from `WindowBase` (sets its
own vtable, never calls `WindowBase::WindowBase`). `PopupWndBase` windows are
**DirectDraw-composited overlays**: `Create` allocates an off-screen `IDirectDrawSurface`
sized to the window's content rect, and Show/Hide `Blt` it directly onto the primary surface
(`DAT_004fd3c0`) instead of relying on GDI compositing — classic 1998
exclusive-mode-DirectDraw UI. Layout: `+0x00 vtable`, `+0x04 hInstance`, `+0x08 hwndSelf`,
`+0x0c hwndOwner`, `+0x10 resourceId`, `+0x38 pOffscreenSurface`,
`+0xa8 className[50]`, `+0xdb bCreated`, `+0x104 rectWindow`, `+0x114 bShown`.
**The class is fully claimed as of v466** — all 23 functions in Ghidra's `PopupWndBase`
namespace carry a marker in `src/PopupWndBase.cpp`.

**`PopupWndBase::Create` (`0x413de0`, vtable slot `0x14`, 701 B, EXACT v466)** — never
overridden by any of the three derived singletons, and every call site reaches it as a direct
call. Registers the window class under the name the ctor pulled out of the locale string table,
creates the HWND, calls `RefreshClientRect` + `LoadCursorSlots`, then lazily creates the popup's
own offscreen composite surface. Three facts worth knowing before touching a caller: the window
CAPTION is not a parameter, it is lifted off the OWNER window with `GetWindowTextA`; the window
STYLE is hardcoded `WS_POPUP|WS_CLIPSIBLINGS|WS_CLIPCHILDREN` and the only style a caller
controls is the CLASS style (which defaults to `CS_HREDRAW|CS_VREDRAW` when passed 0); and
parameters 10 and 11 are genuinely DEAD — neither stack slot is read anywhere in the body. Both
error paths (`RegisterClassA` and `CreateWindowExA` failing) format the Win32 error into a
`LocalAlloc`'d buffer and immediately `LocalFree` it without displaying it — dead development
diagnostics. Only the `CreateWindowExA` failure aborts, via a separate re-test of `hwndSelf`.
The offscreen surface is a 124-byte-descriptor `DDSCAPS_OFFSCREENPLAIN|DDSCAPS_SYSTEMMEMORY`
create, and `+0x28` — modeled `rectOffscreenBoundsMaybe` in v466, previously `pad0x28[0x10]` —
is filled `{0, 0, w, h}` from the dimensions `DDraw_QuerySurfaceDims` reports back, NOT simply
`rectScreenBounds` normalized (DirectDraw may hand back a surface larger than requested).

**`PopupWndBase::LoadCursorSlots` (`0x414130`, ex-`FUN_00414130`, 342 B, EXACT v466)** —
`Create`'s callee, and the other half of the `PopupCursorSlot` story. Loads UI resource `0x1400`
into `cursorNormal` and `0x1403` into `cursorHover` by the same four steps each (resource id →
descriptor → `GetOrLoadFrameBitmap(0,0)` → `LocoBitmap::Convert` → cache `pSurface` as the slot's
mask key); only the FIRST slot also publishes the descriptor's native extent into
`Unk0x3c`/`Unk0x40`. The 256×256 composite surface behind `pCompositeSurface` is
**process-wide, not per-popup**: `g_pCursorSurface` (`DAT_004fd3cc`), created on first use and
refcounted through `g_dwCursorSurfaceRefCount` (`DAT_004fd3d0`) — the SAME pair `WindowBase`
refcounts, so either hierarchy can be the last holder that releases it. Contains a real engine
bug (32-bit writes through two 16-bit scratch locals); see `docs/engine-bugs.md`.

**`PopupWndBase::~PopupWndBase` (`0x413b70`, 155 B, EXACT v466)** plus the compiler's own
`??_G` scalar-deleting thunk (`0x413b50`, 30 B, EXACT) — the exact inverse of
`LoadCursorSlots`, in the same order: both cursor slots (each guarded on its own mask key,
released through the descriptor's `ReleaseRef`, then all three members zeroed), then this
popup's share of `g_pCursorSurface`, then `pOffscreenSurface`.

**`PopupWndBase::WndProc` (`0x415900`, v197: create_function'd — the address was already
documented in prose but Ghidra had never actually split a function there, a plain analyzer
gap like several others below) and `PopupWndBase::RouteMessageMaybe` (ex-`FUN_004143e0`,
`0x4143e0`–`0x414a2b`, 1612 bytes, v197: same story — a genuine Ghidra-missed function
spanning the entire `SetCursorDesc`(`0x414340`)–`FUN_00414a80` gap, found via the raw
`objdump` disasm, `create_function`'d, then read/named/typed) are the `PopupWndBase` mirror
of `WindowBase::WndProc`/`WindowBase::RouteMessage` (see below): `WndProc` recovers `this`
from `GWL_USERDATA` (`-0x15`, note the different magic offset from `WindowBase`'s own `-0x15`
too — actually the SAME literal, both use `-0x15`/-21 decimal) exactly like `WindowBase::
WndProc`, then forwards to `RouteMessageMaybe` via vtable slot **0x24** (the analogous slot
to `WindowBase::WndProc`'s own slot 0x28 target). **`RouteMessageMaybe` is a plain `__stdcall`
free function taking the state pointer as an explicit first parameter — NOT a real
`__thiscall` method** (confirmed via raw disasm: the caller pushes routeMessageMaybe's `this`
as a 5th explicit stack arg, `ret 0x14` = 5 dwords popped, no `mov ecx,this` this-in-register
idiom at all), exactly mirroring `WindowBase::RouteMessage`'s own signature
(`LRESULT __stdcall RouteMessage(WindowBase *pWnd, HWND, UINT, WPARAM, LPARAM)`) — **a
this-typing attempt on this function is a documented false start**: an initial pass here
mistakenly ran `set_function_this_type`, which corrupted the decompile (stray
`in_stack_00000014` locals, `hwndMsg->unused`-shaped bogus field access) until reverted back
to a plain `set_function_prototype` with the explicit `PopupWndBase *pWnd` first param and no
this-typing call at all. See the "PopupWndBase message dispatch" table below for its full
WM_*-to-slot mapping (built the same way `WindowBase`'s own table was: ground-truthed directly
from this function's real branches, not inferred from siblings).

**8 more Ghidra-missed default per-message handlers, all discovered/created/named/this-typed
this session (v197) while walking `RouteMessageMaybe`'s own vtable targets** — all share the
`LRESULT __thiscall Method(PopupWndBase *this, HWND hwndMsg, UINT msg, WPARAM wParam, LPARAM
lParam)` shape (`ret 0x10`, confirmed per-function via raw disasm before typing, several of
which Ghidra had originally under-analyzed to 1 param — same "callee under-analyzed" tell
CLAUDE.md documents):
- **`OnMouseMove`** (ex-`FUN_00414a80`, `0x414a80`, vtable **+0x4c**, `WM_MOUSEMOVE`) —
  only acts if the message's target hwnd is this window's own `hwndSelf`: rebinds the ddraw
  clipper, redraws the software cursor (+ the over-board variant if `Unk0x88` is set), rebinds
  the clipper to the active screen. Otherwise a no-op (always returns 0).
- **`OnSize`** (ex-`FUN_00414ac0`, `0x414ac0`, vtable **+0x64**, `WM_SIZE`) — if
  `bCreated`, calls vtable **+0x18** (`RefreshClientRectMaybe`, see below).
- **`OnPaint`** (ex-`FUN_00414ae0`, `0x414ae0`, vtable **+0x68**, `WM_PAINT`) — only acts
  if `bShown`: rebinds the clipper, `GetUpdateRect`/`BeginPaint`/`EndPaint`, then calls vtable
  **+0x1c** (passed the `PAINTSTRUCT*`) and vtable **+0x20** (no args) before rebinding the
  clipper to the active screen — the per-class "draw content"/"draw cursor overlay" hooks;
  both are the shared `WindowBase::NoOpVirtualMaybe`/bare-`ret` defaults on the base class
  itself (`0x4661a0`, the SAME shared no-op `WindowBase`'s own +0x24 slot uses per the
  "Shared vtable slot conventions" corrections below — one stub, reused across both class
  hierarchies' otherwise-unrelated vtables).
- **`OnSetCursor`** (ex-`FUN_00426a60`, `0x426a60`, vtable **+0x6c**, `WM_SETCURSOR`) —
  returns 1 (handled, suppress the OS cursor) if the target is this window's own `hwndSelf`,
  else forwards to `DefWindowProcA`.
- **`OnEraseBkgndNoOp`** (ex-`FUN_00426ac0`, `0x426ac0`, vtable **+0x74`,
  `WM_ERASEBKGND`) — bare `return 1;`, the standard "claim erased" DirectDraw
  double-buffer idiom (prevents GDI erase flicker under the surface it composites itself).
- **`OnMouseActivateNoOp`** (ex-`FUN_00426950`, `0x426950`, vtable **+0x58**,
  `WM_MOUSEACTIVATE`) — bare `return 0;`, a distinct-address (not literally shared with
  `WindowBase::NoOpVirtualMaybe`) but byte-identical trivial stub. **CORRECTED 2026-07-18: was
  misnamed `OnKeyUpNoOpMaybe` at creation** — a live vtable dump plus a direct read of
  `RouteMessageMaybe`'s own real dispatch (not just cross-referencing `WindowBase`'s
  same-numbered slot, which is a DIFFERENT, unrelated dispatch table — see the "Shared vtable
  slot conventions" note about slot numbers not carrying across hierarchies) proved slot 0x58 is
  `WM_MOUSEACTIVATE`'s slot; `WM_KEYUP` actually dispatches through slot 0x54, which is still
  the plain shared `DefWindowProcStub` default (never through this function). Renamed + Ghidra
  plate comment updated; `src/` transcription uses the corrected name from the start.
- **`OnDestroy`** (ex-`FUN_00426ad0`, `0x426ad0`, vtable **+0x78**, `WM_DESTROY`) — zeroes
  `hwndSelf`, forwards to `DefWindowProcA`.

`WindowBase::RouteMessage`'s own table was (see "Shared vtable slot conventions" below) —
switch case order below is source declaration order as compiled, not WM_* numeric order:

| WM_* message | value | vtable slot | notes |

| `WM_SIZE` | 0x5 | `+0x64` | → `OnSize` |
| `WM_SETFOCUS` | 0x7 | `+0x5c` | |
| `WM_KILLFOCUS` | 0x8 | `+0x60` | |
| `WM_PAINT` | 0xf | `+0x68` | → `OnPaint` |
| `WM_CLOSE` | 0x10 | `+0x7c` | → `OnClose` |

| `WM_SETCURSOR` | 0x20 | `+0x6c` | → `OnSetCursor` |
| `WM_MOUSEACTIVATE` | 0x21 | `+0x58` | |

| `WM_NOTIFY` | 0x4e | `+0x80` | |

| `WM_TIMER` | 0x113 | `+0x2c` (fallback) | inline cursor-frame-redraw-on-move-detection when `wParam==0x43` (the cursor-poll timer id) and a real cursor is active/not captured; only falls through to `+0x2c` otherwise |

Full `PopupWndBase` base-class vtable dump (`0x477898`, confirmed real extent — slot `0x94` is
NULL, slot `0x98` walks into unrelated data, per the "vtable dump can walk into the next
class's table" gotcha): `0x0` dtor (`FUN_00413b50`), `0x4` `Hide`, `0x8` `ShowMaybe`,
`0xc` `SetCursorDesc`, `0x10`/`0x1c` `WindowBase::NoOpVirtualMaybe` (shared no-op),
`0x14` `Create`, `0x18` `RefreshClientRectMaybe`, `0x20` the shared bare-`ret` stub
(`0x4661a0`, same address as `WindowBase`'s own +0x24 default), `0x24` `RouteMessageMaybe`,
`0x28`/`0x2c`/most-unoverridden-message-slots `WindowBase::DefWindowProcStub` (`0x422ea0`,
shared), and the 8 real per-message default handlers listed above at their own slots. Every
slot from `0x28`–`0x90` not listed as one of the 8 real handlers is still plain
`DefWindowProcStub`, i.e. **the base class's own default behavior for WM_CREATE, WM_SETFOCUS,
WM_KILLFOCUS, WM_SHOWWINDOW, WM_ACTIVATEAPP, WM_SETCURSOR(?), WM_MOUSEACTIVATE,
WM_WINDOWPOSCHANGING, WM_NOTIFY, WM_KEYDOWN, WM_COMMAND, WM_LBUTTONDOWN/UP/DBLCLK,
WM_RBUTTONDOWN/UP/DBLCLK, and WM_HOTKEY is just `DefWindowProcA`** — every real behavior for
those messages lives entirely in per-singleton overrides (`BuildToolCursorWnd`/`TutorialWnd`/
`CreditsWnd`'s own vtables).

**The C++ model now spans this whole table (v544).** `class PopupWndBase` in
`src/PopupWndBase.h` used to declare only slots `0x0`–`0x50` (21 of the 37), which was not just
a documentation gap: the three derived singletons' overrides of the slots ABOVE `0x50` had no
base slot to override, so they were appended as NEW virtuals and landed at the wrong slot
numbers. `tools/vtable_audit.py` found it; the block now runs `0x0`–`0x90`.

The two tables are **structurally PARALLEL with a one-slot shift** — `PopupWndBase`'s router
sits at slot 9 (`+0x24`) where `WindowBase`'s sits at 10 (`+0x28`), and from there every
handler lines up: `OnMouseMove` `+0x4c`↔`+0x50`, `OnMouseActivate` `+0x58`↔`+0x5c`, `OnSize`
`+0x64`↔`+0x68`, `OnPaint` `+0x68`↔`+0x6c`, `OnSetCursor` `+0x6c`↔`+0x70`, `OnEraseBkgnd`
`+0x74`↔`+0x78`, `OnDestroy` `+0x78`↔`+0x7c`, `OnClose` `+0x7c`↔`+0x80`. At every shared slot
the two tables hold the **same handler address** (`0x426950`, `0x426a60`, `0x426ac0`,
`0x426ad0`), so those bodies are one ICF-folded copy each rather than two — they live in
`WindowBase`'s TU and are declared-only on `PopupWndBase`. The two hierarchies are therefore
SIBLINGS over a shared message-handler block, not one deriving from the other (`PopupWndBase`'s
own slots 0–8 have nothing in common with `WindowBase`'s), which is why
`src/PopupWndBase.h` declares it standalone. Both tables are the same LENGTH (37 slots): the
one-slot shift is absorbed at the tail, where `PopupWndBase` has `WM_WINDOWPOSCHANGING` at
`+0x90` and `WindowBase` has no counterpart, ending at `WM_ACTIVATEAPP`. ⚠ The shift means a
slot NUMBER still does not name the same `WM_*` across the two hierarchies — but reading one
table across to the other pins ~15 slot identities at once.

Per-singleton overrides above `+0x50`, recovered in v544 once the base model reached them:
`CreditsWnd` `+0x60` `OnKillFocus` (0x40f820) and `+0x7c` `OnClose` (0x40f760);
`BuildToolCursorWnd` `+0x60` `OnKillFocus` (0x438890 — **not** the zero-argument
`NotifyToolModeChanged` it was modelled as, see CODEGEN #133), `+0x7c` `OnClose` (0x437ea0) and
`+0x90` `OnWindowPosChanging` (0x426ac0, ICF-folded with `WindowBase::OnEraseBkgnd`'s
`return 1`); `TutorialWnd` `+0x50` `OnKeyDown` (0x426950, ICF-folded with
`WindowBase::OnMouseActivate`'s `return 0`) and `+0x7c` `OnClose` (0x40f760, ICF-folded with
`CreditsWnd`'s). All three singletons also override `+0x3c` `OnRButtonDown` with the same
folded body (0x451520, `return OnLButtonDown(...)` through the vtable).

### Custom cursor system

The game renders its own cursor (no hardware cursor over an exclusive-mode DDraw surface).

- **`WindowBase::InitCursorDescriptorsMaybe` (0x425dc0)**, called from `WindowBase::Create`:
  resolves 3 named cursor resources through the lazy resource registry — RT_STRING id
  `0x1400` = `"cursors\point"`, `0x1403` = `"cursors\anipoint"`, `0x1402` = `"cursors\eraser"`
  (RF-archive paths) — caching per cursor both the descriptor pointer and its vtbl+4
  ("realize") rect object: `pPointCursorRect`/`pPointCursorDesc` (`+0x60`/`+0x64`),
  `pAnipointCursorRect`/`pAnipointCursorDesc` (`+0x68`/`+0x6c`),
  `pEraserCursorRect` (`+0x70`, filled with the ERASER cursor's rect — eraser is likely the
  default/idle cursor), `pEraserCursorDesc` (`+0x74`). Also seeds the transition
  scheduler's initial state (`Unk0x18`/`0x1c`/`0x20` = width/height/scale from the
  descriptor's `+0x14`/`+0x16`/`+0x160`), and allocates the shared game-cursor DirectDraw
  surface (`g_pCursorSurface`/`DAT_004fd3cc`, error string
  `"CGWND: failed to create cursor"`), bumping its refcount
  (`g_dwCursorSurfaceRefCount`/`DAT_004fd3d0`) once per calling `WindowBase`.
- **`WindowBase::~WindowBase` (0x425910, transcribed 2026-07-16, EXACT match, `src/WindowBase.cpp`)**
  — releases the 3 owned `CursorDesc` pointers via `CursorDesc::ReleaseRefMaybe`
  (vtable slot 2, a refcount-decrement release — NOT a plain `delete`), keyed off each pair's
  alias field (`pPointCursorRect`/`pAnipointCursorRect`/`pEraserCursorRect`, the
  same fields `InitCursorDescriptorsMaybe` fills alongside the real descriptor pointer). Then,
  if this `WindowBase` ever called `InitCursorDescriptorsMaybe`
  (`bCursorSystemInitedMaybe`/`Unk0x48`), decrements `g_dwCursorSurfaceRefCount` and calls
  `g_pCursorSurface->Release()` (plain COM `IUnknown::Release`, vtable slot 2) once the
  count reaches 0.
- **`WindowBase::ScheduleModeTransition` (0x426020)** — a timer-driven cursor-rect
  transition scheduler: caches a target-rect pointer (`Unk0x14`), computes scaled
  width/height (`Unk0x18`/`Unk0x1c`, optionally divided by a scale param), optionally resets
  `rectLastCursorDraw` (`+0x50`, a real `RECT` -- `FUN_00426eb0` casts `this+0x50`
  directly as `RECT*`, named+merged v137, was 4 loose `Unk0x50`-`0x5c` dwords), optionally
  brackets a
  `Ddraw_RebindWindowClipper()` pair around `FUN_00426eb0` (guarded by
  `bSuppressCursorRedraw`), and arms
  `SetTimer` (id `0x43`) at 50ms if the new target equals `pEraserCursorRect` ("redraw fast
  once idle"), else 120ms.
- **`WindowBase::RequestModeTransitionFromSource` (0x425fd0)** — thin wrapper: unpacks a
  `CursorDesc`'s hotspot shorts (`+0x32`/`+0x34`) and scale (`+0x160`) and forwards.
- **`WindowBase::NoOpVirtualMaybe` (0x426130)** — bare `ret 4` no-op base override, reused at
  multiple vtable slots across the family.
- **Call sites (exhaustive `.text` virtual-call-idiom scan):** the ONE real (non-NULL) site

  EXACT MATCH on the first compile (112 B, `src/Ddraw.cpp`)** — the body was never mysterious,
  only mis-rendered: Ghidra loses the local `pClipper` across the if/else and reports it as

  `SetClipper(NULL)` detaches the surface from it first (SetHWnd cannot race a live binding).
  Then `pClipper->SetHWnd(0, hwnd)`, re-attach with `SetClipper(pClipper)`, and `Release()` the
  reference GetClipper/CreateClipper handed over — after the re-attach the surface holds its own.
  So the answer to the long-standing "what does it visually draw" question is: NOTHING. It draws
  no pixels at all; it re-points DirectDraw's idea of the visible region at whichever window is
  now on top, which is why every popup show/hide/move brackets itself in a call to it. — own future session if
  picked up; not needed further here since `verify.py`'s reloc-masked comparison only cares
  about the caller's own call-site shape, not the callee's body.

  earlier in the clip block, register-resident rather than re-derived; `unaff_EDI` likewise for
  the height-clamp delta) — modeled in `src/` as `nClampLeftMaybe`/`nClampHeightMaybe`, two
  locals declared once and conditionally reassigned in the clip branches, matching the

  the prerequisite unblocking this transcription attempt. **v140: exhaustive full-function

  tail blocks. Its absence also masked that the union branch's `srcRect`/`destRect` right/bottom
  edges are sized by the single-frame `nWidth`/`nClampHeightMaybe` (not the union region's own

  the byte-diff moved slightly worse despite the fix being multiply cross-verified correct,
  consistent with this function's already-documented register-allocation noise.

### The 8 bootstrap singleton windows

`Bootstrap_ConstructSingletonWindows` (0x406f90, called from `0x406ba0`) constructs all 8
top-level singleton windows in sequence right before the message pump. All identified,
struct-modeled, and renamed; globals typed `g_p<Class>Wnd` and plate-commented.

**Transcribed v253 (`src/Bootstrap.cpp`, EXACT — the whole 2052-byte function).** `__fastcall`,
sole arg a context object (`hwndParent` @ +0x8, `hInstance` @ +0xc) threaded straight through
from `Config_FUN_00406ba0`. Per window: `g_pX = new X(hInstance, resId); if (!g_pX) return err;
if (!g_pX->Create(hwndParent)) { <teardown>; return err; }`. Resource ids in construction order:
Splash `0x1f8`, Mail `0x1f5`, Map `0x1f7`, BuildToolCursor `0x1fc`, AlbumCard `0x1fb`, EditCard
`0x1fa`, Tutorial `0x1fe`, Credits `0x1fd`. Returns 0 on full success, else a distinct code
`-2..-17` (0xfffffffe down to 0xffffffef; ctor-null and Create-fail each get their own code).
Each failure path tears down the windows built so far in a **fixed order — Mail, Splash, Map,
BuildToolCursor, AlbumCard, EditCard, Tutorial, Credits** (creation order with Mail/Splash
swapped), each `delete` dispatching indirectly through the window's virtual dtor (vtable slot 0);
no leak. Modeling: the 5 real classes are used as-is (ctor/`Create` decls added to their headers
with bare `// 0xADDR` comments); Splash/Mail/Map use standalone/WindowBase-derived partial views
(`SplashWndPartial` polymorphic, real `MailWnd` in `src/MailWnd.h`, `MapWndPartial` in `src/MapWnd.h`)
sized to their exact `operator new` sizes with declared-only ctor/`Create`/virtual-dtor — so
`new PartialT(args)` emits the alloc-protection scaffolding and `delete g_p` the indirect slot-0
dispatch, all as masked relocs. `FullscreenPopupWndPartial` moved from `WindowBase.cpp` into
`WindowBase.h` so Bootstrap can reach the shared Map/AlbumCard `Create`.

| # | Global | Ctor | Create | Size | Base | Class string (id) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `g_pSplashWnd` (`DAT_004fd378`) | `0x4202f0` | `0x4204d0` | `0x224` | `WindowBase` | `FRONTWINDOWCLASS` (504) |
| 2 | `g_pMailWnd` (`DAT_004fd37c`) | `0x42e900` | `0x42edb0` | `0x6e0` | `WindowBase` | `MAILWINDOWCLASS` (501) |
| 3 | `g_pMapWnd` (`DAT_004fd388`) | `0x430a90` | `0x402520`* | `0x2c4` | `WindowBase` | `MAPWINDOWCLASS` (503) |
| 4 | `g_pBuildToolCursorWnd` (`DAT_00485258`) | `0x436b20` | `0x436c50` | `0x1d4` | `PopupWndBase` | `MSGBOXWINDOWCLASS` (508) |
| 5 | `g_pAlbumCardWnd` (`DAT_004fd384`) | `0x401f50` | `0x402520`* | `0x254` | `WindowBase` | `ALBUMCARDWINDOWCLASS` (507) |

**`CreditsWnd`'s whole dismiss surface is transcribed (v537), and it is five vtable slots that
all read the same one flag.** `bAnimationStartedFlag` (+0x12d) is raised once by the slot-0x1c
draw hook and gates every input handler the class overrides:

| slot | addr | name | behaviour when the flag is UP | when it is DOWN |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0x2c | `0x40f870` | `OnTimerDefault` | advance one frame, if the tick targets `hwndSelf` | ignore |
| 0x34 | `0x40f7a0` | `OnLButtonDown` | clear flag, `OnExit()`, UI sound 0x5015, swallow | base default |
| 0x4c | `0x40f840` | `OnMouseMove` | chain `PopupWndBase::OnMouseMove` | swallow |
| 0x50 | `0x40f7f0` | `OnKeyDown` | clear flag, `OnExit()`, UI sound 0x5015, swallow | swallow |
| 0x60 | `0x40f820` | `OnKillFocus` | clear flag, `OnExit()` — **no guard, no sound** | (unconditional) |

So a click and a keypress are the same gesture, mouse-move is the only one that DEFERS to the base
rather than acting, and losing focus ends the credits unconditionally — being taken off-screen is
not a gesture that needs confirming. All five byte-match; see `docs/CODEGEN.md` #111 for the
base-virtual-vs-free-stub call spelling their tails depend on, and #112 for why they were landed as
one batch rather than one at a time.

\* `MapWnd` and `AlbumCardWnd` share one `Create` (`0x402520`, transcribed v170, **EXACT
match**, `src/WindowBase.cpp`, `FullscreenPopupWndPartial::CreateFullscreenPopupWnd`): a
generic "size-to-desktop-rect, call `WindowBase::Create`" helper with zero class-specific logic,
called from `Bootstrap_ConstructSingletonWindows` (`0x406f90`) right after each class's own ctor.
`FullscreenPopupWndPartial` is a minimal partial view (`WindowBase` base + one extra `HICON
hIcon` field both real callers place at `+0xe8`, immediately after `WindowBase`'s own
`sizeof`) — not a real standalone class, same idiom as the project's other opaque-cross-class
partial-view structs. `AlbumCardWnd`'s own same-offset field (formerly `Unk0xe8`) is now named
`hIcon` too, set by this shared helper rather than the class's own ctor. Closing this also
exposed a real under-analyzed-callee gap on `WindowBase::Create` (`0x425b70`) itself: Ghidra's
own auto-analysis inferred only 9 explicit params, but `ret 0x2c` proves 11 — the missing trailing
pair (`dwStyle`/`dwExStyle`, observed values `0x81000000`/`0` at this call site) turned
out to be a genuine dead-parameter engine bug once `WindowBase::Create` itself was transcribed
(v170, EFFECTIVE MATCH — see the "WindowBase" section above and `docs/engine-bugs.md`).

Two more class-name strings in the same `RT_STRING` block belong to on-demand singletons
constructed inside `SplashWnd::Create`, not the bootstrap: `NETSETUPCLASS` (502) and
`APPLSETUPCLASS` (505) — see below.

### `PopupWndBase`

The DirectDraw-composited overlay window base (see the bootstrap table above; NOT the same
hierarchy as `WindowBase`, the real Win32 HWND family — the two coincidentally share the same
low-offset layout convention: `vtable`/`hInstance`/`hwndSelf`/`hwndOwner`/`resourceId` at
`+0x0`..`+0x10`). Base of 3 of the 8 bootstrap singletons: `BuildToolCursorWnd` (0x1d4),
`TutorialWnd` (0x3078, see its own entry below), `CreditsWnd` (0x1184). `src/PopupWndBase.h`/
`.cpp`, sparsely modeled so far (most of the 0x118-byte base struct remains raw `pad0xNN`).

**Vtable slots 0x24-0x4c became real virtuals in v397**, extending the block that v396 and
earlier had taken to 0x20. Declaration order in `src/PopupWndBase.h` IS vtable order, so the
whole run had to go in at once: 0x24 stays a `_v24()` placeholder (it is
`PopupWndBase_RouteMessage`, a `__stdcall` free function taking `pWnd` as an explicit 5th stack
arg — not spellable as a virtual), 0x28-0x48 are declared-only (the base installs the shared
`DefWindowProcStub`/0x422ea0 in all nine), and 0x4c is the existing `OnMouseMove` body, which
moved into the virtual block. That last move was the one measured risk — an internal
unqualified call would have flipped from a direct call to a dispatch — and it was **verified
codegen-inert**: `PopupWndBase.obj` came out the same 14750 bytes with every DIFF count
identical and `OnMouseMove` still EXACT (only its mangled name changed, `QAE`→`UAE`), and
`BuildToolCursorWnd`/`CreditsWnd`/`WindowBase`/`TutorialWnd` were all unchanged. The ten
slot-0x28-0x4c dispatch sites in `PopupWndBase_RouteMessage` now call by name;
`PopupWndBaseVtblProbe` survives only for slots ABOVE 0x4c.

(`cursorNormal` at +0x90, `cursorHover` at +0x9c), each `{ int nMaskSurfaceKey; LocoBitmap
*pBitmap; CursorDesc *pDesc; }` — replacing the old loose `int` + `pad0x94[4]` + `CursorDesc*` +
opaque `pad0x9c[0xc]`. The evidence is three-way symmetry, not a single call site:
`FUN_00414130` fills both by the same four steps (`TileKind_GetOrLoadDescriptor(id)` → `pDesc`
with id `0x1400` for the first slot and `0x1403` for the second, `pDesc->GetOrLoadFrameBitmap(0,

`~PopupWndBase` tears both down by the same guard-release-zero sequence; and

`int nKey` parameter takes; it is genuinely a surface pointer, the same dual purpose already
documented on `nCursorDescKey` (+0x14), the field `SetCursorDesc` stores it into. Note the base
ctor zeroes members 0 and 1 of both slots but NOT member 2. The remodel plus the rename of the

  AcquireWorkSurfaceDC` (0x426b00): a `GetDC`-shaped retry loop (up to 1000x, `Sleep(10)`
  between attempts; fatal `ShowFatalErrorMessageBox(0x49)`/`ExitProcess(1)` if it never

  **Gotcha that cost the first compile attempt 4 bytes of offset drift**: `PopupWndBase` has a
  real vtable component at Ghidra's own `+0x0` (confirmed: `TutorialWnd`'s own struct embeds
  `base PopupWndBase len=280` at offset 0, and `PopupWndBase`'s live dump shows an explicit
  `vtable` component), but a fresh `src/` class with NO declared virtual method gets NO
  synthesized vtable pointer — silently shifting every field access below it by -4 bytes
  (`0x38`→`0x34`, `0x64`→`0x60` in the compiled `.obj`, an exact match otherwise). Fixed by
  declaring `virtual ~PopupWndBase();` (undefined, same idiom as `WindowBase.h`'s own dtor
  declaration) purely to trigger vtable synthesis. **A 2nd gotcha**: `tools/asmscore.py --len`
  needs the function's true INCLUSIVE byte length (`get_function_by_address`'s `Body: START -
  END` is an inclusive END address, so length = END - START + 1, i.e. 0x62 here, not 0x61) —
  passing the off-by-one-short `0x61` truncated the original's final `ret 0x4` mid-instruction,
  making an otherwise byte-identical compile misreport as a 3-byte residual with an "extra"
  trailing `ret 4`. Always double-check `--len` against the inclusive-end arithmetic before
  trusting a nonzero score.
  Companion **`CommitScreenUpdate` (`0x414c20`, 714 B, transcribed v464 in
  `src/PopupWndBase.cpp`, EFFECTIVE — DIFF(62), insns 254/254, identical stack frame)** is the
  release-side counterpart AND the popup's whole **present** step. It hands `hdcToRelease` back to
  `pOffscreenSurface` (that surface's own vtable slot `+0x68`, `IDirectDrawSurface::ReleaseDC`)
  when non-null, then — unless the third parameter says otherwise — `Blt`s `pOffscreenSurface`
  onto `g_pDDrawPrimarySurface` at `rectWindow` translated by `ClientToScreen`, `OutputDebugStringA
  ("")` on failure (the pooled empty literal at 0x4851d0 — a stripped debug message).
  When a software cursor is active (`nCursorDescKey != 0` and `bSuppressCursorRedraw == 0`) it
  first saves the region the cursor will cover from `pOffscreenSurface` into `pCompositeSurface`,
  stamps the masked sprite (`nCursorDescKey` reinterpreted as the mask surface, `DDBLT_KEYSRC`)
  **into `pOffscreenSurface` itself**, presents, and then restores that region from
  `pCompositeSurface` — so the offscreen buffer is left cursor-free. That is the OPPOSITE
  compositing direction from the `RedrawSoftwareCursor` sibling, which composites into
  `pCompositeSurface` and presents from there; the difference is deliberate, not transcription
  noise. It also clamps the cursor rect on the right/bottom edges only (no left/top
  `nClampLeftMaybe`/`nClampTopMaybe` analogue) and refreshes `rectPrevCursor` by whole-struct
  assignment. ⚠ **The third parameter's polarity is the opposite of what its old declared name
  `bFullRedraw` suggested: NONZERO SKIPS the redraw.** Every `(hwndSelf, hdc, 1)` call site is a
  pure DC release; every `(hwndSelf, NULL, 0)` site is a pure present. Renamed `bSkipRedraw` in
  `src/PopupWndBase.h` in v464.

**The page's layout, recovered v438 from `RefreshClientClipRect` (0x441360).** Slot 0x1c runs from
`BeginModalCapture` once the seven resources are realized (before that it is a no-op — every rect
below is sized from a realized descriptor's own natural width/height). Everything hangs off two
anchors: `rectPageMaybe`, a fixed **800x600** page `CenterRectInRect`'d into the window's
`rectClipBounds`, and `rectTrayMaybe`, pinned +0x18/+0x24 in from that page's top-left corner and
copied verbatim into `pTrayBtn->rect`. `rectTextAreaMaybe` then hangs 1 px right / 6 px below the
tray and is copied into `pMatrixBtn->rect` — **the scrolling status text lives inside the "MATX"
panel graphic**. Exit is anchored 0xc8 right of the tray's right edge and 0x43 below its bottom;
Go is anchored to Exit's own left edge, +1 on top. The input-box frame is centered in the tray and
offset (-3, +0x46); `rectInputBox` (the child EDIT itself) insets that by +0x48/+6/-6/-0xa. IPX
hangs off the input frame's left edge, TCP off its right. **The icon's source rect is the odd one
out**: `rectIconMaybe` starts as `{0, 0, iconW, iconH}` but is then used as the OUTER rect of a
`CenterRectInRect` over a copy of `rectClipBounds`, and the RESULT is stored back — so it ends up
a clip-bounds-SIZED window INTO the icon bitmap, centered on the icon, which is exactly what
`OnActivate`'s `RestoreOverlapBlt(rectClipBounds, ., rectIconMaybe, 1)` needs to stretch the
backdrop over the whole screen.

**The label crawls.** `BeginModalCapture` arms a 50 ms `WM_TIMER` (id 0x50) and loads locale
string 0x79 into `szLabelText`; `LayoutAndDrawLabel` (0x4421d0) measures it with
`DT_CALCRECT|DT_SINGLELINE` in `g_UIResources.m_hFont20`, centers the result in
`rectTextAreaMaybe` and flushes it to the edge `nUnk0x140Maybe` names; `OnTimerDefaultMaybe`
(0x4423d0) then steps it ONE PIXEL per tick along that leg, repainting clipped to
`IntersectRect(rectLabelMaybe, rectTextAreaMaybe)` in `0x32c8fa` on a `TRANSPARENT` background,
and turns the corner (1 → 2 → 0 → 3 → 1, re-laying from scratch) when the label runs off the far
edge. The alignment flag follows the overflow direction: off the left edge → `DT_RIGHT`, off the
top → `DT_BOTTOM`, otherwise `DT_TOP`/`DT_LEFT` (both 0).

**Input handling.** `OnLButtonDown` (0x441c80) and `OnKeyDown` (0x441f80) are the same commit path
by two routes, both gated on `bUnk0x148Maybe` (set by `OnActivate`, so a click before the first
full paint is ignored). Go / Enter flashes the Go button, `Sleep(150)`, cancels the pending cursor
transition, `GetWindowTextA`s the child EDIT into `g_pNetSettings->szRememberedAddrPrimaryAlt`,
sets the matching `bRememberedApplSetupValid*Maybe` half, `SaveToDisk`s and advances SplashWnd to
state 3; Exit / Escape does the same flash and bounces to state 7. The two protocol buttons only
rewrite `rememberedProtocolPrimary`/`Secondary` and repaint, and only when their provider was
actually detected. Anything left over is tested against `rectEasterEggSoundMaybe`, which just
plays `rand()/0x1fff + 0x500f` at the click position — the same easter-egg shape
`ApplSetupWnd::rectEasterEggSoundMaybe` (+0x20c) and `MapWnd`'s title banner have.
`OnMouseMove` (0x442090) is pure cursor feedback over the four live buttons.

### SplashWnd and the boot video sequence

`SplashWnd` (sizeof 0x224; ctor also mirrors `this` into a SECOND global `DAT_00485240`
because the two free-function subclass procs are raw `WNDPROC`s with no `this`). Drives the
boot sequence as a state machine (`state` at `+0xe8`, `subState` +0xec).

**Modeled in `src/SplashWnd.h` as a real `class SplashWnd : public WindowBase` since v374** —
promoted from the old padded `SplashWndPartial` view in `SplashWndMaybe.h` when
`SplashWnd::OnLButtonDown` was transcribed and needed the WindowBase base. The Ghidra struct was
brought into line in the same session (the eight loose `rect*_left/_top/_right/_bottom` int quads
at +0xfc..+0x17c are now real `tagRECT` components, and the Enter/Esc glyph pointers are typed
`CursorDesc*`/`LocoBitmap*`); sizeof stays 0x224.

**Vtable 0x4779f8** (installed by the ctor at 0x420321). Slot map, cross-checked against
`WindowBase.h`'s table by ten inherited-default matches plus Ghidra's own independently-derived
`OnKeyDown` at slot 0x54: 0x00 dtor 0x4203a0, 0x04 `EndActiveSession` 0x420860, 0x08
`BeginModalCapture` 0x4206b0, 0x1c `RefreshClientClipRect` 0x421200, 0x20 own `OnActivate` 0x421be0,
0x24 `OnIdlePump` 0x421eb0, 0x2c `OnUnhandledMessage` 0x420ec0, **0x38 `OnLButtonDown` 0x422930**,
0x40 `OnRButtonDown` 0x4323c0, 0x50 `OnMouseMove` 0x422d80, 0x54 `OnKeyDown` 0x420bb0, 0x80
`OnClose` 0x422610, 0x90 `OnActivateApp` 0x420e90.
⚠ **0x422930 was named `SplashWnd::OnLButtonUp` in Ghidra until v374 — that was WRONG.** Its
pointer sits at 0x477a30 = slot **0x38** off the 0x4779f8 base (WM_LBUTTONDOWN); WM_LBUTTONUP is
slot 0x3c, which SplashWnd leaves at the shared `DefWindowProcStub` default 0x422ea0. Corrected
DB-side. The same function's plate comment also mis-attributed it to `NetSetupWnd`.

`SplashWnd::OnLButtonDown` (0x422930, transcribed in `src/SplashWnd.cpp`, PARTIAL) is the
front-end's whole click surface. It swallows clicks entirely until `bReadyForInputMaybe` is
armed, except that a click while `state == 0` kicks the state machine to 7. Six hit regions:
the **Enter** label (draw pressed art → `PlayUiSound(0x5015)` → commit → `Sleep(150)` →
`OnEnterCommitAndDispatch` 0x422660); the **Esc** label (same visual feedback, but
`PlaySoundA(NULL, NULL, SND_PURGE)` then plays the click through DSound and **blocks in a spin
loop until the channel reports `IsReclaimable`** — the teardown that follows must not cut the
sound off — then cancels the cursor mode and dispatches `AppWindow_SetScreenState(0xa)`); and four setting
rects, newly named this session — `rectPlayAlone` (+0xfc, sets
`g_pNetSettings->bSkipSetupWizardMaybe` and drops the session to `SetMode(3)`),
`rectConnectOnline` (+0x10c, the inverse — clears the flag, `SetMode(0)` — live only while
`g_pNetSettings->Unk0x10Maybe != 0`, i.e. a provider list exists; **this is the "opt back into
multiplayer setup" write site**), and `rectRememberChoiceOn`/`Off` (+0x11c/+0x12c, a radio pair
over `bUseSecondaryRememberedChoice`, both dead while the skip flag is set). Each setting rect
repaints via `RedrawSettingRectsMaybe` (0x422010, ex-`FUN_00422010`) and shares a commit tail;
every arm early-returns when the flag it would write already holds the target value.

Key fields past `WindowBase`: `bReadyForInputMaybe` (+0xf4, set after the first state-7
paint, gates Enter/Esc), `hIcon` (+0xf8), the four setting rects (+0xfc/+0x10c/+0x11c/+0x12c),
Enter/Esc label rects (+0x13c/+0x14c),
`rectNameField` (+0x15c — ex-`windowRect`; **corrected v376**: `Create` reads all four of its
members to build `hwndChild`'s `CreateWindowExA` position/extent, so this is the player-name EDIT
control's own rect, not the window's), `rectBackground` (+0x16c), `rectUnk0x17c` (+0x17c — a real
`RECT`, laid out by `RefreshClientClipRect` in the same pass as every other rect, 680x680 at design
coords (300,172)-(980,852); NOTHING in the binary reads it back, so its role is unrecovered),
`bArtLoaded` (+0x18c, the latch over the whole
art block), `hbrSolid`/`hbrHatch` (+0x204/+0x208, the `WM_CTLCOLORSTATIC` brushes),
`hwndChild` (+0x20c), `pVideoPlayer` (+0x210, a real `VideoPlayer*`),
`oldChildWndProc`/`oldVideoWndProc` (+0x214/+0x218, raw `LONG` `SetWindowLongA` return values —
NOT `WNDPROC`), `pNetSetupWnd` (+0x21c, a real `NetSetupWnd*` as of v376 — see below),
`pApplSetupWnd` (+0x220), `pDrawTargetMaybe` (+0x1f0, a
lazily-built composited `LocoBitmap` — see `BuildDrawTargetCompositeMaybe` below).

**The sequencer — `SplashWnd::SetState` (0x4208f0, transcribed v379).** `state` (+0xe8) selects
which of the two setup pages is up, and each transition drives the pages' slot-4/slot-8 virtuals
directly. The dispatch is an if/else-if chain in the source (NOT a switch — the original compares
`2, 5, 4, 3, 6, 7, 1` in that order, with no jump table despite the values being dense):

| new state | what it does |
|---|---|
| 1 | park: `PlaySoundA(NULL, NULL, 0)` (stop the music), hide `hwndChild` |
| 2 | the splash proper: hide `hwndChild`, `pNetSetupWnd->BeginModalCapture()`; if the PREVIOUS state was 4 or 5, also `pApplSetupWnd->EndActiveSession()` |
| 3 | hand-off, never rests here: `pNetSetupWnd->EndActiveSession()`, then re-writes `state` to **5** if `g_pNetSettings->bRememberedApplSetupValidSecondaryMaybe` else **4**, and `pApplSetupWnd->BeginModalCapture()` |
| 4, 5 | application page up: hide `hwndChild`, `pApplSetupWnd->BeginModalCapture()` (identical bodies; cl 11.00 cross-jumps them) |
| 6 | done: `EndActiveSession()` on BOTH pages, `g_pDPlaySessionMgr->SetMode(1)` when the skip flag is set, `g_pGameNetThread->SetPriority(1)`, then `AppWindow_SetScreenState(1)` hands the app its real first screen |
| 7 | wizard entry: tear the video down (restore its window proc, `CloseWindow`, `delete`, `subState = 99`), and — only when arriving from state **0** — create the DirectSound manager (`DSound_GetOrCreateManager` 0x45b7e0); arriving from **0 or 1** also starts the boot music (`"%svideo\\music.wav"`, `PlaySoundA` with `SND_ASYNC|SND_LOOP`). Then `EndActiveSession()` on both pages |

So `DSound_GetOrCreateManager` has exactly one caller (state 7 from a cold state 0), and the
long-unlinked `"%svideo\\music.wav"` string is played from here and from
`ScreenSaver::InitAndPlayIntroMusic` — nowhere else.

**How the front end gets painted, and why it is blank for most of the boot (established v570).**
`SplashWnd` has exactly ONE paint entry: `OnActivate` (0x421be0, slot 0x20). It leaves WM_PAINT
(slot 0x6c) at `WindowBase::OnPaint`'s default, and that default is what fires slot 0x20 — so the
only way anything on this window repaints is an `InvalidateRect`/window-destruction reaching
WM_PAINT. `OnActivate` then has three arms and **only `state == 7` draws**: it arms the point
cursor, stamps the visible window of `pDrawTargetMaybe` over the whole screen, repaints the four
setting rects, draws the Enter and Esc labels in their normal art, commits, and finally sets
`bReadyForInputMaybe`. The `state == 0` arm and the catch-all arm just `CommitScreenUpdate`
whatever is already on the work surface.
⚠ **A blank front end during states 0..6 is therefore CORRECT, not a defect** — while the boot
videos run, MCIWnd is painting the clip over the top with GDI, entirely outside DirectDraw, so
there is nothing for the engine to draw underneath it. The chain that ends the blank period is
indirect and worth writing down: the 0x3b9 notify's default arm calls `SetState(7)`, which
`CloseWindow`s and deletes the `VideoPlayer` — and it is the destruction of that MCI child that
invalidates the parent, producing the WM_PAINT that reaches the state-7 arm. Nothing calls
`OnActivate` directly at that transition.
The other caller is `AppWindow_SetScreenState(2)` → `SplashWnd::BeginModalCapture`, which is what
paints (state 0, i.e. nothing) at cold boot.

**The six hit rects, measured (v571).** `RefreshClientClipRect` authors every rect at its
design-space top-left in a fixed 1280x1024 space, sizes it from its own art descriptor's runtime
native extent, then shifts it into screen space by subtracting `rectBackground`'s origin — so the
numbers are only knowable at runtime. Read out of a live 1024x768 port run (`rectBackground` =
128,128,1152,896, i.e. the expected `(1280-1024)/2, (1024-768)/2`):

| name | client rect | centre | design top-left |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rectEnterLabel` | 775,549,885,659 | 830,604 | 0x387,0x2a5 |
| `rectEscLabel` | 267,549,377,659 | 322,604 | 0x18b,0x2a5 |
| `rectPlayAlone` | 402,362,557,492 | 479,427 | 0x212,0x1ea |
| `rectConnectOnline` | 585,362,740,492 | 662,427 | 0x2c9,0x1ea |
| `rectRememberChoiceOn` | 775,317,885,427 | 830,372 | 0x387,0x1bd |
| `rectRememberChoiceOff` | 775,433,885,543 | 830,488 | 0x387,0x231 |

⚠ **All four SETTING rects are no-ops in the default configuration, and that is correct.**
`rectPlayAlone` early-returns because `g_pNetSettings->bSkipSetupWizardMaybe` is already 1;
`rectConnectOnline` is gated on a non-NULL `pDetectedProviderList`; and the remembered-choice pair
is explicitly dead while the skip flag is set. Only Enter and Esc do anything on a stock boot — do
not read "clicking a briefcase changed no pixels" as a port defect. (Exercised for the first time in
v571 via `LOCO_PORT_CLICK`; see docs/CODEGEN.md #202.)

**The click path out of the front end, confirmed end-to-end (v571).** A click anywhere while
`state == 0` takes `OnLButtonDown`'s first arm → `SetState(7)`, which is both the boot-video skip
and the cheapest way to reach the interactive menu. Then `rectEnterLabel` →
`OnEnterCommitAndDispatch` → (with the skip flag set) `Ddraw_InitTileGridExtent(0)`,
`SetMode(1)`, `SetPriority(1)`, `AppWindow_SetScreenState(1)` → `AppWindow_StartGame` →
`LoadingScreen_Show` + the four backdrop-realization stages → `g_worldLoadThread.Start(
App_LoadWorldThreadProcMaybe)` → the `~curr` layout → `screenstate 1 -> 3`, the live world board.
The full observed chain is `screenstate 0 -> 2 -> 1 -> 3`. Note `SetState 7 -> 1` appears in the
middle of it: that is `SplashWnd::EndActiveSession` parking the state machine, called from
`AppWindow_StartGame`, not a failure.

**`SplashWnd::Create` (0x4204d0, EXACT v379)** sizes the splash window to the whole desktop
(`GetClientRect(GetDesktopWindow(), ...)`), loads icon resource `0x65` into `hIcon`, realizes the
art block, and chains `WindowBase::Create` with style `WS_POPUP|WS_MAXIMIZE|WS_CLIPCHILDREN`
(dead — see the `WindowBase::Create` dead-parameter engine bug). It then builds the two setup
pages as full-screen sibling children, connection page first (`new NetSetupWnd(hInstance, 0x1f6)`
then `Create(hwndSelf)`), application page second (`new ApplSetupWnd(hInstance, 0x1f9)`, `0x260`
bytes). **`hwndChild` is a plain `"EDIT"` control** (class string at 0x47e464) positioned over
`rectNameField`, given `g_UIResources.m_hFont24` via `WM_SETFONT` and an 11-character
`EM_LIMITTEXT`, subclassed to `SplashChildSubclassProc`, then focused. Its initial window
text is simply `""` (the pooled empty literal at `DAT_004851d0`; this carried a spurious *sic:*
about a "shared formatting scratch buffer" until v384). The real player name arrives later from
the slot-8 `BeginModalCapture`'s own `SetWindowTextA`.

**The layout pass — `SplashWnd::RefreshClientClipRect` (0x421200, vtable slot 0x1c, EXACT v376).**
Every rect above is authored in a fixed **1280x1024 design space** (which is exactly
`pDrawTargetMaybe`'s own size) and mapped onto the real display mode at runtime: `rectBackground`
becomes the design-space window of the backdrop that is actually visible, centered
(`left = (pDrawTargetMaybe->width - g_dwScreenWidth) >> 1`, ditto `top`), and every other rect is
`SetRect`'d at its design-space TOP-LEFT with a zero extent, sized from its own `CursorDesc`'s
`nativeWidth`/`nativeHeight`, then `OffsetRect`'d by the NEGATED backdrop origin. The whole pass is
skipped unless `bArtLoaded` — the descriptors are what supply the sizes. Design-space origins:
Enter (0x387,0x2a5), Esc (0x18b,0x2a5), play-alone (0x212,0x1ea), connect-online (0x2c9,0x1ea),
remember-on (0x387,0x1bd), remember-off (0x387,0x231).

**`NetSetupWnd` — modeled v376 (`src/NetSetupWnd.h`).** A real `WindowBase`-derived class,
**sizeof 0x1e4 (484)** pinned by `push 0x1e4; call operator new` at 0x420565 inside

**Video sequence** (`SplashWnd::OnUnhandledMessageMaybe`, 0x420ec0, vtable slot 0x2c — Ghidra
called it `DlgProc` until v378; videos via the `VideoPlayer` class, see AVI/MCI). It dispatches
the custom "video finished" msg `0x3b9` on **`subState` (+0xec), not `state`**, as a two-case
`switch`: subState 0 → `%svideo\IgSpin.avi` (site 0x421084); subState 1 → the ini-configured
intro video (`[Video]`/`Dir`, default `locointr.avi`, site 0x421188); anything else ends the
sequence at state 7. Each step tears down the previous `VideoPlayer` (restore the saved wndproc,
`CloseWindow`, `delete`), builds the next one, and subclasses its MCI child with
`SplashVideoSubclassProc`. **Both steps FALL THROUGH on failure** (`sic`): if `IgSpin.avi`'s MCI
child never materialises, step 0 drops straight into step 1's video, and a failure there lands in
the default arm — and each step bumps `subState` BEFORE it can fail, so the fallthrough leaves it
at 2. `OnIdlePump` (0x421eb0) separately kicks off `legoSpin.avi` (site 0x421f7d) when state==0
and no video object exists. Msg `0x40a` (skip, posted by `SplashVideoSubclassProc` and
`OnKeyDown`) and `WM_SYSCOMMAND`/`SC_SCREENSAVE` both transition to state 7 via `SetState`; the
same handler answers `WM_CTLCOLOREDIT` for `hwndChild` (the player-name EDIT control) with
`RGB(0x8c,0,0)` text, `TRANSPARENT` background and the window's own `hbrSolid`. `SetState` also:
state-7-from-0 plays `"%svideo\music.wav"` via `PlaySoundA` and triggers
`DSound_GetOrCreateManager`; states 2–6 show/hide NetSetup/ApplSetup via their vtable slots
`+4` (Hide) / `+8` (Show); state 6 finalizes into app-state 1 (start game).

**Enter/Esc behavior** (`OnKeyDown`; Esc's code is physically first in the body — branch
identity confirmed by raw disasm): **Esc quits the app** (pressed-glyph redraw → NULL-target
transition cancel → app-state `0xa` → `WM_CLOSE`); it never touches ApplSetup. **Enter** →
`OnEnterCommitAndDispatch` (0x422660): commits the typed player name from `hwndChild`'s edit
control (alphanumeric check via `_strpbrk`) to client identity, then gates on
`NetSettings`:

1. `bSkipSetupWizardMaybe != 0` (**the out-of-the-box default**) → dispatch app-state 1 —
   straight into single-player, no setup UI.
2. Else: if the remembered protocol choice (whichever pair
   `bUseSecondaryRememberedChoice` selects) is still available per `NetSetupWnd`'s
   provider flags → `SetState(4)`/`SetState(5)` (skip NetSetup, reuse the choice);
   otherwise `SetState(2)` (show the NetSetup wizard).

## Front-end screens

Despite the literal class names (mailroom conceit — the whole front end is themed as a post
office), behaviorally these are the game's menu/screens family: build a train town, save it
as a "layout"/album card, mail it, tutorial-guided play. Buttons dispatch through the
app-state machine (`AppWindow_SetScreenState`).

- **`MailWnd`** — the **post-box screen** (ctor 0x42e900, `sizeof 0x6e0`; real
  `class MailWnd : public WindowBase` in `src/MailWnd.h` since 2026-07-25). It displays ONE
  postcard at a time out of a PostBag category and lets the player drag it between categories.
  8 `ResourceRef` icon-buttons (`+0x6a4..0x6c0`, ids `0x3cf0-0x3cf3, 0x3cac, 0x3cf6, 0x3cf5,
  0x3cf9`) plus three card-owned hot areas. Buttons 6/7/8 vary their icon by live
  network-game count (`PostBag_GetCategoryFileCountCached(g_pPostBagCache)`, indexing a 5-entry
  sprite table at `+0x6c4..+0x6d6`). `OnKeyDown` (0x42f810, vtable slot 0x54; called
  `OnEscOrQuit` before the slot was identified): Esc and Q simulate a button-2 mousedown,
  `Sleep(150)`, close, app-state 3. **sic:** button 6 in `OnButtonMouseUp` only releases
  pressed state when the count is nonzero — a zero count `break`s early, leaving the button
  visually stuck down (`docs/engine-bugs.md`).
  - **Category paging.** `bViewingOutboxMaybe` (`+0x606`) selects the category every helper in
    the TU re-derives: 0 → category 2 (inbox), 1 → category 1 (outbox). `pOpenCard` (`+0x608`)
    is the displayed `CarNetState*`; `pHeldCard` (`+0x60c`) is the one picked up onto the
    cursor. The five PostBag helpers are `DiscardHeldCardMaybe` (0x42d8a0, deletes the held
    card's `.crd` + attachment `.dat`), `MoveHeldCardToOutboxMaybe` (0x42da10),
    `MoveHeldCardToInboxMaybe` (0x42db30), `DeleteOpenCardFileMaybe` (0x42dc50) and
    `SelectNextCardMaybe` (0x42dd50, repopulates `pOpenCard`) — all five EXACT since
    2026-07-25. All four move/delete helpers share one loop shape: walk the viewed category's
    `.crd` list, load each card just to compare `nPostSeqId` against `pOpenCard`'s, delete the
    matching file, then rebuild the selection and refresh the button-enable flag.
    `SelectNextCardMaybe` additionally loads the category's FIRST card up front as the wrap-around
    fallback and throws it away again unless the open card turned out to be last.
  - **`HitTestButton`** (0x430090, EXACT) maps a client point to a command id. Hot areas are
    tested in `paButtons` order — `[0..5]` → ids 2..7 — then the standalone `rect0x67c` → 9,
    then `paButtons[6]` → 8. `paButtons[7]` is never hit-tested. The final test returns
    branchless (`neg`/`sbb`/`and 8`), and the function returns **unsigned** so the caller's
    jump table needs no index bias.
  - **`OnLButtonDown`** (0x430190, vtable slot 0x38, EXACT). Three card-owned areas are tested
    ahead of the button row: `rectAttachmentMaybe` (`+0x68c`, live only while
    `pOpenCard->wAttachmentId != 0` — plays sound 0x5464, then `OpenAttachmentMaybe` 0x42f250
    if viewing the outbox), `rectCardMaybe` (`+0x624` — sound 0x5015, `pHeldCard = pOpenCard`,
    swap in the card cursor pair `+0x69c`/`+0x6a0`), and `rectFlagMaybe` (`+0x66c` — toggles
    the flag sprite's two-frame animation by hand). Then the id dispatch: 2 = leave to app
    state 3, 3 = hand off to `AlbumCardWnd`, 4 = `g_pEditCardWnd->BeginEdit(pHeldCard)`,
    5 = delete the open card, 6 = flip the card face (`bCardSideMaybe`), 7 = outbox / next,
    8 = inbox, 9 = decorative (sound 0x5276 only). Every command's held-card path first
    restores the anipoint cursor via the inherited `RequestModeTransitionFromSource`.
    **sic:** command 7 falls through into command 8 when `bButtonsEnabledMaybe` is clear, where
    command 8's own held-card guard then always fails.
  - **Layout.** `RefreshClientClipRect` (0x42f8b0, slot 0x1c, EXACT) anchors TWO rects
    independently against the window's clip bounds: `rectScreenMaybe` (`+0x614`, the backdrop
    art's own native size, via `CenterRectInRect` into a clip-bounds-sized scratch) and
    `rectLayoutBaseMaybe` (`+0x634`, reset to the design resolution 0,0,800,600 and centered).
    Everything else is a `CopyRect` of the design box sized from a `CursorDesc`'s native w/h
    plus a hardcoded `OffsetRect`: the eight buttons at (0x2c,0x22), (0x1a7,0x196), (0x22,0x106),
    (0x29e,0x1c3), (0x2cb,0x12e), (0xa9,0x15e), (0x21c,0xb), (0x16d,0x1a0); `rect0x654` at
    (0x14c,0xb0); `rectFlagMaybe` at (0x100,0xd2); `rectCardMaybe` a fixed 300x200 at
    (0x199,0xb2); and the two `SetRect` hot areas, `rect0x67c` = (0x14b,0x1a3,0x1ab,0x1fb)
    offset by the design box's origin and `rectAttachmentMaybe` = (0x14,-0xb,0x2d,0x3b) offset
    by the card rect's origin. ⚠ Ghidra's *typed* decompile of this function once
    misattributed those `CopyRect` sources to `rectScreenMaybe`; the raw disasm reloads the
    pointer register at 0x42f944, so `+0x634` is correct — see `docs/CODEGEN.md`.
  - **Per-button repaint.** `OnButtonMouseDown` (0x42e150) and `OnButtonMouseUp` (0x42de70) are
    NOT app-state dispatchers (an earlier claim, refuted 2026-07-25 by reading both bodies).
    They take a `HitTestButton` COMMAND ID and repaint exactly one icon in its pressed
    (frame 1) / released (frame 0) state via `ResourceRef::DrawFrame`: ids 2..7 →
    `paButtons[0..5]`, id 9 → `paButtons[7]` (so `rect0x67c` IS that button's hot area,
    resolving the header's "never hit-tested" note), id 8 → `paButtons[6]`. Down also plays
    the shared click sound 0x5015 for ids 2..7 only. Both re-blit the backdrop under
    `paButtons[4]` before drawing it, and both index the `+0x6c4`/`+0x6ce` badge tables by the
    live card count for ids 7 and 8. Neither is byte-exact yet — see the in-source autopsies.
  - **`OnMouseMove`** (0x430800, slot 0x50, EXACT) is purely a cursor-shape update: hovering a
    LIVE button arms the anipoint cursor. Ids 2/3/4 need only "nothing held"; 5/6/7 additionally
    recompute the live card count; 0 and 9 arm the point/anipoint cursor respectively while
    nothing is held. Its switch uses a full 10-entry jump table, so the source spelled out the
    two dead cases (1 and 8).
  - **The live-card-count helper.** Nine sites in the TU share one inlined body: "if viewing the
    outbox, rescan category 1 and refresh `bButtonsEnabledMaybe`; else return the cached
    category-2 count". Modelled as `MailWnd::GetViewedCategoryCardCountMaybe()`, defined
    `inline` in `src/MailWnd.cpp` — no out-of-line copy exists in the binary.
  - **`InitResourceRefs`** (0x42e980, EXACT) is second-stage construction, separate from the
    ctor at 0x42e900: it zeroes the runtime state and allocates the eight buttons. Slot [6] is
    constructed BEFORE slot [5]. It also fills the two badge tables —
    `aBadgeVariantsA` = {0,1,3,5,7} (`+0x6c4`, used for command 7) and `aBadgeVariantsB` =
    {0,1,2,3,4} (`+0x6ce`, command 8).
  - **`DiscardHeldCardMaybe`** (0x42d8a0, EXACT) does not discard: it files the held card into
    category 0 (the Album) via `PostBag_SaveCardToCategory(pHeldCard, 0, NULL)` after deleting
    its `.att` enclosure and clearing `wAttachmentId`. The name predates reading the body.
  - The two gates `OnLButtonDown` checks before anything else are `bAttachmentModalBusyMaybe`
    (`+0xe8`, raised around the modal attachment flow) and `bTearingDownMaybe` (`+0x5ed`).
    `nInputCooldownMaybe` (`+0x5f0`) is set to 8 by a press and decremented per `WM_TIMER`.
  - **The full vtable is at 0x477d88** (dumped v383). MailWnd overrides thirteen slots; all but
    two are transcribed and EXACT: 0 `??_GMailWnd` (0x42e960, cl-generated), 4 `EndActiveSession`
    (0x42f6c0), 8 `BeginModalCapture` (0x42f5e0), 0x1c `RefreshClientClipRect` (0x42f8b0),
    0x20 `OnActivate` (0x42e420), 0x2c `OnUnhandledMessageMaybe` (0x42ee20), 0x30
    `OnTimerDefaultMaybe` (0x42fff0), 0x38 `OnLButtonDown` (0x430190), 0x40 `OnRButtonDown`
    (0x4307c0), 0x50 `OnMouseMove` (0x430800), 0x54 `OnKeyDown` (0x42f810), 0x60 `OnSetFocus`
    (0x42ff20, EFFECTIVE — see `docs/PARKED.md`), 0x80 `OnClose` (0x42ff80).
  - **Screen lifecycle.** `BeginModalCapture` hides the cursor, realizes the button resources
    (`EnsureButtonResourcesRealizedMaybe`, 0x42fe30, gated by `bInit0x5f9`), lays out, forces
    `bViewingOutboxMaybe = 1` (**the screen always opens on the outbox**) and arms a 200 ms
    `WM_TIMER` with id `0x4d` into `nTimerId` (`+0x5fc`, ex-`Unk0x5fc`). `EndActiveSession` is
    its exact inverse, plus an unconditional tail that re-syncs the multiplayer "you have
    outgoing post" indicator (`SetUiModeAndNotifyWidgets(PostBag_RecountCategoryOutFiles() != 0)`)
    — so leaving the mail screen is what updates that flag. The backdrop pair (`+0x644`/`+0x648`)
    is realized separately by `EnsureBackdropRealizedMaybe` (0x42fdf0, gated by `bInit0x5fa`)
    because it OUTLIVES a modal session: only `~MailWnd` (0x42ec10) releases it.
  - **`OnActivate`** (0x42e420) offers the screen to the tutorial: if
    `g_pTutorialWnd->NotifyOrLaunch(1, 0)` returns nonzero, `bTearingDownMaybe` latches and
    `OnSetFocus` then bounces every focus grab straight back to the tutorial window
    (`PostMessageA(WM_PAINT)` + `SetWindowPos`). That is the whole purpose of the flag.
  - **The attachment "open" flow** is `OpenAttachmentMaybe` (0x42f250, EXACT) driving
    `PromptForAttachmentSavePathMaybe` (0x42eea0, **not yet transcribed**). The `.att` payload
    has a `.dat` sidecar holding the attachment's original path; `OpenAttachmentMaybe` reads it
    into `szExtractPathMaybe` (`+0xe9`, a real **0x504-byte** buffer — `0xe9 + 0x504 == 0x5ed`,
    exactly `bTearingDownMaybe`, so the size is pinned not estimated), prompts, then MOVES the
    `.att` there (`CopyFileA` + `DeleteFileA`), deletes the sidecar, clears `wAttachmentId` and
    rewrites the card via `SaveOpenCardToFileMaybe` (0x4309b0). The prompt returns 0 = cancelled,
    2 = the destination directory must be created first, anything else = go ahead.
- **`MapWnd`** — the multiplayer LAYOUT/TOWN selection screen (`MAPWINDOWCLASS`, RT_STRING id
  503, app state 9, `sizeof` 0x2c4, ctor 0x430a90, singleton `g_pMapWnd`/`DAT_004fd388`).
  **FULLY TRANSCRIBED v385 — the real class lives in `src/MapWnd.h`/`src/MapWnd.cpp`** (all 21
  functions in 0x430a90..0x4326f0; 10 byte-exact, 1353 B). The old `MapWndPartial` probe is gone
  and `src/Bootstrap.cpp` now `new MapWnd(...)`s the real class.
  - **What the screen is:** a 3x3 grid (`nProviderSlotsPerRow` x `nProviderSlotRows`) of LAYOUT
    tiles, one per `DPlaySessionMgr` provider slot. Each cell blits that peer's stored layout
    blob (`pLayoutData`, `wLayoutCols` x `wLayoutRows` raw 8bpp, through a scratch `LocoBitmap`
    created/filled/blitted/deleted per call — `DrawPeerScreenshotMaybe` 0x431a10) and then stamps
    every train that peer filed a placement result for as an owner-coloured dot
    (`DrawPeerTrainDotsMaybe` 0x431b30, walking `pResultsChainHead` and mapping each train's
    board position through `WindowBase`'s own 0x425ac0 rect-to-rect point rescaler). Below the
    grid sit nine name plates — `arectSlots[0]` is the LOCAL player's, `[1..8]` the other peers,
    drawn by a loop that SKIPS `selectedProviderIndex` and only advances its rect cursor when it
    actually draws — plus a "refresh the layout list" button (`pRefreshBtnRef`, id 0x3d8b, calls
    `LayoutNet_RequestLayoutList`) and an exit button. A 120 ms `WM_TIMER` (id 0x4d) flips
    `bBlinkPhaseMaybe`, which pulses the HOVERED slot's dot between radius 4 and 7 — the only
    animation on the screen.

    - **What `RoadVehicleActor` adds over `WalkerActor` (v392).** It drops train boarding and
      the population-throttle follow stepper entirely, and adds three things:
      - **Lane offsets.** Slot 23 (`ApplyLaneOffsetMaybe`, `0x453d70`) is a nested 4×4 switch
        over (direction driven IN, direction turned OUT TO) that nudges a position a few pixels
        off the tile centre. The offsets encode **LEFT-HAND traffic**: driving north the vehicle
        sits west of centre, driving south east, driving east north, driving west south. The
        magnitudes are asymmetric between an axis and its reverse because the adjusted position
        is the sprite's top-left anchor, not its middle. Directions are the tile graph's own
        0-3, and this function is what finally pins them: **0 = -x (west), 1 = +y (south),
        2 = +x (east), 3 = -y (north)**, reverse == `(d + 2) & 3`. The pathfinder applies the
        offset not only to the step target but to the STORED destination and destination-tile
        positions, so the later arrival test compares against the same offset point.
      - **Per-step collision.** Slot 22 (`AdvanceMovementMaybe`, `0x453eb0`) commits the move
        first, asks `DecorObjMgrMaybe::TestActorCollisionMaybe` (`0x435200`) whether the new
        rect overlaps any other actor pixel-accurately, and backs the move out if it does —
        additionally dropping its target unless the collision code was 7. That is what makes
        traffic queue rather than drive through itself.
      - **An 8-way facing** (`0x453fb0`) off the signs of both step-delta axes, subframes
        0/2/4/6/8/10/12/14 = W, SW, S, SE, E, NE, N, NW, versus `WalkerActor`'s 4-way
        dominant-axis test.
      Two more kind ids fell out of it, both exact mirrors of `WalkerActor`'s own pair:
      **`0x3001`/`0x3002` = `paths\zebral-h`/`-v`**, the crossing markings a road vehicle
      accepts as part of the road network (`WalkerActor`'s counterpart is `track\zebras-h`/`-v`,
      `0xc6c`/`0xc6e`), and **`0xc4a`/`0xc4c` = `track\xsing1-v`/`-h`**, the level crossings it
      may stand on when their barrier subframe is non-zero. It also carries two dead
      `CalcSqDist` calls left over from the copy-and-edit — see `docs/engine-bugs.md`.

      conga lines rather than into N concurrent path searches**. `-1/-1` means "no anchor
      published yet" and a follower seeing it just re-poses in place. Renamed
      `nTrailAnchorPos{X,Y}Maybe` / `nTrailAnchorCounterMaybe`.

    ⭐ **The OTHER HALF of that flag's protocol is `0x457320` (`WorldBoardPartial::FUN_00457320`,
    the force-rebuild entry, transcribed 2026-08-01), and the two together are a hand-rolled
    thread JOIN.** 0x457320 drops `bTrackGraphsBuiltFlag`, then BUSY-WAITS on
    `g_worldLoadThread.IsRunning()` 50 ms at a time until the idle thread has actually exited,
    and only then rebuilds each graph's adjacency (`TrackGraph::BuildAdjacencyAMaybe` 0x45ce40 /
    `BuildAdjacencyBMaybe` 0x45d1c0, each skipped when its graph pointer is null). The wait is
    what makes it safe: the idle thread's own once-per-world block runs the graph build behind
    the very same flag, so rebuilding underneath it would race. There is no wait handle anywhere
    in the pair — the flag plus the polled `IsRunning` IS the synchronisation. Note the asymmetry
    with `BuildTrackGraphsIfReadyMaybe` (0x457380), which re-tests the screen state BETWEEN its
    two graphs so a state change mid-rebuild leaves graph B untouched and the flag down;
    0x457320 does not re-test, because by the time it rebuilds the idle thread is provably gone.
    Both call sites are the build-mode entry path (`src/AppWindow.cpp`).

  gated cases' branch polarity needed the POSITIVE `if (flag == true) {highlighted} else
  {dimmed}` order (matching the original's real `jne`-to-dimmed/fallthrough-to-highlighted
  shape) — the natural-looking negated `if (flag != true) {dimmed} else {highlighted}` compiled
  with inverted `je`/`jne` polarity at all 4 gated sites (same lever family as
  `DrawOrEraseCardSlot`'s found/not-found fix, second confirmation within this same class). (2) **A
  switch whose lowest explicitly-used case value is > 0, with only no-op cases below it, needs
  an explicit `case 0:` (grouped with the other no-op cases, but crucially WITHOUT a `default:`
  label at all) to keep the compiler's jump table anchored at 0** — declaring cases
  1/2/3/4/5/6/9 plus a `default:` (even one merged with `case 0: case 7: case 8:`) made the
  compiler recognize case 0's target as redundant with `default` and drop it from jump-table
  range consideration, normalizing the table to start at the lowest DISTINCT case (1) via an
  extra `dec eax; cmp eax,8` the original doesn't have; removing `default:` entirely (leaving
  `case 0: case 7: case 8: break;` as the only no-op path, relying on switch's own implicit
  fall-past-the-end for genuinely out-of-range values) restored the original's plain `cmp eax,9`
  with no subtraction. New, more specific lesson than the general jump-table-body-order one
  already documented for this same function family.

    other reader/writer in this class's address range reads the full DWORD too (confirmed via a

    selection must be a **duplicated if/else call, not a ternary-local** — CLAUDE.md's

    regardless of phrasing (tried both `cond ? B : A` and `A + (cond != 0)`, both collapsed to
    the same branchless shape), while the original genuinely branches (`test/jne/push A/jmp/
    push B`). Branch polarity also mattered — `if (!nLayoutMode) {A} else {B}` (false/`0x3c0a`
    case first) matches the original's fall-through; the inverted order flips the `jcc`.

  *)(pErrObj4->pCursorDesc->paFrameEntries + pErrObj4->pCursorDesc->wActiveFrameSetIndex*24)`).
  `hIcon` (`+0x154`, renamed 2026-07-20) is `TutorialWnd::Create`'s own `LoadIconA` result,
  passed straight to `PopupWndBase::Create`.

  **`DrawDescriptionChunks(nChunkCount, pHdc)` (ex-`FUN_00450850`, transcribed
  2026-07-17, EXACT match, `src/TutorialWnd.cpp`)** — NOT an "index"-taking per-item draw
  helper (a stale hypothesis recorded before the body was read); it always operates on the
  CURRENTLY SELECTED item (`categoryRecords[nSelectedItemIndex].dwDescriptionStringId`, a locale
  string id loaded via `UIResourcesPartial::LoadLocaleStringMaybe`). Draws up to
  `nChunkCount` word-wrapped "pages" of that description text into `pHdc`'s rect
  (`this->pErrObj6->rect`), one `DT_WORDBREAK | DT_NOPREFIX | DT_END_ELLIPSIS |
  DT_MODIFYSTRING`-truncated `DrawTextA` chunk at a time, advancing an internal text offset
  each chunk. `DT_MODIFYSTRING` truncates/ellipsis-marks the buffer in place when a chunk
  doesn't fit; comparing the modified copy against an untouched second copy of the same
  chunk (byte-by-byte common-prefix scan) detects whether truncation actually happened.
  Returns -1 as soon as a chunk needed NO truncation (the remaining text was the LAST
  chunk, fully consumed) — its sole caller `RefreshListAndNavState` re-calls with
  `nChunkCount = 1, 2, 3, ...` until it gets -1, a linear search for the minimum chunk count
  that displays the item's whole description (assigned to its own `nCount` local, capped at
  200). The `pHdc` passed in is always an OFFSCREEN measurement surface
  (`AcquireOffscreenSurfaceDC`), never the visible one — this function's real `DrawTextA`
  calls are pure measurement, not visible rendering. Codegen notes: matched the original's
  "never cache `*pHdc`, re-dereference the pointer at every GDI call" idiom (Yoda lesson
  #19's aliasing family) and needed the outer chunk-count loop written as a plain `while
  (nChunk < nChunkCount) { if (nChunk >= 200) break; ... }` rather than the equivalent
  `if (0 < nChunkCount) { do {...} while (...); }` form — the do-while form let `/O2` prove
  the `nChunk >= 200` guard trivially false on the peeled first iteration and fold it away
  (merging it into the back-edge test instead), which the original's actual codegen does
  NOT do (it re-checks unconditionally every iteration); the plain `while` form reproduced
  the original's always-checked shape exactly.

  **Message handlers (all five transcribed v397, ALL EXACT, `src/TutorialWnd.cpp`).** This class
  overrides five of `PopupWndBase`'s dispatch slots. They were unwritable as real C++ overrides
  until v397 extended `PopupWndBase`'s virtual block from slot 0x20 to 0x4c (see that entry).
  - **`OnLButtonDown` (0x451540, slot 0x34)** — the class's real input handler. Hands the click
    to the base default while `bPresenterActiveFlag` is clear; otherwise dispatches on
    `HitTestControl`. Codes 1/2/3 are the three nav buttons and all three run the same press
    flash — draw pressed (`FUN_004527b0(n)`), `CommitScreenUpdate`, `Sleep(150)`, draw resting
    (`FUN_00451fb0(n)`), `PlayUiSound(0x5015)` when the DSound manager exists — before their real
    action: 1 → `FUN_00451920` (prev page), 2 → `FUN_00451c60` (next page), 3 → close. Code 7 is
    the current item's own icon, which acts as close for exactly two icon resources (`0x3d01`,
    `0x3d06`, read through `pErrObj5->pCursorDesc->resourceId`). Closing = `OnExit()` then a
    4-way transition on `lastNotifySubcode` (1→5, 2→6, 3→7, else `nGlobalStateMirror`) fed to
    `AppWindow_SetScreenState`. Codes 4/5/6/8 do nothing.
  - **`HitTestControl` (0x451e90)** — maps a client point to a code 1..8 via eight `PtInRect`
    probes, 0 for none. ⚠ **The code is NOT the slot number** and the probe order is not the slot
    order: 1/2/3 = `pErrObj1/2/3` (each skipped unless its own enabled byte is set), then
    7 = `pErrObj5`, 6 = `pErrObj4`, 4 = `pErrObj6`, 5 = `pErrObj7`, 8 = `pErrObj9`. Returns
    `int`, not the `byte` Ghidra infers — both callers use EAX with no zero-extension.
  - **`OnMouseMove` (0x4517b0, slot 0x4c)** — runs the base handler's software-cursor redraw
    (base-qualified, a direct call), then swaps between `PopupWndBase::cursorHover` and
    `cursorNormal` by hover state. **Carries a genuine engine bug — its four switch arms fall
    through**, so a disabled button's arm tests the NEXT button's enabled byte instead of falling
    back to the resting cursor (`docs/engine-bugs.md`).
  - **`OnUnhandledMessage` (0x4518b0, slot 0x28)** — intercepts only WM_SYSCOMMAND/SC_SCREENSAVE:
    tears the view down and returns to the launching screen via the same 4-way ladder as
    `OnLButtonDown`'s close path, then re-runs `FUN_00463670_LotsOfShowWindow`. Everything still
    falls through to `DefWindowProcA`, so the screensaver is reacted to, not suppressed.
  - **`OnTimerDefault` (0x451880, slot 0x2c)** — runs `FUN_00450450` (the presenter tick) only
    for this window's own 0x54 scroll timer, and only while the presenter is playing.
    `PopupWndBase::Show`'s 0x43 cursor timer never routes here (RouteMessage handles it itself).
  - **`OnRButtonDown` (0x451520, slot 0x3c)** — forwards to `OnLButtonDown` through the vtable.

  **The TU's tail (0x451fb0-0x452cd0) was read out in full in v399** — the "extends past
  `PopupWndBase::MeasureTextLineHeight` (0x452170)" suspicion is now settled fact, and every
  function in that range is a `TutorialWnd` member with a real name:
  - **`RedrawControl` (0x451fb0, EXACT, 448 B)** and **`RedrawControlPressed` (0x4527b0, EXACT,
    296 B)** — the press-flash pair. Both are 10-arm jump-table switches over the SAME control
    code `HitTestControl` returns (which is deliberately NOT the pErrObj slot number): 1/2/3 are
    the nav buttons, 6 the presenter, 7 the item icon, 8 the close button, and 4/5/9 the three
    composite areas that own a draw helper. `RedrawControl` draws each nav button's enabled
    (frame 0) or greyed (frame 2) look — except button 3, whose disabled state draws nothing at
    all; `RedrawControlPressed` draws frame 1 for the three nav buttons and makes 4/5 no-ops.
    Both tables are anchored at 0 and both lay their case bodies out 9, 1, 2, … 8.
  - **`DrawDescriptionPage` (0x452230, EFFECTIVE, 823 B)** — case 4. Draws the one description
    page currently scrolled into view. The page window is derived by TWO `DrawDescriptionChunks`
    probes rather than any stored offset (`nListScrollOffset` gives the start index,
    `nListScrollOffset + 1` the end, -1 meaning "rest of string"), then it presents, re-stamps
    the panel background from pErrObj9's bitmap, repaints the item icon, and RE-ACQUIRES the
    offscreen DC through its `HDC*` parameter — which is why all three DC-taking helpers here
    take the handle by pointer.
  - **`DrawItemTitle` (0x452570, EFFECTIVE, 314 B)** — case 5. The selected item's title, locale
    string `categoryRecords[i].dwTitleStringId`, centred in pErrObj7's rect.
  - **`DrawEllipsis` (0x4526b0, EXACT, 251 B)** — case 9. A literal `"..."` in pErrObj8's rect:
    the "more description text follows" indicator. Uses its own font global, `DAT_004855ec`,
    which is read at exactly one site in the whole image.
  - **`DrawPresenterFrame` (0x452c00, EFFECTIVE, 213 B)** and its helper
    **`RestorePresenterBackdrop` (0x452b00, EFFECTIVE, 249 B)** — case 6. Frame selection is a
    horizontal offset into pErrObj4's bitmap strip by `nFrameIndex * nativeWidth`; the backdrop
    helper re-captures the 0xe8 x 0x130 presenter box out of the shared work surface through the
    usual drop-the-lock/blit/retake-the-lock sandwich.
  - **`OnDrawContent` (0x4528e0, EXACT, 544 B)** — vtable slot 0x1c (verified against the class
    vtable at 0x478428). The view's whole first-paint bring-up: latch `bPresenterActiveFlag`,
    park the cursor at screen centre, swap the narration channel to the selected item's
    `dwNarrationSoundId`, capture the full 0x240 x 0x170 window backdrop, repaint all nine
    controls, restart the 100 Hz presenter timer, present, re-assert the resting cursor. It
    ignores its `PAINTSTRUCT*` entirely while still returning `ret 4`.

  **The notify/launch trio (all three transcribed v401, `src/TutorialWnd.cpp`).** These were the

  sits just below the ctor, is NOT part of it: it is a linked-list node removal on `this+0x124`

    (`lastNotifySubcode`, `lastNotifyCode`) pair onto the `categoryRecords` index the view should
    open on, or -1. The outer switch is on the SCREEN that raised the notification (0..15); only
    screens 4 and 7 raise enough distinct codes to need an inner switch of their own
    (0x818/0x848/0xc54..0xc5c and 0x2406..0x240f respectively). Was `__fastcall` in Ghidra;
    converted to `__thiscall` and this-typed in v401.
  - **`FormatNotifyToken` (0x44f750, EXACT, 582 B)** — formats that pair into the ini token

  - **`NotifyOrLaunch` (0x44f560, EFFECTIVE, 486/494 B)** — the public entry point. Records the
    pair, refuses to open the view in a network game (`connectionMode == 2`) or under the

    `g_pLocalPlayerIdentity->name` accumulates the tokens of every pair already shown, and a
    `strstr` against that value is the already-shown test. A caller passing `code == 0` ALWAYS

    pair and appends the token as it does. Returns 1 when the view was launched. Residual is two
    documented intrinsic classes — see `docs/PARKED.md`.

      **CORRECTED, was previously mischaracterized as "RF-Huffman-shaped scratch decode" (pixel-
      level decompression); it is NOT that.** It's a caption/frame-metadata decode driven by a
      delimited TEXT resource (`szResourcePathBuf`, built by `BuildResourcePath`):
      scans for the `nFrameIndex`-th **`*`-delimited entry** (a run of one or more `*`/`\n` bytes
      is the separator — CORRECTED v205: `BuildResourcePath`'s own newline-per-`getline`
      granularity is a DIFFERENT, lower-level concept from this function's own frame-boundary
      delimiter; a single frame's caption can span several newline-terminated lines, ended by a
      literal `*` in the resource text), parses an optional leading `<NNN>` TileKind-id tag via
      `atoi` (→ `nTileKindId`), looks up that TileKind's own realized frame bitmap
      (`pTileBitmap`, via `pOwnedObj2->GetOrLoadFrameBitmapMaybe(0,0)`) and positions
      `rectTile`, blits it via `pAnimSurface`, then vertically-centers (leading `\n`
      padding) and `DrawTextA`'s the remaining caption text onto `pAnimSurface`'s own DC

      shared `throw <int>;` machinery (0x466ce0), caught by an empty `catch(int)` whose
      continuation is the same "line buffer empty" check the normal empty-entry path also hits.
      Returns 1 on success, 0 if out of range. **Transcribed 2026-07-18 (v205): EFFECTIVE MATCH**
