## Resource registry and bitmap-resource classes

### UIResources registry (`DAT_004855e8`) and locale

A large singleton, `sizeof` **0x241bc** (modeled in Ghidra as `UIResources` and in
`src/UIResources.h`, v356). Init: **`UIResources::Init` (`0x446050`, transcribed and byte-EXACT
v358)**, called once from `0x406ba0`; shutdown counterpart `UIResources::Shutdown` (`0x446340`).
It is also the object passed to the locale-aware string loader `LoadLocaleString` (`0x447330`).
Named `UIResources` (promoted from `UIResourcesMaybe` v284 — `StringTable` was the discarded
alternative).

`Init` is the whole UI-resource layer's bring-up, in order: `Ddraw_Init`; `RFIndex::Open` on the
archive named by `lego.ini`'s `[DIRECTORIES]/ResFile` (it is `RFIndex::Open`'s sole caller); the
five shared fonts, all `CreateFontA`'d from one 52-byte local face-name buffer that an inline
`strcpy` fills with `"Arial"`; the easter-egg unlock table (`DAT_004a99b0`, from `ee.ini`); every
WAV in the 0x5000..0x6060 bank; then every tile-kind descriptor from 0x400 up. It returns 0 if
either of the two things it cannot run without — DirectDraw and the archive — failed, and 1
otherwise. Two `time()` calls bracket the resource load with both results discarded and no
elapsed time ever computed: dead load-timer instrumentation, reproduced as-is.

⭐ **The descriptor pass is `TileKind_LoadDescriptorRange(0x400, 0x4000)` — the same inline range
helper the two lazy descriptor loaders (`0x446ea0` / `0x4470b0`) instantiate with `first == last`.**
v357 inferred that helper from the dead created-count accumulator those loaders emit; `Init`
confirms it, because here the range is genuinely 15361 wide and the accumulator is genuinely live
inside the loop. The only codegen difference between the two instantiations is that over a long
range VC5 strength-reduces the failure-poison store onto a pointer induction variable in a stack
slot instead of indexing `m_apKindDescriptors`.

Layout as far as it is pinned (every offset below is byte-match or disasm ground truth):

| Offset | Member | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| +0x04..+0x14 | `HFONT m_hFont12/14/16/24/20` | five `CreateFontA`s back-to-back in `0x446050`, heights 12/14/16/24/20, weights 800/700/700/700/900; all `DeleteObject`'d in `Shutdown` |
| +0x18 | embedded `RFIndex m_rfIndex` (16 B) | = `0x485600`, NOT a standalone global — the stand-alone `g_RFIndex` every other TU uses IS this member. Modeled by value in `src/UIResources.h` since v358; `0x45ca10` (previously filed as a mystery "partial zero-init" of +0x18/+0x1c/+0x24 skipping +0x20) is simply **`RFIndex`'s default constructor**, called on `this+0x18` from `UIResources`' own ctor (`0x445f70`) — the skipped dword is `Unk0x8`, which `RFIndex::Open` zeroes itself |
| +0x28 | `int m_nLastClockChimeStepMaybe` | last played 5-minute station-clock chime step |
| +0x2c | `CursorDesc **m_pKindSlotPtrsMaybe[0x4001]` | per-kindId alias table; `SetKindSlotPtrMaybe` (0x447290) writes `&m_apKindDescriptors[b]` into slot `a` |
| +0x10030 | `CursorDesc *m_apKindDescriptors[0x4001]` | interned per-kind descriptor; NULL = absent, -1 = creation failed |
| +0x20034 | `SoundBankEntry *m_apSoundBankEntries[0x1061]` | interned sound-bank entry, **indexed by `soundId - 0x5000`** (ids 0x5000..0x6060); same NULL/-1 tri-state |
| +0x241b8 | `int m_nLocaleId` | 1..9, decided once at startup by `Locale_DetectLanguage` (below); switched on by every locale-aware loader here |

⚠ **The sound-bank array's `- 0x5000` index bias is folded into the addressing displacement**,
so `SoundBank_PreloadWavRange` (0x446cc0) reaches it as `[this + soundId*4 + 0xc034]`
(0x20034 - 0x5000*4). Taken literally that base would sit inside `m_pKindSlotPtrsMaybe`, which
is what makes the bias unmistakable; `ReleaseAllCachedResources` sweeps the same storage with
the bias already applied (base +0x20034, count 0x1061), pinning both the true base and width.
This also identifies the two long-standing "globals" `DAT_004a64c8` / `DAT_004a6480` (the
station-clock chime entries) as simply `&m_apSoundBankEntries[0x3ab]` and `[0x399]` — i.e. the
slots for wav ids 0x53ab and 0x5399. The earlier claim of a "`LoadStringA`-populated string
table at +0x11030" was a mis-read of `m_apKindDescriptors` and is retracted.

- **`UIResources::Locale_DetectLanguage`** (0x4463c0, ex-free-`__fastcall`; **READ +
  TRANSCRIBED v416, EXACT**, 1043 B incl. its two switch tables) — decides `m_nLocaleId` once,
  from `LocoWinMain`, and is what every other locale-aware loader in this subsystem keys off.
  The ini wins where it can: `[Locale]/Language` is read (defaulting to the deliberately
  unmatchable `"NONE"`), `_strupr`'d in place and `strcmp`'d against the nine shipped language
  names. The ids are those names' own alphabetical order — **DANISH 1, DUTCH 2, ENGLISH 3,
  FRENCH 4, GERMAN 5, ITALIAN 6, NORWEGIAN 7, SPANISH 8, SWEDISH 9** — which is the full set the
  loaders' `switch`es accept; anything else means "use the raw string id", i.e. English. Only if
  the ini names nothing recognisable (or there is no `IniFile` at all) does it fall back to the
  OS, mapping `GetSystemDefaultLCID() & 0x3ff` onto the same ids: `LANG_DANISH`→1,
  `LANG_DUTCH`→2, `LANG_ENGLISH`→3, `LANG_FRENCH`→4, `LANG_GERMAN`→5, `LANG_ITALIAN`→6,
  `LANG_NORWEGIAN`→7, `LANG_CATALAN`/`LANG_SPANISH`→8, `LANG_SWEDISH`→9, default 3. English is a
  real, explicit case in that switch even though `default` does the same thing — see
  `docs/CODEGEN.md`'s byte-index-table bullet for how that is recoverable at all. Declared on
  `src/UIResources.cpp`'s TU-local `UIResourcesTuLocalView`, not on the shared header, per that
  header's own standing NOTE.
- **`UIResources::ReleaseAllCachedResources`** (0x4467e0, ex-`FUN_004467e0`; **READ +
  TRANSCRIBED v356, EXACT**, 95 B) — frees every interned kind descriptor and sound-bank
  entry through the shared vtable-slot-0 deleting dtor, normalising the -1 poison to NULL
  first, and clears `m_pKindSlotPtrsMaybe` alongside the kind sweep.
- **`UIResources::Shutdown`** (0x446340, ex-`FUN_00446340`; **READ + TRANSCRIBED v356,
  EXACT**, 116 B) — the subsystem teardown: `DSound::ReleaseAllChannels` (if the manager
  exists) → `ReleaseAllCachedResources` → `Ddraw_Teardown` (0x45baa0) →
  `DSound_SaveVolumesAndShutdown` (0x45bb20, which Ghidra had misfiled under `LocoBitmap`
  until v356) → `DeleteObject` on all five fonts. Returns 1 unconditionally.
- **`UIResources::SoundBank_PreloadWavRange`** (0x446cc0, ex-`SoundBank_PreloadWavRangeMaybe`;
  **READ + TRANSCRIBED v356**, EFFECTIVE-parked, `docs/PARKED.md`) — the loader half of the
  sound-bank tri-state: walks an id range, resolves each id's path from the string table
  (locale-remapping ids in the 100..500 band, retrying the raw id if the remapped one has no
  string), `new`s a `SoundBankEntry(nId, szPath)` into the slot, and poisons the slot with -1
  on any failure — including an entry that constructs but reports `bLoaded == 0`. Clamps its
  upper bound to 0x6060 and returns whether the walk ran to completion.

- **`UIResources::TileKind_GetOrLoadDescriptor`** (0x446ea0; **READ + TRANSCRIBED v357**,
  EFFECTIVE-parked one instruction from exact, `docs/PARKED.md`) — the lazy half of the
  kind-descriptor cache and the public entry point (~dozens of `g_UIResources.
  TileKind_GetOrLoadDescriptor(id)` call sites). `kindId` is routed through the
  `m_pKindSlotPtrsMaybe` ALIAS table first: the slot points AT an `m_apKindDescriptors` entry
  that may belong to a DIFFERENT kind id, so the id actually loaded is recovered by subtracting
  the descriptor array's base from the slot pointer — not by using `kindId`. A NULL alias slot
  is an immediate `return 0` (no load attempted). Failure poisons the slot with -1 so the kind
  is never retried, and reports `errno` 1 (bad kind id) or 2 (definition string missing / object
  failed to build).
- **`UIResources::TileKind_GetOrLoadDescriptorNoAlias`** (0x4470b0, ex-`FUN_004470b0`;
  **READ + TRANSCRIBED v357, EXACT**, 468 B) — the unaliased twin: same contract, but indexes
  `m_apKindDescriptors` directly, so it can never resolve to another kind's descriptor and has
  no "no slot installed" early-out. All five callers sit in one function (0x44eac9..0x44ebc4).
- **The shared inline range loader.** Both descriptor loaders above are built from ONE inline
  helper — `TileKind_LoadDescriptorRange(nFirstId, nLastId)`, instantiated with `first == last`
  — which is the inline sibling of the out-of-line wav-side `SoundBank_PreloadWavRange`. That is
  what explains the otherwise-inexplicable machinery both emit over a one-element range: the
  bound clamp, the `<=` guard, and a created-count accumulator that is accumulated and then
  discarded (an inline function's return value, not a dead local). Its body is the canonical
  remap-then-retry idiom of this subsystem: locale-remap ids in [100,500], `LoadStringA`, retry
  with the raw id if the remapped one is empty, then either build the descriptor
  (`TileKind_CreateDescriptor`, 0x446840) or poison the slot with -1.
- **`UIResources::LoadLocaleString`** (0x447330; **READ + TRANSCRIBED v357, EXACT**, 204 B) —
  the stand-alone locale-aware `LoadStringA` wrapper, and the third copy in this TU of the same
  remap-then-retry idiom. Note the [100,500] window is tested SIGNED despite the id parameter
  being `UINT`.
- ⚠ **All three loaders' string buffers are 264 bytes (`0x108`), four MORE than the `0x104`
  length cap they hand `LoadStringA`** — frame-layout ground truth (it is what makes 0x4470b0
  byte-exact), and Ghidra reports it directly as `CHAR local_108 [264]`. Do not "tidy" any of
  them to `sizeof(buf)`.

- **`Locale_DetectLanguage` (0x4463c0):** reads `[Locale] Language`, string-compares against
  9 literals (Danish/Dutch/English/French/German/Italian/Norwegian/Spanish/Swedish;
  English=3=default/no-offset), falls back to `GetSystemDefaultLCID()&0x3ff`. Each
  non-English language adds a fixed RT_STRING id offset before `LoadStringA`. The per-language
  offset constants are NOT yet written to Ghidra as named constants (open).

  `UIResourcesPartial`, `WidgetPicker.cpp`'s `UIResourcesFxPartial`) are now ONE shared header

- **`UIResources::TileKind_CreateDescriptor`** (0x446840, ex-`FUN_00446840`; **READ +
  TRANSCRIBED v355**, `src/UIResources.cpp`, EFFECTIVE-parked — see `docs/PARKED.md`; defined
  on the TU-local `UIResourcesFactoryView0x446840`, a no-data-member subclass of the shared
  `UIResources`, for the same header-churn reason as `TickStationClockChimeMaybe` below) — the
  per-kind descriptor FACTORY behind `TileKind_GetOrLoadDescriptorMaybe`. Signature
  `unsigned char (int kindId, char *pszDefinition)`; `pszDefinition` is the RT_STRING text the
  caller just `LoadStringA`-d for that id. It picks a descriptor class from
  `TileKind_GetCategory(kindId)` — `(kindId >> 10)` truncated to a byte and clamped to 0 past
  15 — and, inside the paired categories, from whether `kindId` itself is even or odd
  (`kindId % 2`, SIGNED, so `kindId` is an `int` not a `uint`). The complete table, all 14 arms
  now read (the "partial" qualifiers in this entry's pre-v355 text are retired):

  | category | id range | class / `operator new` size / ctor |
  |---|---|---|
  | 0 | 0x0000–0x03ff | nothing at all — the arm is an empty `break` |
  | 1 | 0x0400–0x07ff | `CursorDesc` 0x168 / 0x424af0, 3rd ctor arg 0 |
  | 2, 4 | 0x0800–0x0bff, 0x1000–0x13ff | odd id → `CursorDesc(…,1)`; even id → `Obj0x4779e0` 0x630 / 0x41e570 |
  | 3 | 0x0c00–0x0fff | odd id → `CursorDesc(…,1)`; even id → **`BigObj` 0x63c / 0x44b190** |
  | 5 | 0x1400–0x17ff | `CursorDesc(…,0)`, then store + force `bReadyFlagMaybe`(+0x18) = 1 |
  | 6 | 0x1800–0x1bff | `kindId == 0x1802` → nothing; `kindId < 0x1866` AND odd → `CursorDesc(…,1)`; else `CarKindDesc` 0x7ac / 0x40e600 |
  | 7, 8 | 0x1c00–0x23ff | odd id → `CursorDesc(…,1)`; even id → `Obj0x478118` 0x178 / 0x436400 |
  | 9, 10, 11 | 0x2400–0x2fff | `CursorDesc(…,0)` |
  | 12, 13 | 0x3000–0x37ff | `Obj0x4779e0` 0x630 / 0x41e570 |
  | 14 | 0x3800–0x3bff | `CursorDesc(…,0)`, then store + force `bReadyFlagMaybe` = 1 only when `kindId > 0x3801` |
  | 15 | 0x3c00–0x3fff | `CursorDesc(…,0)` (the `ja` default arm) |

  The `new(0x63c)` in the category-3 arm is the **ground-truth `sizeof(BigObj)` oracle**, and
  the `new(0x7ac)`/`new(0x630)`/`new(0x178)` arms are the same for their classes. Note this is
  a **sibling family under `CursorDesc`**, not a chain — `CarKindDesc` and `Obj0x478118` each
  extend `CursorDesc` directly; only `BigObj` sits under `Obj0x4779e0`.

  A slot already holding an object, or the `-1` failure sentinel, returns 1 immediately. After
  construction the object must report itself loaded (`CursorDesc::bLoadOkFlag`, +0x162);
  categories 1 and 15 are exempt from that check, and 5/14 pre-set `bReadyFlagMaybe` so they
  pass it. Otherwise the object is `delete`d (vtable slot 0 with arg 1 — the scalar deleting
  dtor) and the slot is poisoned with `-1` so the kind is never retried. The return value is
  "the slot ended up usable"; all three callers (`TileKind_GetOrLoadDescriptorMaybe` 0x446ea0,
  the resource-init pass `FUN_00446050`, and `FUN_004470b0`) accumulate it as a
  **created-descriptor COUNT**, not as a boolean.

  **`CursorDesc::CursorDesc` (0x424af0) takes THREE args, not two** — corrected v355 and
  reprototyped in Ghidra. Its own `ret 0xc` proves the third slot is real and the body never
  reads it (a dead parameter, same tell as `NameAnchorMaybe_ResolveTileAnchorMaybe`/0x40b740).
  This factory passes 1 for exactly the odd-id fallbacks inside the paired even/odd categories
  and 0 everywhere else, so it reads as "this id is the odd half of an even/odd kind pair";
  `Obj0x478118`'s and `Obj0x4779e0`'s own ctors pass `(kindId, 0, 1)`.
- **`UIResources::TickStationClockChimeMaybe`** (0x447400, transcribed v340,
  `src/UIResources.cpp`, EFFECTIVE-parked — see docs/PARKED.md; defined on the TU-local

  the step into the registry's `m_nLastClockChimeStepMaybe` (+0x28, new field this session)
  and plays the full-hour (`DAT_004a64c8`, wav 0x53ab) / quarter-hour (`DAT_004a6480`, wav
  0x5399) chime `SoundBankEntry` globals via `DSound::AcquireChannelForSound` at screen
  center (category 4), each lazily preloaded via `SoundBank_PreloadWavRangeMaybe` — called
  on the `g_UIResources` global, NOT `this`, per the raw disasm's `mov ecx,0x4855e8` — with
  a `(SoundBankEntry *)-1` load-failure sentinel + `errno = ENOENT` on failure

  RECT-by-value idiom as the `PixelCopyBlit` family, source index 0 = transparent), each

  `WorldBoardMaybe::MarkRectDirty` of the full `rcViewport`.

### `CursorDesc` and its derived family

`CursorDesc` (0x168 bytes; ctor `0x424af0`, loader `LoadMaybe` `0x424bf0`, dtor
`0x424ba0`, scalar-deleting dtor `0x424b40`, vtable `0x477c18`) is a generic
small-bitmap-resource holder; cursors are just its best-understood use. Fields:
`resourceId` (+4), `categoryByte` (+8, from `FUN_00446030(id)`),
`pOwnedObjA`/`paFrameEntries`/`pShadowBitmap` (+0x10/+0x20/+0x24, three owned
sub-objects released in the dtor), `nativeWidth`/`nativeHeight` (+0x14/+0x16,
ushorts), `bReadyFlagMaybe` (+0x18), `hotspotX`/`hotspotY` (+0x32/+0x34, shorts —
a hotspot/anchor pair, NOT duplicate width/height), `nTotalFrameCount` (+0x160, ushort, default 1),
`bLoadOkFlagMaybe` (+0x162). More methods: `ParseTokenFieldMaybe` (0x424e00, INI-token
cursor/sprite descriptor parser — literals `"button"`, `"hotspot"`, `"ShadowId"`, …),
`GetOrLoadFrameBitmapMaybe` (0x425670), `ReleaseRefMaybe` (0x4257f0, this-typed/renamed
2026-07-16 — decrements a short refcount at `+0x158`; once it hits 0 AND `pOwnedObjA` is
non-null AND `bReadyFlagMaybe != 1`, releases `pOwnedObjA` (its own vtable slot 0), then
walks a `Unk0x1a`-sized array of `SoundBankEntry` ids off `paFrameEntries` releasing each via
`SoundBankEntry::Release` — **note (v221): `paFrameEntries`'s element type is now confirmed
`CursorAnimFrameEntry` (24 bytes, see below), not literally "`SoundBankEntry` ids"; this older
description is likely reading one of that struct's own dword fields (e.g. `Unk0x8Maybe` or
`Unk0x10Maybe`) as if it held a raw `SoundBankEntry` id — re-verify `ReleaseRefMaybe`'s own
disasm against the now-fully-resolved struct layout before trusting the old framing.**

⭐ **`BigObj::Load` (`0x44b290`, 602 B) — TRANSCRIBED EXACT 2026-07-31 (v527), first compile, in
its own new TU `src/BigObj.cpp`.** It is the third of the family's four `.dat` loaders to be read
in full (after `CursorDesc::Load` 0x424bf0 and `Obj0x4779e0::Load` 0x41e6e0), and it settles how
the tiers compose:

- **The parse is THREE record blocks over ONE stream, strictly BASE-TO-DERIVED**:
  `Obj0x4779e0::ParseTokenField` (0x41e9f0, class-qualified/direct), then
  `CursorDesc::ParseTokenField` (0x424e00, direct), then the tier's own through the VIRTUAL at
  vtable slot `+0xc` — so a `CarKindDesc`/`Obj0x478118` leaf gets its own. Each stage is gated on
  the previous one succeeding, and `bLoadOkFlag` (+0x162) is rewritten after EVERY stage, not once
  at the end. That layout mirrors the `.dat` file itself: successive keyword blocks, each
  terminated by its own `-9` sentinel, in base-to-derived order.
  ⚠ This is the OPPOSITE order from `Obj0x4779e0::Load`, which runs its own virtual FIRST and
  chains `CursorDesc::ParseTokenField` after. The two loaders were hand-written and disagree.
- **The stream guard differs from both ancestors**: this tier tests `!pStream->bad()`
  (`state & 4`) on both its `istrstream` and its `ifstream`, where 0x424bf0/0x41e6e0 both use
  `is_open()`. See docs/CODEGEN.md #93 for how to tell the two shapes apart in disasm.
- **`kindId` is a genuine DEAD parameter** — the body never reads it, though `ret 8` proves the
  slot is real. Unlike `CursorDesc::Load` this override does not seed `resourceId`/`categoryByte`;
  the caller has already done that through the base.
- Everything else is the family boilerplate: zero `m_type0x63a`/`bLoadOkFlag`, early-out on a NULL
  definition name, `sprintf` `"<prefix><name>.dat"` (a local, kept only for the fallback) and
  `"<prefix><name>.bmp"` into `szBmpPath` at +0x48, try the RF archive under the install-relative
  `"<name>.dat"` key, fall back to a loose `ifstream` (`ios::nocreate`) when the archive parse
  never set `bLoadOkFlag`.

register coin-flip — docs/PARKED.md) and `0x44b0b0` the slot-16 (+0x40)
`ResetToBaseSubFrameMaybe` override (125 B, **EXACT**). Together the two overrides are the
animation logic for the only two track kinds that animate: descriptor type **0xc (POINTS)**
cycles a three-phase tick state 0→1→2→0, pushing each phase out through slot 7 (which, being
`dwTrackState` 1, stores it verbatim); descriptor type **0xb (level-crossing GATES)** re-opens
once `PeerTrainSlotQueueMaybe::IsTileOccupiedByAnyTrainMaybe` reports no train on the tile —
tick state 4 (opening) settles to 0 and 5 (closed) steps to 1 — with slot 7 giving those same
arguments their gate meaning (0 closes to 5, 1 opens to 4). The two overrides are declared on
TU-local views, NOT on `TrackTileObj` in `src/TilePlacedObj.h`: declaring them there costs
1667 B of exact matches across three unrelated TUs (see that header's own note).

**`CarKindDesc` — the train/car kind descriptor (v354).** A THIRD `CursorDesc`-derived sibling
alongside `Obj0x4779e0`/`BigObj`, **not** a `BigObj` subclass: it extends `CursorDesc` (0x168)
directly and is **0x7ac bytes** (vtable `0x477610`, ctor `0x40e600`, `LoadMaybe` `0x40e690`).
Layout: `aHeadingOffsetTableMaybe` (+0x168, `short[400]`) and its opposite-end twin
`aOppositeEndHeadingOffsetTableMaybe` (+0x488, `short[400]`), then `wCarIdAMaybe`/`wCarIdBMaybe`
(+0x7a8/+0x7aa, **unsigned**) — the kind's own first/last SELECTABLE car id, parsed straight out of the `.dat`
stream by its `LoadMaybe` (which also zero-inits both). `PeerTrainNode`'s ctor copies the pair into
`wSelectedCarIdAMaybe`/`wSelectedCarIdBMaybe` and latches A as the initial `wSelectedCarId`;
`PeerTrainNode_UpdateSelectedCar` then toggles the train's selection between exactly those two ids.

Consequence for readers: a `CarNetObj`'s inherited `AnimDescRefObj0x477488::pKindDesc` (+0x40) is
declared `BigObj *` in `src/WidgetBase.h` because most consumers ARE `BigObj` kinds, but for a
train car it really points at an `CarKindDesc`, so reaching the tail needs a cast (Ghidra renders
the same access as `pKindDesc[1].base.<BigObj field>`, an artifact of the declared type — 0x7a8 is
exactly `sizeof(BigObj)` 0x63c + 0x16c, so the "array index 1" is a red herring, NOT a real
next-descriptor access). Note also that `CarKindDesc`'s first heading table is the SAME storage
`SettleClaimedSocketMaybe` used to reach through `BigObj`'s
`aFootprintOccupancyMaskMaybe + heading*4 - 6` (0x16e − 6 == 0x168). **Folded v407** and the
feared codegen risk did not materialise — all eight reads in `src/PeerTrainNode.cpp` now spell
`((CarKindDesc *)pKindDesc)->aHeadingOffsetTableMaybe[h*2]` / `[h*2+1]` and BOTH functions kept
their byte-for-byte result (0x40d8e0 was and remains an exact MATCH; 0x40dc20 stays DIFF(264)).
They were never unaligned loads and never that array: a car's `pKindDesc` is an `CarKindDesc`,
`heading*4` bytes is element `*2`, and 0x168 is this class's own heading table. Modeled in its own `src/CarKindDesc.h`, NOT in
`src/CursorDesc.h`: adding it to that shared header rotates `src/Obj0x4779e0.cpp` and
`src/DPlaySessionMgr.cpp` and costs each one exact match (655 B, measured v354) — the same
shared-header churn hazard as `src/TimeOfDayMaybe.h`'s v331 note.

**Fully transcribed v452 — `src/CarKindDesc.cpp`, 5/5 EXACT (1219 B).** The whole class except
its ctor: `~CarKindDesc` (0x40e680) + `??_G` (0x40e660), `ParseTokenField` (0x40e8d0, renamed in
Ghidra from `ParseHeaderAndLoadTablesMaybe` — it IS the vtable slot 3 override),
`LoadHeadingOffsetTablesMaybe` (0x40e950) and `LoadMaybe` (0x40e690, the slot 4 `Load` override).
Two data-model corrections came out of reading them, both LAYOUT-NEUTRAL (the class is still
0x7ac) and both ground-truthed:
- The two heading tables are **`short[400]`, not `short[320]` + 160 bytes of padding**. The
  zero-fill at the head of `LoadHeadingOffsetTablesMaybe` is `mov ecx,0xc8; rep stosd` at +0x168
  and again at +0x488 — 200 dwords == 800 bytes == 400 shorts each, running exactly to the next
  field. The earlier `short[320]` was Ghidra's own shape, never checked. The loader fills only
  **160** of each table's 200 pairs, so the tail 40 pairs are genuinely spare capacity.
- `wCarIdAMaybe`/`wCarIdBMaybe` are **unsigned**: `ParseTokenField` reads both through
  `??5istream@@QAEAAV0@AAG@Z` (`operator>>(unsigned short&)`, 0x464750), not the signed `AAF`
  overload the heading tables themselves use.

`LoadHeadingOffsetTablesMaybe` is the interesting one behaviourally: the heading tables do NOT
come from the kind's own `.dat` at all. Every train/car kind loads the SAME shared
`"<prefix>trains\\train.dat"` (RF archive first, under the install-prefix-stripped name; a loose
binary `ifstream` as fallback) and reads 160 rows of four shorts, interleaving each row across
both tables — near-end {dx,dy} into the first, far-end {dx,dy} into the twin. `ParseTokenField`
calls it UNCONDITIONALLY, even when the kind's own header record was missing or malformed, so a
kind with a broken `.dat` still ends up with valid geometry. This tier owns no ini keywords: its
whole record is one positional line (a discarded lead token, the two car ids, the `-9` sentinel)
read as a single chained extraction.

The ctor (0x40e600) is deliberately NOT transcribed — it needs `CursorDesc(int, char *, int)`
declared on the rotation-locked `src/CursorDesc.h`; `src/UIResources.cpp` reaches it through its
own `CarKindDescCtorShim0x446840` instead. ⚠ Declaring both `ParseTokenField` and `LoadMaybe` on
this header costs `src/PeerTrainNode.cpp`'s 0x40e520 its EXACT match (−220 B, accepted; the pair
is what trips it, bisected — see `docs/PARKED.md`).

**The descriptor factory `UIResources::TileKind_CreateDescriptor`** (0x446840, ex-`FUN_00446840`,

`operator new`s the right size. Its FULL per-category table — every arm read, plus the
`(kindId, pszDefinition, bOddKindMaybe)` constructor signature it calls each class with — lives
in the `UIResources` section above; the family-relevant summary: `BigObj` is `new(0x63c)`, which
is the ground-truth `sizeof` oracle pinning `sizeof(BigObj) == 0x63c`, and within the descriptor
category that covers trains (category 6, ids 0x1800–0x1bff) ids `>= 0x1866` and EVEN ids below it
get `CarKindDesc` (`new(0x7ac)`, ctor `0x40e600`) while ODD ids below `0x1866` get a plain
`CursorDesc` (`new(0x168)`, ctor `0x424af0`) — train kinds are 0x1804/0x1806/0x1808, all even,
hence `CarKindDesc`. Id 0x1802 is special-cased to build nothing at all.

**`Obj0x478118` — the 0x178-byte `CursorDesc` variant (modeled v355).** The FOURTH sibling in
this family, and like `CarKindDesc` a direct `CursorDesc` subclass rather than anything derived

Keyword spellings were read out of the image's own string bytes, not Ghidra's `s_` labels:

| offset | type | ini keyword | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| +0x168 | byte | `walk_speed` (1st) | parsed as a ushort, stored as its low byte |
| +0x169 | byte | `walk_speed` (2nd) | the walk-step loop at 0x433000 runs `counter < +0x169` and passes +0x168 on as the per-step distance — speed-vs-step-count, not an (x,y) pair |
| +0x16a | byte | `groundwidth` | ctor default **8** |

| +0x16c | byte | `Employable` | |
| +0x16d..+0x16f | — | — | never written by ctor or parser |
| +0x170 | dword | `sex` | the value's uppercased FIRST character as a full dword: `'M'` (0x4d, the ctor default) or, for anything else, `'F'` (0x46) |

**Fully transcribed v452 — `src/Obj0x478118.cpp`, 4/4 EXACT (1250 B).** `~Obj0x478118`
(0x436480) + `??_G` (0x436460), `ParseTokenField` (0x436750, 513 B — EXACT on the first compile)

rather than breaking out of the loop — this tier runs first and leaves the base parser to handle

unset cursor hotspot to (0, 8). The ctor (0x436400) is not transcribed, for the same

### `LocoBitmap`

The general 8bpp-bitmap-to-DDraw-surface class (vtable `0x477d28`; also used standalone as
a small canvas widget, e.g. `CreditsWnd`'s animation canvas). `DAT_00485254` = live instance
counter (incremented in the copy ctor).

```
+0x00  vtable*
+0x04  BOOL bConverted     (0 = raw 8bpp, 1 = live DDraw surface)
+0x08  int  width
+0x0c  int  height
+0x10  BYTE bOwnsPalette
+0x11  BYTE bUnk11
+0x14  WORD *pPalette      (256 entries, pre-converted 16bpp LUT)
+0x18  BYTE *pPixels       (raw 8bpp, width*height; freed after Convert)
+0x1c  IDirectDrawSurface *pSurface (lazy)
```

`DAT_00485254`); copy ctor `LocoBitmap::LocoBitmap` `0x42a1c0` (string tag
`"LOCOBITMAP_COPY_CONSTRUCTOR"`; deep-copies palette+pixels, `Blt`s if the source has a
converted surface); plain (non-deleting) dtor `LocoBitmap::~LocoBitmap` `0x42a370` and its
scalar-deleting variant `LocoBitmap::ScalarDeletingDestructorMaybe` `0x42a140` (**named
2026-07-13** — both free `pPalette`/`pPixels`/release `pSurface` via its own vtable+8

the default ctor + `LoadMaybe` — ctor is a clean **byte-exact match**; `LoadMaybe` compiles and
is structurally close but is NOT yet byte-matching. **v95 progress: 749→691/1065 diff bytes** via three fixes (see below);
**v96 progress: 691→690/1065 diff bytes, `asmscore.py` total 319050→309026** via two more real
fixes — remaining residual is register-swap noise (Yoda #29/#30 class), the parked `fd()`

- **v96: `outWidth`/`outHeight` (the DDraw out-params, added in v95's fix 3) needed to be
  declared as FUNCTION-LEVEL locals up top with the rest, not inside the `else` (DDraw) branch
  at point of use.** A declaration inside the branch pushed every later local's stack offset 8
  bytes off from the original (visible as a consistent `[ebp-0xc8]`-vs-`[ebp-0xc0]`-shaped gap
  recurring at BOTH `LoadResource`/`fd()`-check call sites, well before the DDraw branch even
  runs) — moving the declaration to the top of the function (alongside `pPaletteScratch` etc.)
  closed the gap exactly (both sides now agree on every stack offset). Confirms the "explicit
  locals get their stack slot in DECLARATION order, not first-use order" lesson (already known
  for prologue-store scheduling, see CLAUDE.md's WAVEFORMATEX lesson) generalizes to plain
  frame-layout offsets too, not just instruction scheduling.
- **v96: the pixel-row copy loop's `for (int y = 0; ...)` needed to be `unsigned int y`.** The
  original compiles the loop-exit test as `cmp eax,ecx; jae` (unsigned) — Yoda lesson #2
  ("comparisons are emitted literally") applies to the SIGNEDNESS of the comparison too, not
  just the operator/constant. `for (unsigned int y = 0; y < this->height; y++)` (relying on
  ordinary arithmetic conversion against the `int height` field to force an unsigned compare,
  no explicit cast needed) reproduced the exact `jae` shape; a plain `int y` compiles to `jge`
  (Compiler emits `C4018` signed/unsigned-mismatch warning on the implicit-conversion form —
  expected, not a red flag). Tried and inert this session (both reverted, zero net effect on
  either raw diff or `asmscore.py` score, so not worth keeping as source changes): reordering
  `this->height = ...` before/after the `nPixelBytes` multiply (store position for `[ebx+0xc]`
  was already correctly scheduled either way); splitting the `rowStride = (rowStride -
  (rowStride&3)) + 4;` compound expression into two separate statements (the original's
  `sub;add-immediate-4` shape vs. our `imul`-into-a-different-register reassociated form is
  intrinsic register/expression-tree allocation, not source-order-steerable).
- **v96: NEW open item — a `[ebp-4]` SEH-automatic-state write (`mov dword ptr [ebp-4], 0`)
  sits in a different position relative to an adjacent, independent load at the if/else merge
  point (right after the pixel-load/DDraw branches rejoin, just before the `cleanup:`-label
  `if (pRfStream) delete pRfStream;` cascade).** Confirmed via raw disasm that `[ebp-4]` is the
  same automatic try-scope/`new`-protection state slot documented in CLAUDE.md (BYTE writes of
  1/0/2 at earlier points in this same function, matching the `new`-protection-then-user-try
  state-number pattern from `Wav_ParseAndLoad`'s v92 finding; DWORD writes of 0/-1 at this
  merge point and the final unprotected exit). The original writes state=0 BEFORE loading the
  `pRfStream` pointer for the null-check; ours does the load first, state-write second — same
  operations, swapped order, not yet reproduced by any source reordering tried. Likely the same
  "block layout is trace-driven, mostly not source-steerable" class (Yoda lesson #15) as the
  other scheduling residuals in this function, but genuinely new territory (not yet probed with
  a source-side fix attempt) — worth one dedicated pass next session before parking.
- **Local declaration order is NOT "ifstream first, then the rest" — it interleaves.** The
  real binary zero-inits `pPaletteScratch`/`pRfStream` BEFORE the `ifstream fileStream;` ctor
  call, then `pStream`/`pRfBuf`/`bSuccess` AFTER it — recovered by reading the ctor call's
  target (`ifstream_DefaultCtor`, confirmed via Ghidra decompile of `0x463890`) and noting
  which zero-stores land on which side of it in the raw disasm. Real declaration order:
  `pPaletteScratch; pRfStream; ifstream fileStream; pStream; pRfBuf; bSuccess;`. General
  lesson: don't assume a class-typed local with a real ctor call is declared first just
  because C++ idiom favors it — read which OTHER locals' zero-inits straddle the call.
- **A plain `if (ptr != NULL) { ... }` pointer check can compile with an extra
  `setne al; test al,al` boolification** instead of a direct `cmp+jcc` — recovered by trial:
  rewriting `if (g_RFIndexMaybe.pFile != NULL)` as `unsigned char b = (ptr != NULL); if (b)`
  reproduced the original's exact `setne`/`test` shape (closed a real structural gap, not a
  tie-break). Try this rewrite whenever a top-level `if (ptr != NULL)` diffs as
  cmp+jcc-vs-setne+test.
- **`DDraw_QuerySurfaceDimsMaybe`** (ex-`DDraw_FUN_004014e0`, `0x4014e0`) — real signature
  recovered from the `LoadMaybe` call site (`0x42ae52`): `void __cdecl(void *pSurface,
  unsigned int *pOutWidth, unsigned int *pOutHeight)`, not Ghidra's originally-analyzed
  1-param version (another under-analyzed-callee instance, same pattern as
  `BuildPaletteLUTMaybe` below). Calls `pSurface`'s vtable slot `+0x58` (a
  `GetSurfaceDesc`-shaped query) into a local scratch buffer, then writes the width/height
  fields back through the two out-params; the caller masks each result `& 0xffff` (WORD-sized
  values in a 32-bit slot) before storing to `this->width`/`this->height`. Renamed + prototype
  fixed in Ghidra (`set_function_prototype` succeeded this time — plain pointer params, unlike
  `BuildPaletteLUTMaybe`'s rejected by-value struct — though the decompile view stayed stale
  post-fix, a Ghidra cache quirk, not a real blocker). This closes the pickup's former "DDraw
  branch `local_38`/`local_34` mystery" — the two locals are the query's own out-params, not
  unmodeled `this->width`/`height` sources.
- **Struct pitfall:** `LocoBitmap` has a `virtual` dtor (confirmed by its ctor's own
  `this->vtbl = &PTR_...` store) — the C++ struct definition must NOT declare an explicit
  `void *vtbl;` member; the compiler synthesizes that slot automatically once any method is
  `virtual`. A first attempt that mirrored Ghidra's raw offset-0 `vtbl` field byte-for-byte
  double-counted the vtable pointer and pushed every real field 4 bytes late (a uniform +4
  offset diff on every store in the ctor's compiled output was the tell) — declaring the real
  fields starting directly at `bConverted` (real offset `+0x4`) and letting
  `virtual ~LocoBitmap()` supply the implicit vtbl slot fixed it instantly (ctor now
  byte-exact). General lesson: for any polymorphic class recovered from a Ghidra struct that
  includes an explicit `vtbl`/`vtable` field at offset 0, DROP that field from the real C++
  source once the class has >=1 real `virtual` method — only keep an explicit vtbl field for
  classes accessed purely as opaque structs (no methods defined in the current TU).
- **`BuildPaletteLUTMaybe`'s real signature was wrong in Ghidra** (`(LocoBitmap *this, void
  *param_1)` — only 1 visible explicit param) — a second instance of the
  "caller-forwards-own-params-into-under-analyzed-callee" pattern (see CLAUDE.md's caller/
  callee lesson). Root-caused from raw disasm at the call site (`0x42ad38` inside `LoadMaybe`):
  a `sub esp,0x28` + 10-dword `rep movs` immediately before the `call` copies the just-read
  `BITMAPINFOHEADER` onto the stack **BY VALUE** (not by pointer) as the 2nd argument, with the
  stream pointer as the 1st, the heap palette-scratch buffer (`::operator new(0x428)`, zeroed,
  then the first 40 bytes overwritten with a second `bih` copy) as the 3rd, and `LoadMaybe`'s
  own `flags` parameter forwarded as the 4th — real signature `unsigned char
  BuildPaletteLUTMaybe(istream *pStream, BITMAPINFOHEADER bih, void *pPaletteScratch, unsigned
  int flags)`, confirmed by `ret 0x34` (52 = 4+40+4+4 bytes) at the callee's own return. This
  resolves why `LoadMaybe`'s `flags` param looked entirely dead in Ghidra's decompile — it's
  only ever read inside the mis-analyzed callee. **NOT YET fixed in Ghidra itself** — this
  server's `set_function_prototype` REST endpoint rejects by-value struct params (tried both a
  named `istream *`/`BITMAPINFOHEADER` signature — "Can't resolve datatype: istream *" — and a
  raw `undefined1 bih[40]` array workaround — "Can't parse name: bih[40]"); a `run_script_inline`
  Java-level fix (build the `FunctionDefinitionDataType` directly rather than parsing a
  signature string) is the likely path next time this is worth revisiting, but wasn't attempted
  this session (low priority — the source-level fact is what matters for transcription, and is
  now documented here either way). **v97: transcribed** (`src/LocoBitmap.cpp`), DIFF 167/294
  bytes (down from a first-draft 226/304). Real body: `if (bih.biBitCount != 8) return 0;`,
  read 0x400 bytes (256 `RGBQUAD`s) into `pPaletteScratch+0x28`, `if (gcount()!=0x400) return
  0;`, then pick a palette buffer — either the process-wide shared 256-entry cache
  (`g_pSharedPaletteMaybe`/`g_nSharedPaletteRefCountMaybe`, ref-counted, `bOwnsPalette=0`) when
  `flags!=0 && g_nSharedPaletteRefCountMaybe==0`, or a dedicated non-shared buffer otherwise
  (`bOwnsPalette=1`; on alloc failure this path ALSO tears down the existing shared cache as an
  emergency cleanup — real, reproduced behavior, not a bug) — then packs each `RGBQUAD`'s 8-bit
  B/G/R bytes into the live surface's real bit layout via 3 globals set once by
  `Ddraw::Ddraw_QuerySurfacePixelFormat` (0x45b9c0, found via `get_xrefs_to` on
  `DAT_0048527c`): `g_nRedShiftPosMaybe`/`g_nGreenWidthMaybe` (10/5 for a 555 surface,
  `dwRBitMask==0x7c00`, or 11/6 for 565) and `g_nRBitMaskMaybe`/`g_nGBitMaskMaybe`/
  `g_nBBitMaskMaybe` (straight copies of the surface's real `DDPIXELFORMAT.dwRBitMask`/
  `dwGBitMask`/`dwBBitMask`). All 7 globals named+typed in Ghidra (`n`-prefixed even for the
  3 masks — the linter rejects `dw`-prefixed names against a plain `int`/`unsigned int` type,
  same wall as other Hungarian-prefix mismatches elsewhere in this doc). **Found and fixed one
  real bug: the `if`/`else` branch body order was inverted** (this project's usual
  "positive-condition-with-true-path-first" bug class) — but flipping it turned out to compile
  BYTE-IDENTICAL either way (confirmed by direct disasm diff before/after), so the compiler's
  own branch-polarity choice for this compound `||`/`&&` condition is NOT source-steerable here
  — an extension of Yoda lesson #6 to compound conditions, keep the flipped (now more
  natural-reading, matches which branch the original falls through into first) form since it's
  equivalent either way. **Real fix that DID move the needle: `goto fail;` + a single shared
  `fail: return 0;` tail for the 3 plain "return 0" sites** (biBitCount check, gcount check, and
  the shared-cache branch's own alloc failure) — a bare `return 0;` at each site compiled to 3
  DUPLICATED inline 6-instruction epilogues instead of sharing the ONE physical tail block the
  original uses (confirmed via `get_xrefs_to`-style disasm read: original's fail tail at its own
  end-of-function is jumped to by all 3 sites). Closed 226→167/294. **Remaining residual
  (parked, see `docs/PARKED.md`):** the shared-vs-dedicated palette blocks sit in the OPPOSITE
  physical order from the original (ours: dedicated-first/shared-jumped-to; original:
  shared-first/dedicated-jumped-to) despite the branch-polarity experiment showing this isn't
  literally the condition's fault — likely a deeper block-layout/cross-jump choice (Yoda lesson
  #15/#18 family); plus the usual pervasive register-choice/zero-extension-idiom noise
  throughout the packing loop (`xor reg,reg` + partial-register load vs `movzx`, matches the
  documented intrinsic classes). Not re-probed further this session — real signature still not
  applied in Ghidra itself (by-value struct rejected by `set_function_prototype`'s REST
  endpoint, per the existing note above; still low priority, a `run_script_inline`
  `FunctionDefinitionDataType` build is the likely path if ever revisited).

**v98 (2026-07-15): copy ctor, `AllocSurface`, `Convert`+`PixelCopyBlit` transcribed
(all first-draft/effective, not exact).**
- **New reusable struct: `DDSurfaceDescPadded0x7c`.** The original's DDSURFACEDESC-shaped stack

  `ddsCaps.dwCaps` all match this header's real layout exactly — not a different field order,

  newer/bigger `ddraw.h` while still calling the `DDSURFACEDESC`-typed API). Modeled as
  `struct DDSurfaceDescPadded0x7c { DDSURFACEDESC ddsd; unsigned int reserved[4]; };`, with
  `ddsd.dwSize = 0x7c;` marked `// sic` (a literal, not `sizeof()`). **Any future `CreateSurface`/
  `Lock` call site in this TU family should reuse this struct.**

  (memcpy, if owned) or aliases it (if shared), clones the pixel buffer, and — if `src->pSurface`

  reapplies the colorkey. Residual: an intrinsic 0xc-byte stack-slot-offset gap between the
  `u`/`rect` locals and the original, confirmed NOT declaration/init-order-sensitive via 3

  any other `bConverted` value is a silent no-op. Confirmed the original's 3 early-exit sites do

- **`Convert()`** (`0x42a3d0`) + its callee **`LocoBitmap::PixelCopyBlit`** (new name for

  only `destRect.left`/`.top` are read by the body (`.right`/`.bottom` dead, still built because
  the caller constructs a full RECT), while `srcRect`'s all 4 fields are used (origin + end of
  the source region to copy). Switching from 10 flat ints to this RECT-by-value shape closed

## RF archive reader

Custom "RF" format: `resource.RFH` (index) + `resource.RFD` (57 MB blob), optional per-file
Huffman compression (`loco/rf-extract.py`, `loco/rfh.txt` = full listing).

- **`RFIndex::Open` (0x45caa0): TRANSCRIBED AND EXACT** (v471, `src/UIResources.cpp`, 603 B).
  Closes any open file; swaps the path extension to `"RFH"` (via `sprintf`, not `strcpy`),
  `fopen`s `"rb"`, then loops `while (!feof(pFile))` reading one index record per iteration —
  **FOUR `fread`s**, `[u32 namelen][name][u32 size][u32 flags]` (the two trailing dwords are
  size THEN flags, matching `rf-extract.py`; note `RFRecord` stores them in the opposite order)
  — into 16-byte `RFRecord`s from `operator new(0x10)`, **appending via an O(n²) tail-walk on
  every insert** — a genuine original-engine perf characteristic, reproduced (`// sic:`). On
  EOF: `fclose`, `sprintf` the extension to `"RFD"`, reopen — the persistent handle
  `LoadResource` reads — and `malloc`/`strcpy` a copy of that path into `pRfdPath0xc`. Returns
  whether the `.RFD` opened. Both path buffers are `char[400]`. `this` arrives as a parameter
  (register-relative), so its field writes generate zero fixed-address xrefs — it was findable
  only by TU-contiguity, not xref-chasing. The archive is opened exactly once, early, and no
  close path was found (flagged open, could exist unexercised).
- **`RFIndex::LoadResource` (0x45cd00): TRANSCRIBED AND EXACT** (v514, `src/UIResources.cpp`,
  236 B). Null-guards `pFile`, then walks the index list summing every preceding record's
  `size` — the sum IS the match's data offset in the `.RFD` (records packed head-to-tail in
  index order) — `_stricmp`-matching `pName`; `fseek`s, `_malloc`s `size`, `fread`s. Plain
  records (`flags == 0`) return the buffer with `*outSize = size`; Huffman ones get inflated
  into a second buffer sized by the blob's leading dword (the uncompressed length, read via
  `DerefIntMaybe`/0x45c820) by `Rf_HuffmanDecompress` (0x45c830, see below), which
  also fills `*outSize`, and the compressed copy is freed. Load-bearing shape: the scan is one
  `while (pRec != NULL && _stricmp(...) != 0)` — an outer null guard around any do/for(;;)
  form makes /Og peel the first iteration and tail-merge the loop's null break into
  `return 0`.
- **`Rf_HuffmanDecompress` (0x45c830): TRANSCRIBED AND EXACT** (v534, `src/UIResources.cpp`,
  105 B) — and it is **the only HAND-WRITTEN ASSEMBLY found in the app region so far**. `cld`/
  `lodsd` string ops and the `sar`/`adc`/`lea` bit-extraction triple are constructs cl emits
  from no C, so the original source is an `__asm` block and the transcription is a verbatim
  copy of it. Only the trailing `*pnOutSize = *(int *)pCompressed;` is C — the compiler
  interleaves its own `pop edi/esi/ebx` through those instructions, which it would never do
  inside a verbatim `__asm` block, and that interleaving is how the boundary was located.
  Stream layout, cross-checked against `loco/rf-extract.py`'s `huff_decompress()` (a working
  reference decoder for the same format): `[0]` u32 decompressed size, `[4]` u32 root node,
  `[8]` a 0x800-byte node table of u16 pairs, `[0x808]` the LSB-first bitstream. Each step
  indexes `tree[node * 4 + bit * 2]`; a node below 0x100 is a terminal and IS the literal byte,
  after which the walk restarts from the root. One deviation from the reference: bits refill a
  DWORD at a time (`dec ecx` from 32), not a byte at a time — same bit order, wider refill.
  Two idioms worth not re-deriving: `dec edx` in the preamble pre-decrements the write pointer
  so the per-symbol `inc edx` lands on output byte 0 (there is no post-store increment), and
  `mov bx, [edi+ebx]` writing only the low half of `ebx` is safe ONLY because the table is
  0x800 bytes — `node <= 0x1ff` keeps the `lea`-scaled index under 0x800, so no stale high bits
  survive to defeat the `cmp ebx, 100h` terminal test.
- **`RFIndex`** (16 bytes, embedded in UIResources at +0x18): `0x0 pFile` (FILE*, the RFD
  handle), `0x4 pRecords` (list head), `0x8 Unk0x8` (zeroed twice, never read),
  `0xc pRfdPath0xc` (malloc'd copy of the .RFD path). **`RFRecord`** (16 bytes): `0x0
  pName`, `0x4 flags` (bit0 = compressed), `0x8 size`, `0xc pNext`.
- **`LoadResource` caller clustering** (16 functions / 18 sites):

  | Address(es) | Subsystem |
  |---|---|
  | `0x43d820`, `0x409e70` | Layouts loader — `<installdir>\Layouts\index.lay` (see Layout sharing) |
  | `0x42ab10` | `LocoBitmap::LoadMaybe` (generic BMP loader, loose-file fallback) |
  | `0x447ba0` | `ThumbnailBmp_LoadMaybe` |
  | `0x415a00` | `InitFields` — `post\Edit\colour.dat` |
  | `0x424bf0`, `0x41e6e0`, `0x436490`, `0x40e690`, `0x44b290` | the 5 `CursorDesc`-family `LoadMaybe` bodies (`"%s%s.dat"`/`"%s%s.bmp"` path building) |
  | `0x44fb10`, `0x40fe50` | `"%s%s%s"` 3-part (theme-prefixable) paths — `ResourceRefCategoryTable_LoadCategoryFileMaybe` and one unread |
  | `0x40e950` | `"%s%s\%s"`-ish, unread |
  | `0x448a70`, `0x413660` | WAV resources (DirectSound TU) |
  | `0x438e40` | `NetResource_RequestMissingAppearances` (GameNet) |

- **`Ddraw_Init` (0x45b500, EFFECTIVE, `src/Ddraw.cpp` — transcribed v530):** `DirectDrawCreate()`
  → `DAT_004a9908` (`IDirectDraw`) → QI `IID_IDirectDraw4` → `DAT_00485440` (the handle ~all DDraw
  code uses, 23 callers; really an **`IDirectDraw4*`**, modelled as `IDirectDraw2*` because every
  slot any transcribed caller uses is at the same offset in both). ⚠ The old note that this needs
  a DX5 SDK header is **REFUTED** — every descriptor field it touches is at an identical offset in
  `DDSURFACEDESC` and `DDSURFACEDESC2`, so `DDSurfaceDescPadded0x7c` covers it; see CODEGEN #99.
  `SetCooperativeLevel` on two branches gated by `g_screenSaver.bScreenSaverMode` (0x4a9918, NOT
  `DAT_00485918`): **`== 1` (screen-saver mode) takes `(g_pApp->hwndOwner, DDSCL_FULLSCREEN |
  DDSCL_NOWINDOWCHANGES | DDSCL_EXCLUSIVE)`, everything else takes `(NULL, DDSCL_NORMAL)`** — the
  windowed-vs-exclusive question the old note left open, now settled.
  `CreateSurface` → `DAT_004fd3c0` (**primary/front**, 28 xrefs, `DDSCAPS_PRIMARYSURFACE`) and
  `DAT_004fd3c4` (**back/work surface**, 99 xrefs, sized to `g_worldBoard`'s viewport and asked
  for as `DDSCAPS_OFFSCREENPLAIN | DDSCAPS_SYSTEMMEMORY` — SYSTEM memory, not video; on failure it
  retries once with the IDENTICAL caps and arguments, `// sic:`). Then it keys the work surface's
  magenta (`DDCKEY_SRCBLT`, 0x7c1f in 555 / 0xf81f in 565) and attaches a clipper to the primary
  surface, creating one only when `GetClipper` returns `DDERR_NOCLIPPERATTACHED`.
  Probes the red bitmask (`== 0x7c00`) to detect **555 vs 565** and writes the format-descriptor
  globals:

  | Global | 555 | 565 | Meaning |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `DAT_00485274` | 0x22b | 0x235 | format tag |
  | `DAT_00485278` | 10 | 11 | red-field bit shift |
  | `DAT_0048527c` | 5 | 6 | green-field bit width |
  | `DAT_00485280` | 0x3def | 0x7bef | post-`>>1` channel-bleed guard mask for the 50%-alpha shadow/blend blitter family (`0x42bec0`/`0x42c050`/`0x42c130`/`0x42c220`/`0x42c470`: `(a>>1 & m) + (b>>1 & m)`) |
  | `DAT_00485288/8c/90` | raw R/G/B masks from `GetSurfaceDesc` | | uninterpreted |

### DDrawSurface TU (`src/DDrawSurface.cpp`) — the FIRST .obj in `.text` — COMPLETE (5/5 EXACT)

`0x401000..0x40161f`, 1533 bytes, all five functions byte-matched. Pinned as one TU by
contiguity (the five run back to back with only `nop` padding, and 0x401620 is
`PostBagFileCache`'s constructor, a different .obj). **Distinct from `src/Ddraw.cpp`**, which
owns 0x45baa0/0x45bbc0 some 350 KB further into `.text` — same subsystem, different compile
unit; the shared declarations live in `src/Ddraw.h`.

Nothing here was blocked on the DirectX 5 header problem that still holds `Ddraw_Init` back:
`Blt`/`Restore`/`GetSurfaceDesc`/`GetDC`/`ReleaseDC`/`Lock`/`Unlock` are all present at the
right vtable slots in the DX2-era `<ddraw.h>` VC5 ships, and the one DX5-shaped thing (the
124-byte CreateSurface descriptor) was already modelled as `DDSurfaceDescPadded0x7c`.

| addr | name | size | what it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0x401000 | `DDraw_CreateSurfaceFromFile` | 368 | `GetFileAttributesA` → `LoadImageA(LR_LOADFROMFILE)` → `CreateSurface` → colorkey → StretchBlt → `DeleteObject`. **Carries an original engine bug** (video-memory retry re-uses the failed caps — see `docs/engine-bugs.md`). Its 2nd parameter is read into nothing; the one call site passes `LR_LOADFROMFILE`, which the body hardcodes anyway. |
| 0x401170 | `DDraw_StretchBlitBitmapToSurface` | 269 | ⚠ **SIX parameters, not the five Ghidra had inferred** (`pSurface, hBitmap, short xSrc, short ySrc, int nWidth, int nHeight`) — confirmed by 0x401000's own call site pushing 6 dwords (`add esp, 0x18`). `Restore`s the surface first, then blits the GDI bitmap through `GetDC` stretched to the surface's full extent. `nWidth`/`nHeight` of 0 mean "the bitmap's own". A failed `CreateCompatibleDC` is logged but NOT bailed on — that is the original's shape. |
| 0x401280 | `Ddraw_BltUpdateRect` | 601 | Present one client-area rect from the work surface to the primary, mapping client→screen coords and clipping to the window. Every `DDERR_SURFACELOST` retry also re-dirties the whole board viewport (a restored surface has lost its contents, so the cached dirty-tile set no longer describes the screen). See `docs/CODEGEN.md` #43 for the one-instruction lesson that closed it. |
| 0x4014e0 | `DDraw_QuerySurfaceDims` | 82 | The surface's width/height, **narrowed to 16 bits** (the body writes both out-params with `mov WORD PTR`, never a full dword). `src/LocoBitmap.cpp` and `src/PopupWndBase.cpp` still carry file-local `extern` declarations of it typed `unsigned int *` and cast at the call site — wider than the function really writes. Harmless (we never link) but they should converge on `src/DDrawSurface.h`'s declaration when those extern blocks are retired. |

Locks the shared work surface through `WorldBoardMaybe`'s cached descriptor/guard pair only if it is not already held, so a caller that already holds it pays nothing. Always returns 1. See `docs/CODEGEN.md` #44 for the `unsigned short`-storage / `int`-counter split its loops need. |

Callers of `Ddraw_BltUpdateRect` (12 sites): `UpdateDirtyTiles` (0x456695),
`CommitScreenUpdate` (3), `LoadingScreen_Show`/`LoadingScreen_Animate` (6), `AppWndProc` (2).

## Tile/scenery placement and world objects

Pure game/placement logic, DDraw-adjacent but distinct (none of these call DDraw directly).

- **`0x420000`** — RESOLVED 2026-07-29 (v494): `ScriptEventLoader::ProcessInsertSeqSpawnsMaybe`,
  TRANSCRIBED in `src/ScriptEventLoader.cpp` (PARTIAL, 195/195 insns, parked -- see
  docs/PARKED.md v494). Not "scenery-type dispatch": it is the InsertSeq spawn pump. See the
  ScriptEventLoader section.
- **`0x456d90`** — `WorldBoardMaybe::CheckInsertSeqPerimeterMaybe` (**READ AND TRANSCRIBED
  2026-07-27**, `src/WorldBoardMaybe.cpp`, EFFECTIVE at 241/241 instructions; the earlier
  "grid bounds/collision" reading was a description of its indexing, not its purpose). The
  PLACEMENT PRECONDITION a kind descriptor's InsertSeq record (`BigObj` +0x560 count /
  +0x564 values) encodes: starting from the object's front-row tile it walks the one-tile-wide
  perimeter around its footprint clockwise — right along the row above, down the column to its
  right, left along the row below, up the column to its left — consuming ONE InsertSeq entry per
  tile. `-1` = don't care, `0` = that tile must be EMPTY, anything else = the tile's plane-A
  occupant's kind must carry that `resourceId`. Four loops share one running index and one
  running verdict, and each stops the moment the sequence runs out or the verdict goes false.
  Footprint extents come from the descriptor's BITMAP occupancy pair (+0x16b/+0x16c), not its
  physical one. The grid indexing is `this->aTileCellsMaybe[x * 65 + y].aPlaneASlotsMaybe[0]`
  while the BOUNDS come from the `g_worldBoard` global rather than `this`. ⚠ Reproduced engine
  bug: the ring's bottom-left corner is visited twice, so a walk consumes `2*cols + 2*rows + 5`
  entries for `2*cols + 2*rows + 4` tiles (docs/engine-bugs.md).
- **The track-graph cluster** (`0x457380`–`0x457b60`, the tail of `WorldBoardMaybe`'s .obj) —
  fully read 2026-07-27: every function in it is now transcribed, eight of the nine EXACT.
  - **`BigObj::IsPlainRunMaybe` (`0x41f430`, EXACT, `src/Obj0x4779e0.cpp`)** — "is this kind a
    PLAIN RUN rather than something the navigation graph should give a node of its own": a
    track-family piece (`categoryByte` 3) whose `m_type0x63a` is a straight or a curve
    (`IsType0x63aInSetE`/`InSet10`), or one of the two plain path pieces (`categoryByte` 0xc,
    `resourceId` 0x3001/0x3002). This is the predicate all four graph walkers use to decide
    which tiles to step THROUGH on the way to the next junction. ⚠ Its home TU is
    `src/Obj0x4779e0.cpp` (address adjacency to `ParseSeqRecordMaybe`) even though its `BigObj`
    siblings live in `src/CursorDesc.cpp`.
  - **`TrackGraph_GetLinkCostAMaybe` (`0x457b60`, EXACT, `src/WorldBoardMaybe.cpp`)** — the EDGE
    COST between two adjacent tile kinds, `-1` when they do not connect at all: the gate every
    walker runs before accepting a neighbour, and the per-step weight
    `LinkTrackGraphNeighbours*Maybe` accumulates along a run. Path-to-path (both 0xc) costs
    **50**, track-to-track (both 3) costs **10** — so a route prefers rail over walking 5:1 —
    and a path and a track meet only at a LEVEL CROSSING, recognised in the same two shapes
    `NetSessionEventQueue`'s own crossing scan uses (track side `IsType0x63aInSet12` with the
    path side above `resourceId` 0x3010, or track side `IsType0x63aInSetE`), also costing 10.
    ⚠ It is a `__thiscall` **MEMBER** of `WorldBoardMaybe`, NOT the free `__stdcall` function it
    was first transcribed as (CORRECTED 2026-07-27). It never reads `this`, so its own body is
    byte-identical under either spelling (`ret 0x8` both ways) and matched EXACT while
    mis-modeled; the only evidence anywhere is the `mov ecx,ebp` its callers emit in front of the
    call. Renamed with an `A` suffix to pair with the B-graph twin below.
  - **`TrackGraph_GetLinkCostBMaybe` (`0x457c20`, EXACT, was `FUN_00457c20`)** — the same for
    graph B, the ROAD network, and also a `this`-ignoring member. Every accepted edge costs a
    flat **100**: graph B has no rail-versus-foot preference to express, so it is a pure
    connectivity table rather than a weighting. Road↔road and road→path always connect; road↔track
    only across a points/switch orientation (`IsType0x63aInSet10`); path→road only when the path
    side is a plain run; path→path only when BOTH sides are. Written as nested `switch`es on the
    two `categoryByte`s, which is visible in the codegen — cl lowers each as a `sub`/`je` chain
    over the cases actually present, so the arms that merely fall through to the `-1` default are
    still there to read.
  - **`IsTrackGraphNodeAMaybe` (`0x4573e0`, EXACT)** / **`IsTrackGraphNodeBMaybe` (`0x4576b0`,
    EXACT)** — "does this tile deserve a TrackGraphNode of its own rather than being a plain run
    between two junctions". Four steps: walk each of the four directions THROUGH intervening
    plain runs until a non-run tile is reached and drop the branch if the link cost is negative;
    count the survivors under an OPPOSITE-PAIR rule (branch `i` counts only when the
    perpendicular `i+1` also survived, or the branch straight opposite did not — so a tile with
    exactly two opposite branches is a pass-through and scores 0); for graph selector 7 on a full
    4-way crossing only, discount the four DIAGONAL neighbours whose category is 0xc; and finally
    force a node for two specific kind ids. B is the same function without the diagonal step.
    Both take `(TilePlacedObj *, short)` — the callers pass their `TrackGraph::nGraphKindMaybe` —
    and B never reads the selector, which is why it still returns via `ret 0x8`.
    ⚠ The diagonal step OVERWRITES the branch array, so the final kind-id checks inspect the
    diagonals on the paths that reach them: see `docs/engine-bugs.md`.
  - **`LinkTrackGraphNeighbours{A,B}Maybe` (`0x457830`/`0x457900`, both EXACT)** — fill the
    tile's four graph-A/graph-B neighbour slots. Per direction, walk outward one tile at a time
    accumulating the run's cost, stopping at the first tile that is unreachable, already a graph
    node, or off the board. The tile RECORDED is the last non-plain-run tile seen, so a run of
    plain track/path between two junctions collapses into ONE edge whose cost is the sum of its
    steps — exactly the edge `TrackGraph::BuildAdjacency*Maybe` then shares between the two nodes.
    The cost accumulates on every accepted step while the slot only updates on non-plain-run
    tiles; the two tests are deliberately not the same.
  - **`GetNeighborObject` (`0x4579d0`, EFFECTIVE, DIFF 52/392)** — the primitive all four walkers
    step with, and more than a grid offset. The step is taken from the object's own ENTRY/EXIT
    POINT on that edge (`BigObj +0x5fc`, `aEntryExitMaybe`), not from its tile position; a kind
    whose record leaves the edge at (0, 0) has no connection there at all; and the neighbour is
    then asked for ITS entry/exit point on the OPPOSITE edge (`(dir - 2) & 3`), with the two
    points required to lie within a squared distance of 0x11 of each other. That last test is
    what stops a run of track from turning a corner it does not physically make. A neighbour with
    no kind descriptor skips the proximity test. See `docs/PARKED.md`.
  - **`BuildTrackGraphsIfReadyMaybe` (`0x457380`, EXACT)** — rebuilds each non-empty graph's
    routes while app-state is 3, then raises `bTrackGraphsBuiltFlag`. The state is re-tested
    BETWEEN the two graphs, so a state change during graph A's rebuild leaves graph B untouched
    and the flag down.

  **Transcribed 2026-07-26** (`src/WorldBoardMaybe.cpp`): `WorldBoardMaybe::PlaceObject`
  (`0x4550c0`, PARTIAL) and `WorldBoardMaybe::FindNearestObjOfCategoryMaybe` (`0x457ce0`, EXACT).
  `PlaceObject` stamps a newly created object into every cell its kind's **two** occupancy tables
  claim: the physical footprint (`aFootprintOccupancyMaskMaybe`, X×Y×layers) fills plane-A slots
  one per layer, and the bitmap footprint (`aBitmapOccupancySlotGridMaybe`) fills plane B, where
  the grid entry is the **1-based** plane-B slot index to claim (0 = tile not covered). Only the
  plane-B pass dirties tiles. Unless the caller says otherwise, `row` is first biased by
  `bBitmapOccupancyRowsMaybe - bFootprintYStepsMaybe`, i.e. the two footprints disagree about
  where the object's origin sits; both legality passes (`TestOrClearFootprintMaybe`, ex-
  `FUN_004553e0` — pass 0 tests, pass 1 also EVICTS what it finds) then add that bias straight
  back, so they are always asked about the row the caller named.
  `FindNearestObjOfCategoryMaybe` walks square rings outward from the tile containing a pixel
  position, one edge at a time (each edge dropping the corner the previous one covered), keeping
  the best squared distance; its "found" test sits at the TOP of the ring loop, so the ring that
  produced a hit is finished before the search stops — which is what makes the result the
  *nearest* match rather than the first one seen.

  **Transcribed 2026-07-26 (v419)**, completing the place/unplace pair:
  `WorldBoardMaybe::TestOrClearFootprintMaybe` (`0x4553e0`, **EXACT**) and
  `WorldBoardMaybe::FlushQueuedBigObjMaybe` (`0x455ab0`, PARTIAL).
  `TestOrClearFootprintMaybe` walks the PHYSICAL footprint mask nested layer-outermost (where
  `PlaceObject` walks it row-outermost) and answers "is every tile this kind wants free?". Free
  is a three-way test and only the middle case refuses: an empty plane-A slot passes, and so does
  an occupied one whose occupant is *evictable* — the master gate `DAT_004fd3dc` is on, the
  occupant is saveable (`+0xc0`), and either the placement cursor is not snap-locked
  (`PlacementCursorMaybe +0xe4`) or the app state (`g_nScreenState`) is 3 or 1. Anything else
  clears the result but does NOT return early, so the eviction pass still completes for the tiles
  that did pass. Before any of that, a map-edge connector kind (`categoryByte == 3` and
  `BigObj::IsType0x63aInSet1234`) must also satisfy `BigObj::IsAtMatchingBoardEdgeMaybe`
  (`0x44bdb0`, ex-`FUN_0044bdb0`): `m_type0x63a` 1 wants column 0, 2 the right edge
  (`col + bBitmapOccupancyColsMaybe == wCols`), 3 the top
  (`row == bBitmapOccupancyRowsMaybe - bFootprintYStepsMaybe`) and 4 the bottom
  (`row + bBitmapOccupancyRowsMaybe == wRows`) — i.e. this is what refuses to let a tunnel mouth
  be built anywhere but on its own board edge.
  `FlushQueuedBigObjMaybe` is `PlaceObject`'s exact inverse: it walks the bitmap footprint (plane
  B) then the physical one (plane A, biased by the same Y-extent difference), clears any slot
  still holding the object, and compacts that plane's high-water mark back down over the trailing
  holes; only the plane-B pass dirty-marks, the same asymmetry `PlaceObject` has. It then hands
  the object to `NetSessionEventQueue::BigObj_Remove`. Both per-cell scans run slot-DOWNWARD, and
  the two planes disagree about where to start — plane B always sweeps all 7 slots from 6, plane
  A starts at the cell's own current count.
  **Both plane counts are SIGNED** (`char`, not `byte`): `-1` is the "plane empty" resting value,
  which the down-scans (`>= 0`) and the compaction step (which decrements past 0) both need.
  Corrected in the Ghidra `BoardTileCellMaybe` struct and in `src/WorldBoardMaybe.h` in v419.

  **Dirty-bitmap bit index is `wCols * row + col`, row-major, everywhere** —
  `MarkRectDirty`, `FlushQueuedBigObjMaybe`, and both readers (`UpdateDirtyTiles`, `0x456700`).
  `src/`'s `PlaceObject` carried the transposed spelling until v419; it is not an engine bug,
  just a transcription error that was invisible because both forms are one `imul` plus one `add`.

  **Off-by-one bound-check bug** (`WorldBoardMaybe_GetPlaneASlotMaybe`/`0x455620`,
  `WorldBoardMaybe_GetPlaneBOccupantPositionMaybe`/`0x455740`, and — confirmed v432 —
  `GetPlaneASlotGridPosMaybe`/`0x4557c0`): the bounds checks allow index
  `0x51`/`0x41` (i.e. `< 0x52`/`< 0x42`), one past the true 81×65 physical capacity in each
  axis — X=81 aliases into the `+0x52484` tail fields, Y=65 aliases into column X+1 row 0.
  Not exploitable under normal play (would need gameplay to reach those exact edge tile
  coords); `// sic`-flag at both call sites per project convention rather than "fixing."

  - **44 bytes**, pinned hard by `WorldBoardMaybe_InitFieldsMaybe`'s own two
    `push 0x2c; call operator new` sites (0x454d20/0x454d51). Those also pin the ctor argument:
    `pTrackGraphAMaybe = new TrackGraph(7)` and `pTrackGraphBMaybe = new TrackGraph(8)` — so

    `ShortInitObj0x45cdf0` placeholder: 0x45cdf0 was never an embedded sub-object of the board,
    it is `TrackGraph::TrackGraph`.
  - Layout: `nNodeCount` +0x0, `paDirMatrix` +0x4, `papNode` +0x8, `nGraphKindMaybe` +0xc, then
    five pure-SCRATCH members (`pabVisitedMaybe` +0x10, `nRouteStepCountMaybe` +0x14,
    `pabRouteDirMaybe` +0x18, `panRouteNodeIdMaybe` +0x1c, `panBestCostMaybe` +0x20,
    `papRouteTreeMaybe` +0x24, `papRouteTreeParentMaybe` +0x28) that only hold allocations
    between `BuildAllRoutesMaybe`'s own malloc and free — which is why the actors' read-only
    view of the class never saw them.
  - It is a **JUNCTION graph, not a tile graph**: only tiles the board's
    `IsTrackGraphNodeAMaybe`/`BMaybe` predicate (0x4573e0/0x4576b0) calls a junction get a
    `TrackGraphNode`, and a plain unbranching run of path/road between two junctions collapses
    into one `TrackGraphEdge` whose `nCostMaybe` is the run's length. That is exactly why
    `TilePlacedObj::nGraphNodeIdAMaybe`/`nGraphNodeIdBMaybe` are −1 most of the time — a −1 is
    what sends both pathfinders to their per-tile cost argmin instead of to this graph.
  - Routing is **precomputed, not searched at run time**. `BuildAllRoutesMaybe` (0x45d560) runs
    an all-pairs pass: per source node, `PropagateDistanceMaybe` (0x45d6c0) does a depth-first
    cheapest-cost relaxation building a spanning tree of node COPIES (marking edges
    already-taken in `TrackGraphEdge::Unk0x4`, saved and restored around each descent), then
    `SolveRouteMaybe` (0x45dbc0) walks that tree per destination and stamps the first step of
    the winner. `StampRoutePairsMaybe` (0x45dad0) exploits the fact that every sub-route of a
    cheapest route is itself cheapest, stamping BOTH directions of every pair along the winner
    rather than re-searching them. At run time each actor only calls `GetStepDirectionMaybe`.
  - `paDirMatrix` is **lower-triangular** and packs BOTH directions of a node pair into one
    byte (bits 0–1 and bits 2–3), so an N-node graph costs N·(N−1)/2 bytes rather than N².

    `GetStepDirectionMaybe` (0x45dd80) reads it, `SetStepDirectionMaybe` (0x45dde0) writes it.

    path in GetOppositePath\n")` default — expanded at all three of its call sites (both
    `BuildAdjacency` twins and `StampRoutePairsMaybe`). It has no standalone address.
  - ⚠ `BuildAdjacencyBMaybe` carries a `nGraphKindMaybe == 7` branch that stamps the tile's
    graph-**A** node-id slot. Only graph B ever calls it and graph B is always 8, so the branch
    is **dead** — a leftover of the copy-and-edit that made B out of A.

     free-slot-insert failure, and the "eviction not requested" guard) must be written as
     three SEPARATE, explicit `return` statements**, not one shared trailing return reached by
     fallthrough — the original duplicates the cheap 2-instruction "load return value + jump
     to epilogue" tail at each site rather than merging them into one shared point (the
     opposite tie-break from the more commonly-documented "independent returns don't
     auto-share, force it with `goto`" lesson — here plain source-level duplication was

  zeroed them in the opposite order) and MUST be declared (and the whole cache-search loop
  placed) *after* both buffers per the original's own instruction order, not before.

`bCarSlotOccupiedCount` (+0x8d, was `Unk0x8dMaybe` — a live occupancy counter incremented by
`GetCarSlotMaybe`/0x458430 each time a new car fills an empty `+0x90` decor slot, NOT dead state),
`bSaveableFlag` (+0xc0, was `Unk0xc0Maybe` — ctor sets 1; cleared for auto-placed global
edge-link connectors and default-backdrop-board loads; `SaveBoardLayout` only serializes items
with this byte set, `WorldBoardMaybe::FlushQueuedBigObjMaybe` gates unregister-and-destroy on it
— deliberately NOT named `bReady`, since the embedded `AnimDescRefObj0x477488` base already has
its own unrelated `bReady` at a different offset), `dwPlacementArgB` (+0xbc, was `Unk0xbcMaybe` —
reconciled with `NetSessionEventQueue.cpp`'s own divergently-named `dwUnkBcMaybe` partial-view
field for the same offset; confirmed a straight round-trip,
`ObjectPlacementRecord::dwArgBMaybe` → this field on load → back to `rec.dwArgBMaybe` on save,
concrete per-kind meaning still unknown). **Biggest finding: `TrackConnectorTileObj`/
`TrackDepotTileObj::dwUnk0x124Maybe` (+0x124) was RETYPED, not just renamed** — it's the head of
a real singly-linked FIFO (`TrainClaimWaitNode{PeerTrainNode *pTrain; TrainClaimWaitNode *pNext;}`,
new struct in `src/TilePlacedObj.h`) of trains waiting to claim/couple at this tile once it frees
up: both leaf dtors walk-and-delete it, `FUN_0044f3a0` appends (called from
`PeerTrainNode::PeerTrainNode_UpdatePlacementTickMaybe`'s non-global-connector branch),
`FUN_0044f410` removes a specific node by `(wTrainId, byte)`, and `FUN_00412a80` (a per-tick pump)
pops the head once `pOwningTrain==0` and hands the popped train to
`PeerTrainNode::ClaimDecorObjMaybe`. Named `pClaimWaitQueueHeadMaybe` (deliberately NOT
`pPendingTrainQueueHead` — that exact identifier is `DPlaySessionMgr`'s own, conceptually-similar
but structurally distinct session-level queue). `TrackDepotTileObj::bClaimLockedFlag` (+0x128,
was `bUnk0x128Maybe`) — a re-entrant-claim guard bit, distinct from `dwOccupancyClaim`'s own
0/1/2 occupancy state; set on successful claim start, cleared by `FUN_00412a80` once the owning
train's own state shows it departed.

## DirectSound

**Import disambiguation** (DPLAYX and DSOUND both import by ordinal):

| IAT addr | Library | Ordinal | Real API |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0x4637d8` | DPLAYX.DLL | 1 | `DirectPlayCreate` |
| `0x4637de` | DSOUND.DLL | 1 | `DirectSoundCreate` |
| `0x4637e4` | DSOUND.DLL | 2 | `DirectSoundEnumerateA` |
| `0x4637d2` | DPLAYX.DLL | 4 | `DirectPlayLobbyCreateA` |

  (`DAT_004fd3bc`, 0xb8 bytes, ctor 0x412bd0); calls the device init then the listener
  broadcast, and applies ini `[Sound] VolumeLow/Med/High` (defaults 75/75/78).

  nDefaultChannelCount, HWND hwndOwner)` (return type CORRECTED v88: byte-truncated
  BOOL/`unsigned char`, not `unsigned int`/`HRESULT` — every return point sets only AL; see
  `docs/PARKED.md` item 12). Returns 0 on any DirectSoundCreate/SetCooperativeLevel failure,
  1 on success. Sole caller passes 16 and the main app HWND
  (`DAT_004aa4a0+8`). Ini `[Sound] SelectBestDevice` (default 1) enumerates devices
  (callback `LAB_00412fb0`) to pick a GUID before `DirectSoundCreate`. `GetCaps` (0x60-byte

  caps.dwFreeHwMixingStaticBuffers != 0) ? max(dwFreeHwMixingStaticBuffers-1, nDefault) :
  nDefault`; channel array allocated `count*0x3c+4` (array-with-header idiom via 0x4671e0);
  per channel `DSoundChannel::Init` (0x40ec70, byte-matched) then 0x40f040 copies the 4
  category ceilings.

    self-clear `pExternalHandle` if bound, reset state to idle).
  - `ClearExternalHandle`/`BindExternalHandle` — MATCHED. A weak-reference idiom: a caller
    can hold a `DSoundChannel**` "handle" that the channel nulls out the moment it releases
    itself, so external code can detect a channel got reclaimed out from under it.

    re-asserting state=2; otherwise rewinds to position 0 (unless coming from the paused
    state, in which case it resumes without rewinding) and re-`Play`s honoring the loop flag.
  - `IsIdle` — MATCHED (`nState==1`).
  - `IsReclaimable` (ex-`FUN_0040eeb0`) — PARKED (jump-table-vs-ifchain compiler threshold,
    not source-steerable at 4 cases). True for idle(1)/the transitional state(4) and for
    playing(2) channels the hardware reports as actually finished; false for paused(3) and
    for playing(2) channels still genuinely active. This is the manager's "can I steal this
    channel" predicate (see `DSound::ReclaimFinishedChannels` below).
  - `SetBounds(int x, int y)` — MATCHED. **CORRECTED 2026-07-14: this was the function
    previously mis-documented as `SetXY0x40ef00`, "a generic widget XY setter with 5+
    unrelated callers."** `get_xrefs_to` shows exactly ONE caller
    (`DSound_SetListenerPosition`), and the body calls `DSoundChannel::SetPosition` by raw
    address, which only makes sense against a real `DSoundChannel*` — the old claim is
    retracted. Sets `nBoundX/nBoundY` then re-applies `SetPosition` with the unchanged
    current position to recompute pan against the new bounds.
  - `SetPosition(int x, int y)` — PARKED (register-swap class; algorithm confirmed
    correct). Clamps `(x,y)` into `[0, nBound)`, then computes stereo pan: `offset =
    (x - nBoundX/2) / (nBoundX/2)` (a signed [-1,1]-ish fraction from center); `offset==0` →
    pan 0 (centered); `|offset|==1` → pan ±10000 (DirectSound's `DSBPAN` extremes); else
    `pan = ±1000 * log2(1/(1-|offset|))`, sign matching `offset`. Re-derived from raw x87
    disasm (`fldln2`+`fyl2x` twice + `fdivp` = `log(ratio)/log(2.0)`, i.e. true base-2 log —
    this is what Ghidra's decompiler labels bare `log2(...)` calls, one per `fldln2+fyl2x`
    pair) and confirmed constant-for-constant against the `.rdata` doubles at
    0x477628/30/38/40 (0.0/1.0/10000.0/2.0).
  - `SetCeilingsAndApply(int low, int med, int high1, int high2)` — MATCHED (sets the 4
    ceiling fields, declaration-order-sensitive: natural param order low/med/high1/high2
    matches, NOT the order Ghidra's own pseudocode happens to print them in).
  - `SetCategory(int category)`/`SetVolume(int percent)` — `SetCategory` MATCHED.
    `SetVolume` PARKED (register-swap class; algorithm confirmed correct): looks up the
    ceiling by `nCategory`, `atten = (uint)(ceiling*percent) * 0.01` (the unsigned cast
    forces the 64-bit-fild-with-zeroed-high-dword idiom for a safe uint→double convert, one
    fild site PER SWITCH CASE in the original — this only reproduces when each case computes
    the double directly rather than through a shared post-switch int variable); `atten<=0`→
    -10000 (silence), `atten>=100`→0 (full volume, 0 dB), else `db = 1.0 -
    exp((255.0 - atten*2.55) * 0.03611937255272424)` — the `exp()` inlines via the classic
    x87 idiom (`fldl2e`/`frndint`/`f2xm1`/`fscale`), confirmed constant-for-constant against
    0x477658/68/70/78 (0.01/2.55/255.0/0.03611937255272424) and the -10000.0/0.0 clamps at
