### WAV/RIFF loader TU (`src/Wav.cpp`) — Phase 4's 3rd DirectSound-cluster TU

**Tiny, self-contained TU, address-contiguous 0x413660-0x413ab0** (starts immediately after
`src/DSound.cpp`'s 0x41365a with no gap, ends where the unrelated `PopupWndBase::PopupWndBase`
begins) — just 2 real functions plus the `/GX`-auto-generated `catch(int)` funclet. **First use
in this project of a genuine, explicit `try`/`catch`** (not just RAII auto-unwind scaffolding
— confirmed by a real `Catch_00413971` funclet with its own resume address) and **first direct
use of the statically-linked iostream classes** (`istream`/`ifstream`/`istrstream` from
`toolchain/vc50/INCLUDE`'s real VC5 headers) as actual C++ types rather than opaque cross-TU
externs. WIP as of v93 — semantics fully understood and both functions compile with correct
call shapes (confirmed via raw disasm cross-check against the real header declarations, plus
Ghidra's own EH-analyzer decompile of the catch funclet), but NOT yet byte-matching (582/806 +
160/320); both remaining residuals confirmed intrinsic/dead-ended this session (a caller-buffer
undersizing bug found+fixed, a stack-slot reuse tie-break, and a block-duplication layout
artifact — see `docs/PARKED.md`) — deprioritized in favor of a new TU pending a fresh idea.

- **`Wav_ParseAndLoad(LPCSTR pszPath, WavResource *pOut)`** (0x413660) — loads a WAV
  resource by path: tries the RF archive first (`g_RFIndexMaybe.LoadResource`, stripping the
  fixed install-path prefix `DAT_004a99c8` via `strlen`), falling back to a loose
  `ifstream` (`ios::in|ios::nocreate|ios::binary`, "fd() != -1" open-success check) if the
  archive isn't loaded or the resource isn't in it. Parses RIFF→WAVE→"fmt "→"data" chunks via
  the private helper below, bulk-copies the fmt chunk's raw bytes and reads the PCM data into
  `*pOut`. **Real parse/format errors are a bare `throw <int-errcode>;`, NOT a call to a
  helper function** (v91 correction — `FUN_00466ce0`, ex-modeled as an opaque
  `Rf_ThrowLoadErrorMaybe(int code)` extern, is really the compiler's own
  RaiseException-based `_CxxThrowException` equivalent: Ghidra's decompile of 0x466ce0 shows
  it copying an 8-dword `ThrowInfo`-shaped template from `DAT_004792c0`, splicing in the 2
  caller-passed pointers, then calling `RaiseException(code, flags, nArgs, &args)` — textbook
  MSVC C++-EH-via-SEH codegen for a thrown POD. Every call site pushes `&<local int>` (the
  thrown value's address) and the FIXED constant `0x47a950` (the compiler-synthesized
  `_ThrowInfo` descriptor for type `int`) — confirmed at all 8 sites in this function via raw
  disasm. `xrefs_to` on 0x466ce0 shows the same shape at 24 total sites across 6+ other
  loader subsystems (bitmap/thumbnail/layout loaders: `LoadMaybe`, `ThumbnailBmp_LoadMaybe`,
  `LayoutSet_LoadIndexFileMaybe`, ...) — every one of those should get the same
  `Rf_ThrowLoadErrorMaybe(code)`→`throw code;` fix once tackled, not just this TU) and IS
  reported to the caller (v92 correction — the outer handler is `catch (int nErr) {
  nReturnCode = nErr; }`, NOT an empty `catch (...) {}`; confirmed via Ghidra's own
  EH-analyzer decompile of the `Catch_00413971` funclet: `*(ebp-0x20) = *(ebp+8); return
  0x413916;`, i.e. the caught error code becomes the function's own return value). The `try`
  itself only wraps the chunk-parsing logic (`Wav_ReadOrFindChunk` calls onward) — the
  RF-archive/file-open resource acquisition above it is NOT inside the user `try` (it only
  needs the separate, automatic `/GX` `new`-alloc protection). A NULL `pOut` is still reported
  via a distinct early `return -1;` before any of this. Sole caller:
  `SoundBankEntry::EnsureLoaded` (0x448d60, see the dedicated `SoundBankEntry` section below).
- **`Wav_ReadOrFindChunk(istream *pStream, int *pOut, int reserved, int mode)`**
  (0x413980, private, only caller is `Wav_ParseAndLoad`) — mode 0: plain 12-byte read (used
  for the RIFF/WAVE header). Mode 0x10: searches forward from the stream's current position
  for an 8-byte `[id][size]` chunk header matching `*pOut`'s id, skipping non-matching chunks
  via `istream::ignore()` (confirmed via the inline `ios.h`/`istream.h` header definitions:
  `ignore(n)` inlines to `lock(); _fGline++; get(NULL,n+1,EOF); unlock();` — matches the raw
  disasm's `EnterCriticalSection`/field-increment/`FUN_00464c70`(=`get`)/`LeaveCriticalSection`
  sequence exactly once the redundant `+1` is removed from the call site, since `ignore()`
  already adds it internally — a real transcription bug caught and fixed this session).
  Modes 0x20/0x40 are a real but unexercised no-op branch (this TU's only caller never passes
  them — likely shared with a different, not-yet-found caller elsewhere). **`// sic:`**: the
  mode-0x10 success path copies 5 dwords from a local `int[5]` chunk-header buffer back into
  the caller, but only writes the first 2 via the 8-byte header read — the other 3 are
  genuinely uninitialized stack garbage, copied faithfully into the caller's locals (harmless:
  the caller never reads them back).
- **Stream-method mapping, confirmed by cross-referencing `toolchain/vc50/INCLUDE`'s real VC5
  headers against the raw disasm** (useful reference for any future TU using these classes):
  `FUN_00464db0`/`(this,off,dir)` = `istream::seekg(streamoff,ios::seek_dir)` (out-of-line,
  not inlined); `FUN_00464e50`/`(this)` = `istream::sync()` (out-of-line, 0 explicit args);
  `FUN_00463810`/`(this,buf,n)` = `istream::read(char*,int)` + separately `gcount()`;
  the vbase-adjusted `*(byte*)(...+8)&4`/`&1` bit-tests = inlined `ios::bad()`/`ios::eof()`
  (both plain inline accessors on the `state` field, vbase-adjusted since `ios` is a virtual
  base of `istream`); `FUN_00463aa0` = `ifstream::open(const char*,int,int)`; `FUN_00463b10`
  = `ifstream::close()`; the scalar-deleting-dtor-shaped virtual calls on stream objects at
  cleanup = plain `delete pStream;` (both `istrstream`/`ifstream` have real virtual dtors via
  their `ios` virtual base). `0xa1` open-mode constant = `ios::binary|ios::nocreate|ios::in`
  (0x80|0x20|0x1).
- **`RFIndex` cross-TU access confirmed**: `DAT_00485600` (used both as `&this` for
  `RFIndex::LoadResource` and, dereferenced, as a `pFile != NULL` "archive is open" flag) is
  the SAME object as `UIResources`(`DAT_004855e8`)`+0x18`'s embedded `RFIndex` — consistent
  with the RF-archive-reader section's existing documentation.

### SoundBankEntry TU (`src/SoundBank.cpp`) — Phase 4's 4th DirectSound-cluster TU — COMPLETE

**Address-contiguous cluster, 0x448990-0x448f2f**: preceded by an unrelated `PostMessageA`
stub (0x448970, ends 0x448990 with no gap), followed by `UiIconListItem`'s ctor (0x448f30, a
different class). All 6 functions transcribed as of v113: 2 ctor overloads (0x448990/0x448a20),
the virtual dtor (0x4489d0, vtable slot 0 — also the auto-generated scalar deleting destructor,
inline body in `src/DSoundChannel.h`), `ResolvePathAndCheckExists` (0x448a70),
`ParseSettingsLine` (0x448c90, vtable slot 1 — was a genuine Ghidra analyzer gap,
`create_function`'d this session), plus `EnsureLoaded`/`Release` (v112).

**Correction to earlier sessions' model (v112):** `WavResource`'s previously-documented
vtable (`0x478278`) and 2 ctor overloads (`0x448990`/`0x448a20`) actually belong to
**`SoundBankEntry`**, not `WavResource` — Ghidra's `WavResource::WavResource`
ctor names were a mis-collision (both ctors were decompiled through the small 0x20-byte
`WavResource` type, which is undersized for what they actually construct: both allocate via
`operator new(0x12C)` = 300 bytes, matching `SoundBankEntry`'s real `sizeof`, not
`WavResource`'s 32). `WavResource` itself remains exactly as previously documented — a
genuinely separate, small POD (vtable + `fmtChunkRaw[0x14]` + `nDataSize` + `pData`) that
`EnsureLoaded` constructs as a local scratch and passes to `Wav_ParseAndLoad`; the two classes
are related by composition (a `SoundBankEntry` owns a transient `WavResource` while
loading), not identity.

**v113 modeling fix (the "double vtable" trap):** once `ResolvePathAndCheckExists`
(0x448a70) and `ParseSettingsLine` (0x448c90, vtable slot 1) were retyped from
`WavResource*` to `SoundBankEntry*` via `set_function_this_type`, transcribing the class's
dtor and `ParseSettingsLine` as real C++ `virtual` methods required REMOVING the
explicit `void *vtable;` field that earlier sessions had modeled directly on the struct —
once the class has a genuine `virtual` method, the compiler auto-inserts its OWN vtable
pointer, and keeping both double-counts, shifting every field access in the WHOLE TU by +4
bytes (this transiently "regressed" the already-matched `EnsureLoaded`/`Release` from
v112 — not a real regression, just the double-vtable bug rippling through the shared header).
Fixed by dropping the explicit field, matching `DSound.h`'s established no-explicit-vtable-field
convention for `virtual`-bearing classes.

- **`SoundBankEntry`** (`sizeof == 0x12C` = 300 bytes, confirmed by 2 independent
  `operator new(0x12C)` sites: `SoundBank_PreloadWavRangeMaybe`/0x446cc0,
  `Sound_PlayOneShotAtPositionMaybe`/0x447a70; polymorphic, vtable `0x478278`) — full field
  layout as modeled in `src/DSoundChannel.h` (Ghidra struct kept in sync). Source no longer
  declares an EXPLICIT `void *vtable;` field (see the v113 fix above) — the compiler's own
  IMPLICIT vtable pointer occupies the same offset 0 a manual field would have, so the REAL
  runtime offsets are unchanged from earlier sessions: `+0x0 vtable (implicit)`, `+0x4
  nSoundId`, `+0x8 bPersistent` (skip auto-unload-at-refcount-0 in `Release`), `+0x9
  bLoaded` (dual-purpose: `EnsureLoaded` success flag AND, earlier in the object's life,
  `ResolvePathAndCheckExists`'s "settings resolved" flag — same field, two different
  lifecycle stages, confirmed via both functions' raw disasm), `+0xc pMasterBuffer`

- **`ResolvePathAndCheckExists()`** (0x448a70, **PARKED, DIFF 317/508**,
  `src/SoundBank.cpp`) — resolves this entry's per-sound settings override

  against the raw disasm; the remaining 317/508 diff is a pure register-allocation/codegen tie-break
  cascade (an elided redundant `strlen` rescan in the `strcpy`+`strcat` sidecar-path build,

- **`ParseSettingsLine(istream *pStream)`** (0x448c90, **byte-exact MATCH**,
  `src/SoundBank.cpp`, vtable slot 1 — was a genuine Ghidra analyzer gap between two already-
  analyzed functions, `create_function`'d this session) — reads consecutive whitespace-
  delimited "Key Value" pairs from `pStream` until eof, updating

  `MaxInstances`/`ResourceReplayDelay`/`Global` keys are present (`Global` takes no value, just

  stream isn't `bad()` — set BEFORE the `eof()` check (confirmed via raw disasm: the original
  uses a comma-expression-shaped side effect, `(uVar2=1, eof-check)`, so a stream that's
  already at eof on entry still returns 1) — a `bad()||eof()` combined check or nesting the
  flag assignment inside the eof branch both compile to a structurally different, non-matching
  shape.
- **`EnsureLoaded()`** (0x448d60, **EFFECTIVE DIFF 8/379**, `src/SoundBank.cpp`) — lazily
  loads this entry's WAV data into a fresh `IDirectSoundBuffer` on first call; every call
  increments `nRefCount` regardless (refcounted cache: a buffer already loaded is a cheap
  refcount-only hit and returns immediately). Builds a `DSBUFFERDESC` (`dwFlags =
  DSBCAPS_CTRLVOLUME|DSBCAPS_CTRLPAN|DSBCAPS_LOCSOFTWARE|DSBCAPS_STATIC` = `0xca`, plus
  `DSBCAPS_GLOBALFOCUS` = `0x8000` when `bGlobalFocus` is set), bails with a hardcoded
  `E_NOTIMPL`-shaped code (`0x80004001`) if the parsed format's `wBitsPerSample < 8` (NOT
  `nBlockAlign`), then `Lock`s the ENTIRE new buffer, `memcpy`s the WAV's PCM bytes
  (`wav.pData`, NOT `wav.fmtChunkRaw`) into it, `Unlock`s, and frees the temporary
  resource-heap PCM buffer. Return value is the standard masked-bool-in-EAX idiom (real
  semantics: plain `bool`).
- **`Release()`** (0x448ee0, **byte-exact MATCH**, `src/SoundBank.cpp`) — releases one
  reference; when the count reaches 0 (and the entry isn't `bPersistent`), `Stop()`s+

  destructor (no vtable reset, no `operator delete` — the `SoundBankEntry` object itself
  survives). Called in the "acquire, play, release" idiom seen in `Sound_PlayOneShotAtPositionMaybe`
  (0x447a70): `new SoundBankEntry(name); if (EnsureLoaded()) { AcquireChannelForSound(...);
  Release(); } delete this;` — confirms `EnsureLoaded`/`Release` are a matched
  acquire/release pair around each play, independent of the object's own lifetime.

## AVI/MCI video

Small, self-contained — splash/boot only (3 `.avi` strings in the whole binary).

**`VideoPlayer`** (vtable `0x4784c4`, single-slot — the adjacent dwords belong to an
unrelated rect/hit-test class, ctor/dtor 0x4544e0/0x4545a0):

```
+0x00  vtable*
+0x04  HWND hwndVideo       (MCIWnd child)
+0x08  int  left, +0x0c top (dest rect, 0)
+0x10  int  right  (hardcoded 0x280=640)
+0x14  int  bottom (hardcoded 0x1e0=480)
+0x18  HWND hwndParent
+0x1c  HINSTANCE hInstance
+0x20  char filename[]      (inline)
```

Ctor `0x454250` (0x524-byte alloc): copies filename, probes existence
(`CreateFileA`+`CloseHandle`), on failure posts app-private msg `0x3b9` ("video failed") to
the parent, else computes the dest rect (`0x425a50` = generic center-rect-in-rect) and calls
`OpenAndPlay` (0x454380): `MCIWndRegisterClass` + `CreateWindowExA("MCIWndClass")`,
`MCIWNDM_OPENA`, `MCIWNDM_PUT_DEST`, `MCIWNDM_GETDEVICEID`, `mciSendCommandA(MCI_PLAY,
MCI_NOTIFY|0x01000000)` — all IDs numerically confirmed against `vfw.h`/`mmsystem.h`. Dtor
`0x454330` (inline `MCI_CLOSE`/`WM_CLOSE` + conditional delete). Call sites: the 3 splash
videos (see SplashWnd) — `0x421084` (`<res>\video\IgSpin.avi`), `0x421188` (ini `[Video]`
intro), `0x421f7d` (`<res>\video\legoSpin.avi`).

## DirectPlay: session and lobby layer

### Provider probing and connection types

- **`DPlay_ProbeAvailableProviders` (0x45eab0):** builds a linked list of available
  connection types (cached at `this+0xd6c`; bails if the live `IDirectPlay4A*` at
  `this+0x1588` is already set) by instantiating + QI + releasing each stock service
  provider. **Type tags, GUID-confirmed** (raw file-byte GUID decode, exact matches):
  **1 = Modem** (`DPlay_ProbeModem` 0x45eec0 — **EXACT, transcribed v434**; the only arm that
  needs more than "can DirectPlay instantiate this provider?", since the modem SP installs fine
  on a machine with no modem attached. After the usual create/QI/release-the-temp bring-up it
  sizes and `GlobalAlloc`/`GlobalLock`s the provider's connection-caps blob
  (`IDirectPlay4::GetConnectionCaps`, vtbl+0x48, called twice — once with a null buffer to get
  the size) and feeds it to `pDPlaySecondary->EnumAddress` (vtbl+0x14) with the standalone
  DPAID-phone-number callback at 0x45fbd0, which copies the phone number into
  `this->sPhoneNumber` (+0xd70). The answer is literally `sPhoneNumber[0] != 0` afterwards —
  `sPhoneNumber[0]` is cleared right before the enumeration so a stale number can't answer for a
  modem that has gone away. Every failure path here is SILENT, unlike `DPlay_InitConnection`'s
  own copy of the same caps dance, which formats and reports each HRESULT — this is a background
  capability probe, not a user-initiated connect), **2 = TCP/IP**
  (`DPSPGUID_TCPIP` = `36E95EE0-8577-11CF-960C-0080C7534E82`), **3 = Serial** (brute-force
  `CreateFileA` COM-port probe), **4 = IPX**
  (`DPSPGUID_IPX` = `685BC400-9D2C-11CF-A9CD-00AA006886E3`). The same tag scheme drives the
  "Select Connection" dialog (resource 0x7d0a, dlgproc 0x461020 → `this+0x518` = 1..4).
  Transcribed v434 (`src/GameNet.cpp`, EFFECTIVE at byte_diff 39 / insns 286/286 — see
  `docs/PARKED.md`). The cache field is now modelled: `GNetManager::pProviderList` (+0xd6c,
  `DPlayProviderNode *`, ex-`pListHead3Maybe` in Ghidra). Node = 8 bytes, `{pNext, nProviderType}`
  with the type stored FIRST and the list pushed newest-first, so the probe order Modem → IPX →
  TCP/IP → Serial comes back out reversed. The probe is one-shot (non-null head returns
  immediately) and refuses to run while a connection is live.
- **`GNetManager::ProbeComPort` (0x45ee60):** the Serial arm's per-port existence test — builds
  `"COM<digit>"` on the stack and `CreateFileA`/`CloseHandle`s it. **Genuinely `inline`** in the
  original: `DPlay_ProbeAvailableProviders` expands it four times
  (`ProbeComPort("1") || … || ProbeComPort("4")` gating the whole Serial probe), while the
  out-of-line COMDAT at 0x45ee60 exists only for the one real call, from the
  `GameNetThreadState` ctor at 0x438c67. That caller is the other half of the story: it stores
  the probe's returned list head into `g_pNetSettings+0x10` and then runs its own `i = 0..3` loop
  building the digit string as `'0' + i` and writing each result byte into
  `g_pNetSettings->bComPortAvailableMaybe[i]` — i.e. NetSettings' "which COM ports exist" array
  is populated by this exact helper. Both halves landed v518: the ctor (0x438bc0) is transcribed
  in `src/GameNet.cpp` (EFFECTIVE park, one COM-loop register rotation) bracketed in
  `#pragma inline_depth(0)`/`(8)` so its ProbeComPort calls stay real `call`s — which is also
  what makes the TU EMIT the out-of-line COMDAT, and 0x45ee60 (93 B) fell out EXACT for free as
  predicted. The body therefore moved out of `src/GNetManager.h` (now declared-only there) to an
  out-of-class `inline` definition mid-`src/GameNet.cpp`, between the two consumers (VC5 inlines
  with whole-TU visibility, so the ctor alone can't be shielded by placement).
- **`GNetManager::CreateLobby` (0x45e4b0, ex-`DPlayLobby_Init`) — EXACT, transcribed v434.** The
  real ctor body (0x45e490 is a 26-byte forwarder that does nothing but call it, and whose second
  argument is the parent **HWND**, not a flags word as a prior guess had it — both call sites pass
  0). Zero/default-inits every scalar field, then brings up the DirectPlay **lobby**:
  `DirectPlayLobbyCreateA` → `QueryInterface(IID_IDirectPlayLobby3A)` into `pDPlaySecondary` →
  Release the transient object. **This confirms what `pDPlaySecondary` is**: the IID at 0x479048
  decodes from the raw .rdata bytes to `{2DB72491-652C-11D1-A7A8-0000F803ABFC}` =
  `IID_IDirectPlayLobby3A`, promoting the "IDirectPlayLobby3-shaped" guess to a fact (its
  `EnumAddress` @vtbl+0x14 and `CreateCompoundAddress` @vtbl+0x38 both line up). NOT DirectSound
  init — an early misattribution, long corrected; that is `DSound_InitDeviceAndChannelPool`
  (0x412c50). Non-obvious defaults set here: `bAllowHostMigration` and
  `bShowErrorMessageBoxMaybe` start **TRUE** (so DirectPlay errors DO pop message boxes out of the
  box) and `nSendThrottleQueueDepth` starts at **10**. `sic:` both HRESULTs are stored to
  `hrLastResult` and then ignored — a failed lobby create is only noticed much later, when
  `DPlay_InitConnection` dereferences the null `pDPlaySecondary`; and `sConnectParam` is never
  cleared here (only `DPlay_TeardownConnection` clears it), so it starts life as heap garbage.
- **`~GNetManager` (0x45e5a0) — EXACT, transcribed v434.** Non-virtual, called directly by
  `delete`. `DPlay_TeardownConnection`, release `pDPlaySecondary`, free the cached
  reliable-message payload, then drain **all four** owned lists. The object turns out to own
  THREE separate found-session-shaped lists (+0xd60 `pListHead0Maybe`, +0xd64 `pListHead1`, +0xd68
  `pListHead2Maybe`) plus `pProviderList` (+0xd6c) — and only `pListHead1`'s nodes carry HGLOBAL
  session-desc memory, which is why only that drain does the GlobalHandle/GlobalUnlock/GlobalFree
  dance. That asymmetry is the clearest signal the three lists have different producers;
  `DPlay_BuildOtherSessionsList`'s "only pNext/pszName populated" list matches the cheap shape.
- **`DPlay_TeardownConnection` (0x45fc30) — EXACT, transcribed v434.** `CancelMessage(0,0)`
  (IDirectPlay4 vtbl+0xcc) + `Close` (vtbl+0x10) + `Release`, both found-session lists drained,
  and the session identity/protocol scratch reset — clearing only the FIRST BYTE of each string
  field, the usual "empty C string" idiom.
- **`DPlay_ReportNetworkError` (0x460ea0) — EXACT, transcribed v434.** The shared error sink every
  DirectPlay failure path routes through. Composes
  `"<LoadStringA(nPrefixResId)>\r\r<pszMessage>"` (either half optional) into a `char[0x200]`,
  records it in `sLastErrorText` (+0x945) **regardless of how or whether it is then displayed**,
  and then EITHER calls the `pfnErrorTextHookMaybe` hook (+0x940, `__cdecl void(char *)`) with the
  text and returns 0, OR — only when `bShowErrorMessageBoxMaybe` (+0x944) is set — shows a
  MB_TOPMOST `MessageBoxA` captioned with resource string 0x7d06. With neither, it is silent.
  The hook REPLACES the message box rather than supplementing it; no setter for it has surfaced.
- **`DPlay_SelectConnectionDlgProc` (0x461020) — EXACT, transcribed v434.** The radio-button ids
  map to provider tags **out of id order**: 0x7d32→4 (IPX, and the one pre-checked), 0x7d33→2
  (TCP/IP), 0x7d34→1 (Modem), 0x7d35→3 (Serial). The Serial arm is deliberately asymmetric — its
  `EndDialog(hDlg, 1)` / `return 1` runs whether or not any button was checked, so dismissing the
  dialog with nothing selected still reports success and leaves `nProtocol` at its previous value.
  `sic:` the WM_INITDIALOG arm returns FALSE, so Windows keeps its own default input focus.

### `NetSettings` — persisted network settings

Singleton `g_pNetSettings` (`DAT_004fd3a8`), 0xb0 bytes, ctor `0x440c60` (bootstrap-
allocated). **Everything past the vtable is a flat 0xac-byte blob** serialized to/from
`NetSettings.dat`: `LoadOrInitFromDisk` (0x440d00; valid iff the first word reads the magic
`0x6a`, else reset to ctor defaults and write back), `SaveToDisk` (0x440ea0; the exact
inverse `WriteFile`, called whenever settings change). Fields: `magicMaybe` (0x6a),
`bValidSaveLoadedMaybe`, `bSkipSetupWizardMaybe` (**default 1 — out of the box, Loco skips
the multiplayer wizard entirely**; cleared only by `NetSetupWnd::OnLButtonUp`'s
Connect-Online branch), `bUseSecondaryRememberedChoice`, two remembered-choice pairs
`bRememberedApplSetupValidPrimary/SecondaryMaybe` + `rememberedProtocolPrimary/
SecondaryMaybe` (**domain = the full provider tag set 1–4** — Modem/TCP/Serial/IPX; the
NetSetup UI only ever tests 2/4 because only those two are exposed as toggle buttons),
`nTickSleepMs` (+0xc, the net thread's `Sleep` interval), `Unk0x10` (provider linked-list
head, populated from the probe by the GameNetThreadState ctor), `bComPortAvailableMaybe[0..3]` (+0x14, "which COM
ports exist" cache — the ctor probes `CreateFileA("COM0".."COM3")`). The two remembered-choice
pairs are DUPLICATED for primary (+0x28, used when not hosting and connectionMode!=1) and
secondary (+0x1c, used when hosting): `nRememberedCustomValueSecondary` (+0x20, int,
itoa'd when secondary==3), `szRememberedAddrPrimary`/`szRememberedAddrPrimaryAlt`
(+0x2c/+0x6c, two 0x40-byte connection-address string buffers, selected by primary==1/2) /
`nRememberedCustomValuePrimary` (+0xac, int, itoa'd when primary==3) — all confirmed and
byte-matched EXACT by `GameNetThreadState::DPlay_PrepareInternetConnection` (0x43a760,
v269, `src/GameNet.cpp`; was `Unk0x20`/`Unk0x2c`/`Unk0x6c`/`Unk0xac` placeholders, widened from
1-byte to their real sizes and renamed). **`0x467ea0` IS the CRT's own `_itoa`, and `0x467ee0`
its `xtoa` helper (CONFIRMED v401, closing a long-standing speculative-name item).** The body is
verbatim the CRT source: `_itoa` forwards to `xtoa(val, buf, radix, is_neg)` with
`is_neg = (radix == 10 && value < 0)`. The old placeholder name `Itoa10Signed` is retired
repo-wide; call sites now use `_itoa` from `<stdlib.h>` and need no declaration of their own
(measured: retiring the `src/GameNet.h` declaration moved no TU's byte count).

### `DPlaySessionMgr` — session/lobby/roster manager
**Provider slots are reached through a bounds-guarded inline accessor, not a raw subscript.**
The real source has an in-class (⇒ implicitly inline) member
`DPlaySessionMgrProviderSlot *ProviderSlotAt(int i) { return i >= 0 ? &aProviderSlots[i] : 0; }`.
It leaves no function in the binary — it inlines into every caller as the `jl → (ptr = NULL)`
guard in front of each `lea base + i*0x4c + 0x518`, and if-converts to a branchless
`setl; dec; and` inside loops. That guard is dead in practice (every index is a masked byte or a
loop counter), which is why it was misfiled as an intrinsic codegen tie-break for ~100 sessions
before v360. Callers do NOT uniformly null-check the result: `FindTrainPlacementResult` and
`RemoveTrainPlacementResult` check their first two lookups and dereference straight through on
the third, and `SetTrainPlacementResult` checks only its create path — each of those is an
observable byte-level fact, so read the call site's disasm rather than assuming consistency.
Use the accessor for any new `aProviderSlots` ADDRESS-taking site; plain
`aProviderSlots[i].field` subscripting stays correct where the original emits no guard (e.g.
`SetMode` 0x43d2b0, and the per-slot reset loops).


Singleton `g_pDPlaySessionMgr` (0x804 bytes, ctor 0x43d0a0, allocated at bootstrap site 0x406c9d).
**Do not confuse with `g_pNetManager`/`GNetManager` (`DAT_0048525c`)** — a prior mislabel;
the two are distinct objects, and `DAT_004fd3a4` (the event-queue this-ptr) is yet another
global. `src/DPlaySessionMgr.h`'s shared `DPlaySessionMgr` class view now also mirrors
`aProviderSlots[9]`/`selectedProviderIndex` (added for `EditCardWnd::
BuildPlayerRosterList`, `src/EditCardWnd.cpp`) alongside its existing `connectionMode`
and the 4 heading-dispatch wrappers — extend that struct in place for new callers rather than
declaring a fresh per-TU local view (this project's universal convention, per CLAUDE.md's
"never duplicate a struct across TUs" rule — `UIResources`/`src/UIResources.h` was
the last holdout with independent per-TU local copies, consolidated 2026-07-17).
Fields: `field_0x8` +0x8 (set to 9 by `ResetProviders`; copied into a send-node's
`bReliable` slot by `GameNet_PostResetConnection`), `nProviderSlotsPerRow` +0xc and
`nProviderSlotRows` +0x10 (the roster grid width/height, both set to 3 by `ResetProviders`;
`HasProviderSlotRoomInHeading` divides `selectedProviderIndex` by these to get a
row/col), `sessionName` +0x14 (reset to `"Default"`),
`aProviderSlots[9]` +0x518 (stride 0x4c; 9 = DPlay max players), a second 0x4c-stride array
+0x54e(?), `connectionMode` +0x7c4 (1 = network game active, 2 = "Layouts" world type,
3 = idle), `bConnectPendingMaybe` +0x7c8, `pSelectedProvider` +0x7cc,
`selectedProviderIndex` +0x7d0, `searchProviderId` +0x7d4, `queueSourceId`
+0x7d8, `pPendingTrainQueueHead` +0x7e0, `playerCountMaybe` +0x7e8, `nDispatchTick`
+0x7ec, `stateTimeoutMs` +0x7f0, `rosterBroadcastTickMaybe` +0x7f4, `retryCountMaybe`
+0x7f8, `timeoutMsMaybe` +0x7fc.

**Byte-matched 2026-07-18 (v230), `src/DPlaySessionMgr.cpp`:** `ResolveIdToSlot` (0x43d230,
linear scan of `aProviderSlots[i].providerId`, returns the index or -1) and
`HasProviderSlotRoomInHeading`/src `Test` (0x43de30, the real body behind the 4 heading
wrappers: `heading/40` → axis 0/2/4/6 = up/right/down/left, tests whether the grid cell at
`selectedProviderIndex` has a neighbour in that direction; returns a bare-`al` bool). Both are
context-insensitive leaves; `Test` needed the `heading/40` switch discriminant hoisted ahead
of the row/col divide to match.

**Byte-matched 2026-07-19 (v231), `src/DPlaySessionMgr.cpp`:** `GetSelectedProvider`
(0x43d210, 19B — returns `pSelectedProvider` iff `connectionMode == 2`, else NULL) and
`SetMode` (0x43d2b0, 136B code + a 4-entry jump table — the mode-transition dispatcher above).
`SetMode` is a jump-table `switch(mode)` (0..3, default clamps `connectionMode` to 3); the case
labels must be **declared in jump-table target-address order** (case 2 @0x2d1 < case 1 @0x31c <
default @0x32a < empty cases 0/3 @0x334), not numeric order, or the case bodies land in the
wrong physical layout (Yoda #16). Its case-2 provider scan also needed the two found-branch
assignments emitted `pSelectedProvider = &aProviderSlots[i]; selectedProviderIndex = i;`
(pointer first) to keep the address-computation accumulator in `edx` instead of reusing `eax`.
New fields modeled in `src/DPlaySessionMgr.h`: `bConnectPendingMaybe` +0x7c8, split from the
old `pad0x7c8` blob; `pSelectedProvider` +0x7cc typed `DPlaySessionMgrProviderSlot*`;
`searchProviderId` +0x7d4; `stateTimeoutMs` +0x7f0.

**Byte-matched 2026-07-19 (v233), `src/DPlaySessionMgr.cpp`:** the **ctor** `DPlaySessionMgr()`
(0x43d0a0, 106B) and the compiler-generated **scalar deleting destructor** `??_GDPlaySessionMgr`
(0x43d110, 30B). Modeled by making the src class polymorphic with a single `virtual
~DPlaySessionMgr()` — the compiler then synthesizes both the ctor's `mov [this],&vtbl` prologue
store AND the ??_G COMDAT as byproducts (the real dtor body @0x43dc30 stays declared-only, so
??_G calls it as an external — this compiles cleanly to `.obj` and matches without transcribing
the 396-byte dtor). The ctor stores its vtable directly, zeroes the connection state machine
(connectionMode=3 idle, searchProviderId=0, retryCount=0xf, timeoutMs=0x960), and calls
`ResetProviders(1)` first. Also renamed the src class `DPlaySessionMgrPartial` → `DPlaySessionMgr`
to match Ghidra, cleared the `// TODO: sync` debt on the 6 existing methods (`ResolveIdToSlot`
moved into the `DPlaySessionMgr` Ghidra namespace, `Test` renamed to its real Ghidra name
`HasProviderSlotRoomInHeading`), and extended the struct tail with the ctor's fields
(field_0x4/0x7d8/0x7dc, pPendingTrainQueueHead +0x7e0, field_0x7e4, playerCountMaybe +0x7e8,
nDispatchTick +0x7ec, rosterBroadcastTickMaybe +0x7f4, retryCountMaybe +0x7f8, timeoutMsMaybe
+0x7fc, field_0x800; sizeof 0x804). `field_0x8` was `int field_0x8` @+0x8 already.

**`DPlaySessionMgr` is polymorphic with its OWN 16-slot vtable at `0x4781c8`, but is NOT a
`WindowBase` subclass** (an earlier note claimed it was — refuted v233). Two proofs: (1) the ctor
stores its vtable with **no base-ctor call** — a standalone-polymorphic class model byte-matches
it exactly; (2) a slot-by-slot vtable compare against `WindowBase` (`0x477c30`) shows the shared
method BODIES (`0x425fd0`, `0x426020`, `0x425b70`, `0x426140`, and the `DefWindowProcStub`
`0x422ea0`) appear in DPlaySessionMgr's table too but at **shifted slot offsets** (WindowBase
slot 3/4/6/10/11 → DPlaySessionMgr slot 5/6/8/12/15), which single inheritance never produces
(it preserves base slot offsets). So DPlaySessionMgr merely reuses some shared dispatch/stub
helper bodies, not WindowBase's vtable layout — model it standalone. Slot 0 = the scalar dtor
`0x43d110`; slots 1-4 own overrides (0x440cc0/0x440f80/0x441a00/0x441870); remaining slots a mix
of own methods and the shared helper bodies. The **real dtor `~DPlaySessionMgr` (0x43dc30, 396B)
is byte-matched (v234)**. It has a PLAIN prologue (no SEH) — `0x43dbb4` is an unrelated SEH
funclet belonging to `LayoutSet_InitFromConfigFileMaybe`, not the dtor's. Algorithm: re-stamp the
vtable, then under `g_pGameNetMsgQueueLock` (`0x4fd394`, Lock/Unlock = 0x449410/0x449420)
drain `g_pNetMsgLocalQueueHead` (`0x4fd3a0`) node-by-node; for each node with a non-null
payload a jump-table `switch(node->type)` frees the payload by opcode — **case 2** payload is its
own owned sub-list (`NetMsgType2PayloadNode`: next @+0, sub-payload @+8, each `operator delete`d);
**cases 0xf/0x11** `delete` the *send* queue's pending object (`g_pNetMsgSendQueueHead`
[`0x4fd39c`] `->pPayload`, virtual scalar-deleting dtor); **cases 0x15/0x17** `HeapFree`; **default**
`operator delete(payload)` — then `operator delete(node)`. After unlock it `delete`s both
polymorphic queued-node lists (`field_0x7dc` and `pPendingTrainQueueHead`, chained @node+0x70,
freed via vtbl[0](1)), then walks `aProviderSlots[9]` freeing each slot's results-chain (+0x38,
next @node+0x10) and layout blob (+0x44). Byte-match note: the case-2 sub-list `while` derives its
head from a **fresh `g_pNetMsgLocalQueueHead->pPayload` read** (CSE'd to the same load as the
outer null-check, but source-level distinct so /O2 keeps the loop's top guard instead of eliding
it as provably-non-null — a plain `p = payload;` would drop the guard and mis-match by 2 insns).

**Byte-matched 2026-07-19 (v236), `src/DPlaySessionMgr.cpp` — LayoutNet producers:**
`LayoutNet_RequestLayoutList` (0x43d620, 148B, **EXACT**) and `LayoutNet_
ReplyWithStoredLayoutMaybe` (0x43d520, 253B, **EFFECTIVE**, DIFF ~42B). Both are real
`__thiscall DPlaySessionMgr` methods with a `LayoutNet_` role-prefix name (this-typed into the
`DPlaySessionMgr` namespace; the `LayoutNet` Ghidra namespace they sat in was a mislabel — they
take `this` in ECX, not a stack ptr). RequestLayoutList broadcasts a 6-byte opcode-0x3f8 message
(`LayoutReqWireMsg`: `wOpcode` +0, `bProviderIndex` +4 = `(byte)selectedProviderIndex`) via
send-queue type 6, then a bare type-0x19 no-payload command. **Exact-match lever:** the byte
store `pMsg->bProviderIndex = selectedProviderIndex` must materialize the int in a full
32-bit register first (`mov eax,[this+0x7d0]; mov [pMsg+4],al`) — any direct/cast narrowing
byte-loads instead; a `unsigned int idx = selectedProviderIndex;` temp read AFTER the opcode
store (so it isn't hoisted) reproduces the dword load. ReplyWithStoredLayout answers a peer's
layout request: if connected + the selected slot has a stored layout blob, it packs the blob into
an opcode-0x3f9 `LayoutBitmapWireMsg` (0x14-byte header: `wOpcode` +0, `wCols`/`wRows` +6/+8 from
the slot's +0x40/+0x42, `unkDword2Maybe` +0xc from slot +0x48, `nPixelCount` +0x10 = cols*rows,
then the 8bpp bitmap bytes at +0x14; buffer `::operator new(nLayoutDataSize + 0x28)`) and
sends it reliably; else it posts a bare type-0x1b "no layout" node to the LOCAL queue. The
opening slot select is an **inlined `GetSelectedProvider`** (its native `if (mode != 2)`
test, so the zero/false case is the fall-through — a `(mode != 2) ? 0 : pSelectedProvider`
ternary matches; `== 2` inverts the branch). Residual is a single intrinsic ax↔cx allocator swap
on the cols/rows shorts that cascades (see `docs/PARKED.md`). The 0x3f9 wire header is **shared**
with the not-yet-transcribed `LayoutNet_SendCurrentLayoutBitmap` (0x43d350). Also this
session: **`GameNetMsgQueue_EnqueueOrProcessLocalNodeMaybe` (0x43f140)** — the local-queue
enqueue, a `this`-ignored `__thiscall` (all ~35 call sites load `ecx=g_pDPlaySessionMgr` before the
call though the body never reads `this`); its Ghidra convention was corrected `__stdcall`→
`__thiscall`, and it's declared as a `DPlaySessionMgr` method so `g_pDPlaySessionMgr->…(node)`
reproduces the ecx-load + call.

**Byte-matched 2026-07-19 (v237), `src/DPlaySessionMgr.cpp` — LayoutNet/LayoutSet cluster
finished:** `LayoutSet_LoadSlotBitmap` (0x43d6c0, 344B, **EXACT**) and
`LayoutNet_SendCurrentLayoutBitmap` (0x43d350, 456B, **EFFECTIVE**, DIFF ~227B). Both are real
`__thiscall DPlaySessionMgr` methods (this-typed out of the mislabel `LayoutNet`/`LayoutSet`
Ghidra namespaces). **Send** snapshots the live board into a `new LocoBitmap()` (rendered by
`WorldBoardMaybe::CaptureBoardToBitmap(&g_WorldBoard, pBitmap, 0)` — 0x457080, board→raw-bitmap
capture), packs it into an opcode-0x3f9 `LayoutBitmapWireMsg`, caches a private copy in the local
provider slot (`aProviderSlots[selectedProviderIndex]`: `pLayoutData` +0x44 = `operator
new(pixelCount)` blob, `nLayoutDataSize` +0x3c, `unkDword1Maybe`/cols|rows dword +0x40,
`unkDword2Maybe` +0x48 = selected slot's own +0x48 **plus 1**), and sends it reliably. The
`new LocoBitmap()` triggers the `/GX` automatic new-alloc SEH scaffolding (LocoBitmap has a
non-trivial ctor), not a user try/catch; it's a raw pointer `delete`d explicitly at the end
(vtbl[0](1)). Residual = the same intrinsic ax/cx cols/rows swap as Reply (`docs/PARKED.md`);
**REFUTED**: placing Send (Reply's real .obj predecessor) before Reply did NOT fix Reply's swap.
New src-only detail: `LayoutBitmapWireMsg` +0x6 modeled as a `union { unsigned int
dwColsRows; struct { short wCols, wRows; }; }` (byte-packed `#pragma pack(1)`) — Send writes
the two shorts then re-reads them as one dword (`mov ecx,[msg+6]`) to stash cols|rows into the
slot's +0x40.  **LoadSlot** loads a slot's saved layout from disk: frees any cached blob + zeros
the slot's layout fields, and if `strlen(slot.sLongName) != 0` (the layout filename lives in the
slot's `sLongName` +0x12) builds `"%sLayouts\%s"` (fmt 0x47eb0c, prefix `g_pInstallPathPrefix`
0x4a99c8 already ends in `\`) via `wsprintfA` into a 1284-byte stack buffer, decodes it through a
temporary `ThumbnailBmp` (`ThumbnailBmp_LoadMaybe` 0x447ba0), and on success copies the decoded
dims+pixels back into the slot. **Two exact-match levers:** (1) DIRECT `aProviderSlots[slotIndex]
.field` subscripting throughout, NOT a hoisted `pSlot` pointer — reproduces /O2's per-field
anchors, notably the `(slotIndex+0x12)*0x4c` index folding for the +0x40 field (0x558 == 0x12*0x4c);
a hoisted pointer anchored at `&aProviderSlots[i]` mis-anchors every access (138715→16670 once
switched). (2) `wLayoutCols`/`wLayoutRows` (+0x40/+0x42) are **signed** `short` — LoadSlot
sign-extends cols (`movsx`) in the cols*rows product. **ThumbnailBmp fields pinned** (byte-match
confirmed, now in the new shared `src/ThumbnailBmp.h`): `wWidth` +0xb2, `wHeight` +0xb4, `pPixels`
+0x1c4 (the decoded 8bpp buffer; the pixel-pointer offset was byte-match-verified — an off-by-4
guess produced the single residual byte). `ThumbnailBmp` (472B) was extracted from `src/
WidgetPicker.h` into `src/ThumbnailBmp.h` now that a 2nd TU uses it (WidgetPicker still 4/12,
no regression); it stays opaque (`void* this`) in Ghidra.

**`DPlaySessionMgrProviderSlot`** (0x4c, **byte-packed** — `dwTailAliasMaybe` sits at the
2-unaligned +0x32, so no compiler padding; see `src/DPlaySessionMgr.h`): `providerId` +0x0,
`bDirtyMaybe` +0x4, then the +0x5..+0x35 span (**split 2026-07-18** from a single
`sAddressOrName[49]` blob into its three real sub-fields, confirmed by the roster pack/unpack/
copy helpers below touching each separately): `sAddressOrName` +0x5 char[13] (short/display
name — the one `BuildPlayerRosterList` copies), `sLongName` +0x12 char[32] (long name/address),
`dwTailAliasMaybe` +0x32 dword (the "last 4 bytes" tail alias `ResetProviders` overwrites with
board dims — see Bonus finding below), `bEnabled` +0x36, `bUnk0x37` (1 byte, alignment
pad — confirmed genuinely never accessed anywhere in a full-`.text` objdump sweep),
`pResultsChainHead` +0x38 (**RESOLVED 2026-07-12**, was the "2 unexplained byte gaps"; a
`GameNetRosterResultNode *` (typed v242). Head of a per-slot linked list of roster/result nodes.
`GameNetRosterResultNode` (0x14 bytes, modeled v242): `trainId`+0x0, `posX`+0x4, `posY`+0x8,
`bOwnerAMaybe`+0xc, `bSlotKeyMaybe`+0xd (the slot the node is filed under = ownerB), `pNext`+0x10.
Managed by the placement-result group (Find/Set/Remove @ 0x440750/0x440610/0x4404c0, all thiscall
`DPlaySessionMgr` methods, transcribed v242 EFFECTIVE — the dead signed-index guard on
`&aProviderSlots[idx]` blocks EXACT, see docs/PARKED.md). Torn down node-by-node in both
`ResetProviders`'s and `~DPlaySessionMgr`'s per-slot reset loops, walked and serialized 8-bytes-per-node
into msg `0x3f6` by `GameNet_BroadcastRosterTick`), `nLayoutDataSize` +0x3c, `unkDword1Maybe`
+0x40 (**a byte-level alias like `dwTailAliasMaybe`, CORRECTED 2026-07-19 — the old "RESOLVED
2026-07-12: genuinely one dword, the 2×16-bit zero-stores are codegen noise" claim was REFUTED
by the `ResetProviders` byte-match**: a single `unsigned int = 0` compiles to ONE dword store,
one instruction short of the original's TWO 16-bit zero-stores, so +0x40 really is two logical
16-bit fields on the reset path. The wire producer (`GameNetManager_HandleQueuedEvent`
case `0x16`, wire offset +6) still reads/writes the SAME 4 bytes as one dword — so `src/
DPlaySessionMgr.h` models +0x40 as a `union { unsigned int unkDword1Maybe; struct { unsigned
short wLayoutCols, wLayoutRows; }; }`, exactly the `dwTailAliasMaybe` pattern. Ghidra
keeps the dword `unkDword1Maybe` view, matching the +0x32 precedent — a union can't be modeled
inline. **The two 16-bit halves are the stored layout bitmap's width/height** (identified v236 —
`LayoutNet_ReplyWithStoredLayout` reads +0x40/+0x42 as the `wCols`/`wRows` of the 0x3f9
layout-bitmap wire message and multiplies them for the pixel/byte count), renamed from
`wUnk0x40`/`wUnk0x42`), `pLayoutData` +0x44,
`unkDword2Maybe` +0x48 (same producer, wire offset +0xc; a genuine single dword — its lone
32-bit zero-store in `ResetProviders` byte-matches as `unsigned int`). **Bonus finding:**
`ResetProviders`'s per-slot reset loop overwrites the *first 4 bytes* of the `dwTailAliasMaybe`
span (absolute +0x32–0x35) with `g_WorldBoard.wCols`/`wRows` (the board grid dims at
WorldBoard +0x3e/+0x40) as two 16-bit stores — a confirmed intentional overlap (the tail-alias
dword's bytes double as packed board-size metadata on reset), not a bug; modeled as the
`{wCols, wRows}` arm of the +0x32 union.

Methods: `SetMode` (0x43d2b0 — mode-transition dispatcher; case 2 searches the provider
slots for `searchProviderId`; case 1 arms a 500ms timeout; default resets to idle 3),
`ResetProviders` (0x43d130 — **BYTE-MATCHED v235**; names the session "Default", sets the 3×3

blob); `bInit == 0` = re-reset path that frees each slot's result chain node-by-node + layout

`slot` pointer, gives the original's esi-anchored-at-slot+0x38 induction base; and
`pLayoutData = 0` must live inside both branches (cross-jumped to one shared store) so an
already-null slot skips the redundant zero-store),

consumer dispatcher over the command queue at `DAT_004fd3a4`, opcodes 2,3,4,5,9,0xb,0xc,0xf,

slots; case 0x16 receives a layout blob into a slot — the receive side of layout sharing;

layout recovered from the raw jump table [9/4/2/0xb/0xc/5/3/0xf/0x11/{0x12,0x15,0x17}/0x13/0x14/
0x16/0x1b/0x18/0x1a/0x1c]. Case 2 drains a `NetMsgType2PayloadNode` sub-list; case 3 snapshots
`GameNetThreadState::dpidCurrentPlayer`+0x10 into `queueSourceId`+0x7d8 and strcpy's the local

by name when providerId==-1 — then, if it's not already the target slot, copy its name/id/owner-pair

### Connection establishment

- **`GNetManager::DPlay_InitConnection` (0x45f390, ex-doc-name `DPlay_EstablishConnection` —
  renamed to match the current Ghidra/`src/` name; also the object literally referred to as
  "0x45f390" throughout the rest of this section)** — the real connection routine. **Transcribed
  2026-07-20 (v280), match-fixed 2026-07-20 (v281), `src/GameNet.cpp`, PARTIAL (compiles clean,
  idiom+Ghidra-sync lint clean; `asmscore.py --len 2076` total score down to 1426710 from v280's
  2173791 via 4 structural fixes — both protocol-dispatch switches fused into the original's
  single bounds-check+jump-table shape, a genuine COM-reference-leak engine bug found and fixed
  (see below), an unsigned Serial-port comparison, and per-case (not shared) `elems[0]` setup;
  this is by far the largest and most COM-heavy function in the codebase, remaining residual is
  register-swap/block-layout noise already established as intrinsic elsewhere — see
  `docs/PARKED.md`).**
  - `nProtocol==0`: shows the "Select Connection" dialog (resource 0x7d0a,
    `DPlay::DPlay_SelectConnectionDlgProc`/0x461020 — its radio buttons 0x7d32/33/34/35 set
    `nProtocol` to 4/2/1/3 respectively, **closing the long-standing "setter not yet
    identified" question**); returns 0 if cancelled. `nProtocol!=0`: sets `nProtocol =
    nProtocol` directly, truncate-copies `pszSessionName` into the newly-carved
    `sConnectParam[0x400]` (+0x51c, no length cap) and `nUnk3` (the .ini Port) into
    `wPortOrExt` (+0x91c).
  - `nProtocol` **is the DirectPlay protocol tag: 1=Modem, 2=TCP/IP, 3=Serial, 4=IPX**
    (ground-truthed via the function's own SP-GUID jump table, a direct array index — no
    ambiguity). Bounds-checked to `[1,4]` (else return 0), then does the classic 2-step
    DirectPlay bring-up: `DirectPlayCreate(&guidSp, &pTempDPlayIface, 0)` (guidSp a LOCAL
    value-copy of the per-protocol `DPSPGUID_*` — NOT a pointer to the global, a real structural
    lever confirmed this session) → `QueryInterface(IID_IDirectPlay4, &pDirectPlay4)` →
    `Release` the temp object.
  - Builds a per-protocol `DPCompoundAddressElement` array (element0 always
    `DPAID_ServiceProvider` + `&g_guidDPSP<Protocol>Maybe`, referencing the GLOBAL's address
    directly, not the local `guidSp` copy — confirmed via raw disasm each of the 4 protocol
    cases independently sets ALL THREE of `elems[0].guidDataType`/`dwDataSize`/`lpData` from
    scratch, redundantly reloading the same `DPAID_ServiceProvider` GUID 4 times rather than
    sharing one assignment before the switch — not DRY, but faithful to the original): Modem
    adds a phone-number + device-
    name pair extracted via a GetCaps-shaped `GlobalAlloc`/`GlobalLock` dance (vtbl+0x48, exact
    method name unconfirmed) and an `EnumAddress`-shaped callback (`pDPlaySecondary`
    vtbl+0x14, callback body at 0x45fbd0 — an already-compiled standalone helper, not
    transcribed, referenced only by address); TCP/IP adds a `DPAID_INet` address element
    (`sConnectParam`) plus an optional port element (`wPortOrExt`) when nonzero;
    Serial adds an optional COM-port-settings element (new `SerialPortSettings` struct,
    +0x1570: port number via `atoi(sConnectParam)` clamped `[1,4]`, fixed 9600 baud) only
    when `sConnectParam` is non-empty; IPX adds nothing else. Calls
    `pDPlaySecondary->CreateCompoundAddress(elements, nElements, addrBuf, &dwAddrSize)`
    (`pDPlaySecondary` +0x15e0, a SEPARATE IDirectPlayLobby3-shaped COM object created

## GameNet: gameplay sync layer

The gameplay-data sync layer above raw DirectPlay. Callers of `DPlay_SendMessage` cluster in
`0x4386xx`–`0x43cxxx` — likely one "gameplay net-sync" TU, separate from the setup/lobby TUs
near `0x45e000`–`0x461000`.

### Network thread

Spawn chain: `FUN_00422820` (bootstrap; allocates the 0x38-byte thread state) →
`ThreadWrapper::Thread_Start` (0x461790) → `_beginthreadex` (0x468870, renamed/named v73 —
CRT `_beginthreadex`, `calloc`s a `_tiddata`-shaped context via `calloc`/0x46f6d0, also renamed
v73) → `CreateThread` → `Thread::Thread_TrampolineProc` (0x461890) →
**`GameNetThread_TickLoop`** (0x439240, **transcribed v262 — EFFECTIVE**, `src/GameNet.cpp`) —
**tick-driven, not message-pump-driven**: a bare `do{}while(true)` with
`Sleep(g_pNetSettings->nTickSleepMs)` (`NetSettings`+0xc). Each tick: if
`g_pNetManager && g_pNetManager->bSessionJoined` calls `GameNet_DispatchMessage`;
drains the local command queue via `GameNet_ProcessLocalCommand` (0x439550, opcodes 0–0x19 —
enqueued by other threads e.g. UI, a distinct mechanism from network opcodes) — but if a dispatch
went reentrant (`bDispatchBusyMaybe`), instead flushes+disposes the whole send queue (type-0xe/0x10
payloads via virtual dtor, else raw `operator delete`) and EXITS the thread. Otherwise every
`nTrainAdvanceIntervalMaybe` (default 0x14) ticks runs `TrainNet_AdvanceLocalTrainSteps` (no sleep
that tick); other ticks pump the pending outbound file transfer (if `pOutboundTransfersMaybe`), age
each active train's hand-off timer (`--PeerTrainNode.wHeading`; on expiry tear down the session
+ drain the peer list — only when `connectionMode==1`), then Sleep. Residual = 3 redundant
null-checks the original keeps but our cl folds (see docs/PARKED.md); register roles + Sleep-IAT
hoist into ebp all match.

**`GameNetThreadState`** (0x38 bytes; the ctor is `GameNetThreadState::GameNetThreadState` 0x438bc0, transcribed v518 EFFECTIVE, which
also populates `NetSettings.Unk0x10` from the provider probe; created by
`SplashWnd::StartGameNetThread` 0x422820 as a plain `new GameNetThreadState(hInstance,
hwndOwner)`, sourced from the splash window's own `WindowBase` fields). **The holding global is
`g_pGameNetThreadState` (0x4fd3a4) itself** — the manager and the send-queue context are one
heap allocation. **v378 merged the second model:** `src/GameNetMsgQueue.h` used to carry a
separate `class GameNetMsgQueue` over the same object (with `bDiscardMessages`@0xd ==
`bShutdownRequestedMaybe`@0xd and `nQueueSourceId`@0x10 == `dpidCurrentPlayer`@0x10), which was
both a never-duplicate-a-struct violation and a latent symbol bug — MSVC mangles a global's C++
type into its name, so the two `extern` declarations named DIFFERENT symbols. The class now lives
alone in `src/GameNetThreadState.h` (split out of `src/GameNet.h` so consumers that only POST to
the send queue don't drag in the whole wire-record set), and `EnqueueOrFreeNode` (0x4393d0) /
`StopThreadAndWait` (0x4394e0) are its members. Distinct from `g_pDPlaySessionMgr` (DPlaySessionMgr) and
`g_pNetManager` (0x48525c, the 0x160c-byte DirectPlay connection object). Field map (v254 survey
+ transcription):
`+0x00` own vtable (`0x4781c4`, unexplored), `+0x04`/`+0x08` ctor-arg context pointers,
`+0x0c bStopRequestedMaybe` (connected/stop gate), `+0x0d bDispatchBusyMaybe` (DispatchMessage
reentrancy gate), `+0x10 dpidCurrentPlayerMaybe`, **three `PeerTrainNode*` list heads (node
next@+0x70): `+0x14 pTrainListActiveMaybe` (drained as notify 0xf), `+0x18
pTrainListAwaitingAckMaybe` (sync-sent, drained as notify 0x11), `+0x1c pTrainListRehomedMaybe`
(removed/rehomed)**, `+0x20 nTickCounterMaybe`, `+0x24 nTrainAdvanceIntervalMaybe` (init 0x14),
`+0x28 pOutboundTransfersMaybe` (`FileTransferNode*`), `+0x2c pInboundTransfersMaybe`
(inbound file-transfer/per-player records, SAME `FileTransferNode` node type as +0x28), `+0x30
bStateFlag30Maybe`, `+0x34 nPendingFileReceiveCountMaybe` (0 ⇒ teardown).

**Transcribed (v254, `src/GameNet.cpp` — new TU, contiguous cluster 0x438e40–0x43d096):** the
inbound-message handlers are `__thiscall` **methods of `GameNetThreadState`** (Ghidra boxes
them in a plain `GameNet` namespace with `void*this` + the `GameNet_` prefix; modeled as members
so the thiscall convention reproduces). 4 EXACT: `GameNet_RemoveOrRehomeNode` (0x43a6d0),
`GameNet_HandleTrainStateAck` (0x43b6d0), `GameNet_DrainPeerListAsNotify` (0x43cbe0),
`GameNet_DrainBlockedTrainListAsNotify` (0x43cc40). Inbound train-sync/ack packets use
`TrainStateWireMsg` (`src/GameNet.h`: +4 trainId, +6/+7 owner bytes, +8 count). `PeerTrainNode
+0x8c dwAckPlayerId` (DPID of the acking peer) added this pass.

**Transcribed (v255):** 2 more EXACT + 1 EFFECTIVE, all `GameNetThreadState` methods.
- `GameNet_HandlePlayerLeft` (0x43a5c0, EXACT) — a player left: resolve DPID→slot, reset our own
  self-DPID to 1 if it was theirs, `RemoveOrRehomeNode` + `RemovePeerTrainsForPlayer` their trains,
  then walk the per-player inbound-file record list (`PlayerRecordNodeMaybe`, +0x2c) unlinking every
  record owned by the leaver — `CloseHandle` its transfer handle, post a type-0x18 notify, free the
  node (plain `operator delete`), restart from head — then post a type-0xb "player left" notify.
- `GameNet_RemovePeerTrainsForPlayer` (0x43b770, EXACT) — host-only (`connectionMode==2`): resolve
  the player→slot (or our own selected slot when playerId==0), then remove every active train owned
  by that slot (secondary owner if playerId!=0, primary owner if ==0) or acked by that player —
  flip its heading a half turn, re-stamp owner, clear each car's net-state (`CarNetObj_ApplyNetState`,
  cars 1..count via the shared `CarNetObjPartial`), post a type-0x11 notify, restart from head.
- `GameNet_HandleSelfStateRotate` (0x43a4b0, EFFECTIVE — intrinsic find-first loop peel, see
  docs/PARKED.md) — inbound "rotate self train 180°": post type-0x17, then if it targets our slot,
  find the matching active train and flip its heading a half turn (0↔180, 90↔270), post type-0x11.
  Uses `TrainRotateWireMsg` (+4 trainId dword, +8 owner byte — distinct layout from TrainStateWireMsg).

`CarNetObj` partial view consolidated into shared `src/CarNetObj.h` (was DPlaySessionMgr.cpp-local),
now used by both DPlaySessionMgr.cpp and GameNet.cpp.

**Transcribed (v256):** 2 more EXACT + 1 EFFECTIVE.
- `GameNetThreadState::GameNet_TeardownAndFlushQueues` (0x43ac10, EXACT) — tear down the DPlay
  transport: if a session is joined (`connectionMode==2`) send a bare 0x3fd "leaving" opcode + Sleep(10),
  then `g_pNetManager->DPlay_TeardownConnection()` + `delete g_pNetManager` + null the global; finally
  (host/local, `connectionMode` 2 or 0) drain all three train lists deleting each node via its virtual
  scalar-deleting dtor. Returns `char` 1. The 0x3fd send buffer is a 4-byte stack local where only the
  low word is written (`mov word[..],0x3fd`) — reproduced with a `struct { u16 wOpcode; u16 wPad; }`
  (a `short` local compiled a full dword store instead); the high word ships uninitialized (sic).
- `GameNetThreadState::StopThreadAndWait` (0x4394e0, EXACT) — shut the net worker thread down: if
  running, enqueue a type-8 shutdown command (→`GameNet_ProcessLocalCommand` case 8 = stop flag +
  teardown), then spin `Sleep(10)` until `g_pGameNetThread->Thread_IsRunningMaybe()` is false.
  Called from the clean-exit path (`Config_SaveWindowAndCleanExit`).
- `GameNetThreadState::GameNet_BeginFileTransfer` (0x439d00, EFFECTIVE — intrinsic register
  3-cycle, see docs/PARKED.md) — opcode 0x11: a peer requested one of our clipart `.att` files; alloc

  `HeapFree` are the genuine raw Win32 API here (not `operator new`/`delete` — resolves the old
  "needs cross-check" open item), and the exact error string is "Network Receive failed
  (GetNetMessage)\r\rDirect Play code: %s" (0x48185c — the v290 scoping guess dropped the

  Structure: loops on `IDirectPlay4::Receive` (vtbl+0x64, confirmed real signature
  `Receive(DPID *lpidFrom, DPID *lpidTo, DWORD dwFlags, LPVOID lpData, LPDWORD lpdwDataSize)` via
  raw disasm arg-push order) with two persistent scratch heap buffers held across the whole loop
  (`szMsgBuf`=0x7ff bytes, `szErrBuf`=0x400 bytes, freed only on the function's return paths).
  `lpidTo`'s own out-param storage is `&this->dpidLocalPlayer` itself — every receive OVERWRITES
  that field with whichever player the message was addressed to, not just our own id (usually a
  no-op since nearly all traffic targets us directly, but the field isn't purely "our own player
  id" the way its name suggests, `// sic`). `lpidFrom`'s storage is a fresh heap-allocated 4-byte
  int, reused across buffer-growth retries. Every receive uses a GROWING `lpdwDataSize` starting
  at `0x7ff`, growing by `+0x7ff` each retry while `hrLastResult == 0x8877001e`
  (DPERR_BUFFERTOOSMALL). On a real receive error (`hrLastResult != 0`): frees the message buffer
  + lpidFrom storage, then either silently returns 0 if the error is `0x887700be`
  (DPERR_NOMESSAGES — normal "nothing more to receive" exit) or formats+reports the HRESULT via
  `DPlay_ReportNetworkError`. On success, `*lpidFrom == 0` signals a RAW SYSTEM message (`DPSYS_*`,
  no Loco envelope) — dispatches on `*(uint*)lpMem` (opcodes `3`=CREATEPLAYERORGROUP builds an
  0x88-byte join-notify node, type `0x46`/70, DPID + truncate-copied player name, SAME 0x80-char
  truncate idiom as `DPlay_FindSession`'s password copy, `// sic` 1-byte overflow for a

  just the DPID; `0x31` calls `DPlay_TeardownConnection` then builds a 4-byte node, type `0xa`/10;
  `0x101`=host-migration, see correction above, type `0x3c`/60; `0x103` builds an 0x88-byte node,
  type `0x50`/80, DPID + truncate-copied address/name string (same shape as opcode 3's node, name
  at a different wire offset); `0x104`=session-name-changed, see correction above, type `0x5a`/90,
  0x404-byte node, only built if the name actually differs — self-echo suppressed). If a node was
  built, wraps it `{fromPlayerId=0, pPacket=node}` in an 8-byte `DPlayRecvMsg` and returns it (all
  4 heap buffers freed); if none matched (or opcode 0x104's names were equal), frees the message
  buffer + lpidFrom storage and loops back to receive again (silently drops the unhandled/no-op
  system message). If `*lpidFrom != 0` (a real app-envelope message): checks the WORD at
  `lpMem+2` == `300` (0x12c, matches `DPlay_SendMessage`'s own stamp) — if it does NOT match,
  reports "Version check failed on Network Message", optionally echoes a 4-byte `{type=0x1e,

    **Four more methods transcribed 2026-07-28 (v491)**, continuing v490's interior run — three

    - `RebuildCarSlotsFromSelectionMaybe` (0x44dea0, 156 B, **EXACT**) — re-spec the train parked
      on the selected DEPOT tile from the four-entry selection the train-config menu built
      (`WorldActionCursor::HandleMenuCommandMaybe`'s `0x3866` command): `anSelection[0]` is the
      lead unit's kind, `[1..3]` the three towed slots (0 = leave empty). The LEAD unit is
      retagged IN PLACE through `CarNetObj::SetCarTypeAndCategory` (vtbl+0x3c) rather than being
      freed and rebuilt, so the locomotive keeps its identity across a re-spec; only the towed
      cars are dropped and re-allocated. Finishes by re-binding the train to the tile via
      `ClaimDecorObjMaybe`, which re-lays every car's track anchors around the new consist.
      ⭐ The first argument is a `TrackDepotTileObj *`, pinned by the guard's own two fields
      (`dwOccupancyClaim` +0x11c == 1 and `pOwningTrain` +0x120 non-null) and by the tile it hands
      to `ClaimDecorObjMaybe`; the return is `char` ("did anything change"), not `void` — both
      call sites discard it. The three towed slots are dropped by calling
      `PeerTrainNode_ReleaseCarSlot(1)` THREE TIMES with a constant index of 1, because each
      release compacts the survivors down into slot 1 for the next call.
    - `DetachFromBoardMaybe` (0x44e630, 406 B, **EXACT**) — unhook a train from every board-side
      cache still pointing at it, so the node can be released or re-placed without leaving
      dangling back-references. Order: stop the cars (`SetCarsReady(false)`), give back the
      CONNECTOR tile the train was crossing (dropping its claim-wait entry first if still queued),
      give back the DEPOT tile it had claimed (same, plus clearing the tile's owner/lock/claim
      triple through the shared slot-7 `ReleaseChannelAndDispatch`), then hand every anchor — the
      lead one and both sides of every car — back to its tile via
      `NameAnchorMaybe::ReleaseTileClaimMaybe`. Both grid-position pairs are re-armed to the
      {-1,-1} unset sentinel, and BOTH board lookups add 1 to the Y: the stored row is the
      train's own, the tile it occupies is the row below.
      ⭐ The two switches resolve to DIFFERENT tile leaves, which is what makes the body
      cast-free: the `dwModeAMaybe` switch operates on a `TrackConnectorTileObj` (it is the tile
      `RemoveClaimWaiterMaybe`/0x44f410 is called on), the `dwModeBMaybe` switch on a
      `TrackDepotTileObj` (`bClaimLockedFlag` +0x128 and `KeyedList_RemoveByKeyMaybe`/0x412b50 are
      depot-only). Same inclusive `<= wCarSlotCount` walk and same guarded/unguarded asymmetry
      between its two car loops as `IsTileOccupiedByAnyTrainMaybe`.
    - `ClaimSlotForTrain` (0x44df40, 224 B, PARTIAL) — take the first free board slot for a train
      and give it somewhere to arrive: in a SOLO or HOSTING session an arbitrary station of the
      right category (`PickRandomBigObjByCategory`), in a JOINED session (`connectionMode` 2) the
      specific board tile the host named (`GetPlaneASlotMaybe`, with quadrants 1 and 2 — the two
      south-facing board edges — taking the row below). Answers 0 ONLY when the roster is full;
      failing to find any arrival tile is not a failure, the train just parks in sound state 3.
      `coord` arrives BY VALUE as one dword (`ret 0xc`).

### Opcode dispatch and handlers

**`GameNet_DispatchMessage` (0x4396c0)** — the gameplay opcode dispatcher (~20 Loco opcodes:
0xa, 0x14, 0x3c, 0x3e8, 0x3ea–0x3fd). **Transcribed PARTIAL 2026-07-19** (`src/GameNet.cpp`,
`GameNetThreadState::GameNet_DispatchMessage`, this-typed; drains `DPlay_ReceiveAndDispatch`
in a loop and fans each message out by 16-bit opcode). A real 20-entry jump table (`opcode-0x3ea`,
dense 0..0x13, table at 0x439ca4) handles the `>=0x3ea` range. **The outer opcode dispatch is a
flat cascading if/else-if chain matching the disasm's literal `cmp/jg/je` shape, NOT nested range
guards** (2026-07-19 register-allocation pass, v264): `if (wOpcode<=0x14) {...} else if
(wOpcode<=0x3e8) {...} else {switch(...)}`, with the LAST-tested condition at each tier
(teardown/0xa, redirect/0x3c) written as the innermost/`else` branch so the compiler places it as
the fall-through — matching the original's layout where the range-boundary/first-tested branches
are jumped-away targets and the last equality check stays inline (same branch-order-as-fall-
-through lever as the `PostBag_ScanCategoryCrdFilesMaybe`/`AlbumCardWnd::DrawOrEraseCardSlot` precedents,
here nested two levels deep). `wOpcode` must be a plain (signed) `int`, not `unsigned short`/
`unsigned int` — a narrower local left the comparisons on the raw 16-bit `ax` register with
unsigned `jbe`/`ja` opcodes instead of the original's `xor eax,eax; mov ax,[mem]` zero-extend-then-
32-bit-signed-compare idiom (`cmp eax,N; jg`). **The jump-table case bodies are laid out in the
ORIGINAL's memory order `0xe,0x13,7,6,0,1,2,8,9,0xa,0xb,0xc,0xf,0xd,0x10,0x11,0x12,4`** (decoded
from the raw dword table at 0x439ca4) — an earlier attempt mis-sorted this (put `0x13` before
`0xe`; the real jump-table addresses are `0xe`→0x4398ca < `0x13`→0x439916, so `0xe` sorts first),
which alone was worth ~270k of the total asmscore weight. Case `0xc` does NOT share the
`enqueue_tail` goto target with cases 6/7 (its own tail jumps straight to `post_switch` with no
register reload, a distinct physical call site) — confirmed via raw disasm at each case's actual
exit jump target. These 3 fixes took the function's `asmscore --dump` total weighted score from
2,019,714 → 627,414 (69% reduction); remaining residual is dominated by the well-precedented
`ebp`/`ebx` symmetric register-swap class (Yoda #29/#30) plus the same redundant-`g_pNetManager!=0`
-recheck fold already parked EFFECTIVE in the sibling `GameNetThread_TickLoop` (0x439240) — next
session should `asmscore --dump` case-by-case from here rather than re-deriving the top-level shape.

**2026-07-19 fine-grained case-by-case pass (v265), asmscore 627,414 → 568,617 (9.4% further
reduction), 3 real bugs fixed, still PARTIAL:**
1. **Case 7 (`0x3ea`+7, `RosterSnapshotWireMsg`) was missing `dpidCurrentPlayerMaybe =
   lpMem->fromPlayerId;` as its first statement** — the raw disasm at 0x439925 shows `mov
   edx,[esi]; mov [edi+0x10],edx` BEFORE the `new NetMsgQueueNode()` call (`this+0x10` is the
   confirmed `dpidCurrentPlayerMaybe` member, `GameNet.h:173`); this write was simply absent
   from the transcription. Found via raw-disasm cross-reference at the exact `asmscore --dump`
   offset (0x265) — the v264 pickup's own guess that this lived in "case 4/clipart" was wrong;
   the jump table (`0x439ca4`, 20 dwords) decodes slot 7 → 0x439925, not case 4.
2. **The same case's 9-slot roster-unpack loop cached `pSlots` in a local pointer, violating
   the aliasing rule (Yoda #19)** — the original RELOADS `pNode->pPayload` fresh every
   iteration (`mov ecx,[esi+8]` at the loop top) rather than keeping a cached pointer live
   across the loop. Fixed by dropping the `pSlots` local entirely and subscripting
   `((DPlaySessionMgrProviderSlot*)pNode->pPayload)[i]` directly. The loop's exact register
   residency (original keeps a persistent `edi` byte-offset + `ebp` records pointer in
   registers; our compile spills both to stack slots under the extra register pressure from
   fix 1) did not fully resolve — parked, see below.
3. **`Profile_SavePlayerUserFile` (0x4532a0, called from case 0) was declared with the wrong
   calling convention** — plain (`__cdecl`-default) instead of `__fastcall`. Ghidra's own
   decompile already shows `void __fastcall Profile_SavePlayerUserFile(LocalPlayerIdentity
   *param_1)`, and BOTH real call sites (`0x439a43` here, `0x4226d6` in a different TU) do a
   bare `mov ecx,[g_pLocalPlayerIdentity]; call` with no push and no post-call `add esp`
   — a single-arg `__fastcall`, not a stack-passed pointer arg. Our old declaration
   (`src/LocalPlayerIdentity.h:25`) compiled a spurious `push`+cleanup at the call site.
   Fixed by adding `__fastcall` to the declaration; verified no regression in the other TU that
   includes this header (`DPlaySessionMgr.cpp`/`EditCardWnd.cpp` don't call it, so it was inert
   there, but re-checked their own match counts unchanged anyway).
Also confirmed via raw disasm: case 0's early reads of `pMsg->bStateFlag`/`pMsg->sessionId`
(BEFORE the train-heading-reset loop that doesn't touch either) are genuine SOURCE ORDER, not
compiler hoisting — the original loads both fields textually before the loop even though they're

**2026-07-19 continued (v267), asmscore 568,617 → 501,479 (11.8% further reduction), 1 real
structural bug + 1 real calling-convention bug fixed, still PARTIAL:**
1. **The v265 pickup's own conclusion that the scattered `mov ecx,[g_pDPlaySessionMgr]`/
   `[DAT_004fd3b0]` `-`/`+` diff lines were "diff-alignment noise" was WRONG** — a raw
   relocation-count audit (`objdump -r -b coff-i386` on `build/GameNet.obj`, counting
   `g_pDPlaySessionMgr` reloc sites and comparing 1:1 against the original's own `4fd3ac`
   occurrences) found the candidate had 13 reload sites vs. the original's 12, a real (if
   small) extra. Root cause: **cases 6 and 7 (adjacent in jump-table layout order) both
   `goto`'d the SAME far-away `enqueue_tail:` label also shared by `resolve_and_enqueue`
   (cases 0xa/0xb/0xf)** — but the original's case 6 has a bare `jmp` straight into case 7's
   OWN inline tail (raw disasm: `0x43998b jmp 0x439a03`, landing on case 7's own `mov
   ecx,[g_pDPlaySessionMgr]; call EnqueueOrProcessLocalNodeMaybe`), a DIFFERENT physical call site
   than the one `resolve_and_enqueue` shares among 0xa/0xb/0xf. Our compiler did not merge
   case 6/7's shared tail with the far one (too much intervening dissimilar code between
   them), so each of the 3 logical "goto enqueue_tail" groups (6+7, and 0xa/0xb/0xf) should
   get its OWN physically-local shared label, not one label all 5 cases point at. Fixed by
   giving case 6/7 a private `case6_7_enqueue:` label placed inside case 6's own `if` block
   (case 7 jumps forward into it) — required hoisting `LayoutNameWireMsg *pMsgLayoutMaybe`
   to a plain (uninitialized-at-declaration) function-top local, since VC5 emits a hard
   `C2362` ("initialization of 'pMsg' is skipped by 'goto'") if a goto target sits past a
   local's OWN initializing declaration inside the block it jumps into — a plain assignment
   statement (not a declaration+initializer) is not an initialization-skip and compiles
   fine. This is a refinement of the existing "a shared `goto <label>` tail DOES merge under
   /O2" lesson: the merge is local/trace-driven (Yoda #15's geography), NOT global across
   every `goto` to the same C-level label name — 2+ logically-identical gotos to one label
   can still compile to 2+ DISTINCT physical tail blocks if they're far apart in the jump-
   table's own layout order, and each such cluster needs its own label to reproduce that.
2. **`PostBag_BuildClipartFilePath` (0x445700, called from case 4) was declared as a plain
   free `__stdcall` function, but is really a genuine `__thiscall` method of
   `PostBagCacheBundle` that never reads its own `this`** — the same "this-in-ecx but never
   read" class already documented for `PostBagCacheBundle::PostBag_BuildAttFilePath`
   (`src/PostBag.h`). ALL 4 real call sites (3 in still-untranscribed
   `NetResource_RequestMissingAppearances` at 0x438ed6/0x438fe6/0x4390db, 1 here at
   0x439bf4) load `ecx=g_pPostBagCache` (`DAT_004fd3b0`) immediately before the call —
   confirmed via `get_xrefs_to` + raw disasm at all 4 sites. The callee's own compiled body
   is unaffected (still `__stdcall`, byte-identical either way since it never touches ecx —
   verified `src/EditCardWnd.cpp`'s own match unchanged), so only the CALLER needed fixing:
   added a member declaration to `PostBagCacheBundle` (mirroring `PostBag_BuildAttFilePath`'s
   existing "member decl for call sites, free extern for the definition" split) and changed
   this call site to `g_pPostBagCache->PostBag_BuildClipartFilePath(...)`.

  local install cannot resolve. Three request sources, each with the same existence test:
  (1) the card's up-to-128 `decalSlots`, walked until the first empty `placementSeq` and
  **deduplicated** through a temporary 12-byte `MissingClipartNode` list (one card usually stamps
  the same sticker many times, so the raw slot array would request duplicates); (2) the corner
  badge `byStampSlotA`/`byStampVariantA`, packed via `PostBag_PackDecalKind(0x1e, variant)`;
  (3) `byStampSlotB`, packed via `PostBag_PackDecalKind(0x1f, 1)`. The existence test is
  `PostBag_BuildClipartFilePath` then "present if `g_RFIndex` has it OR `GetFileAttributesA`
  finds a loose file"; a miss sends a 6-byte opcode-0x3ed `ClipartRequestWireMsg` to
  `dpidCurrentPlayer` and bumps `nPendingFileReceiveCount`, which is what lets the inbound 0x3ee
  handler tear the connection down once the last file lands. ⚠ The request message's two selector
  bytes are in the OPPOSITE order to the 0x3ee reply's, and its `wPad` ships uninitialized — see
  `docs/engine-bugs.md`. Inbound opcode 4 (0x3ee) writes received bytes straight to a file
  (world/resource push to a joining client).

### File transfer

Two list roots on the thread state — **`+0x28` outbound, `+0x2c` inbound** (no function
touches both): `GameNet_BeginFileTransfer` (0x439d00, opcode 0x3fb/local 0x11; opens
`GENERIC_READ`/`OPEN_ALWAYS` — sending), `GameNet_HandleFileTransferBlock` (0x43a140, opcode
0x3fc/local 0x12; opens `GENERIC_WRITE`/`CREATE_NEW` — receiving; "Attachment
First/Interim/FINAL Block out of se[quence]" validation strings),
`NetFile_PumpPendingTransferSend` (0x439df0 — the outbound chunk pump, opcode 0x3fc).
**`FileTransferNode`** (0x1c): `kind`@0, `idWordAMaybe`/`idWordBMaybe`@4/6,
`hFile`@0xc, `blockCount`@0x12, `pNext`@0x18.

### Layout sharing

A previously-undocumented feature: share custom track layouts with other players. A per-slot
(0x4c-stride) array of named `.lay` bitmap layouts loaded from `%s\Layouts\%s[.lay]`,
exchanged over DPlay via opcodes 0x3f0/0x3f8/0x3f9/0x3fa and local commands 0x19/0x1b —
stored in `DPlaySessionMgr`'s provider-slot array (case 0x16 of the queued-event dispatcher
is the receive side). Functions: `LayoutNet_PostSimpleOpcode` (0x43d250),
`LayoutNet_SendCurrentLayoutBitmap` (0x43d350), `LayoutNet_ReplyWithStoredLayout`
(0x43d520), `LayoutNet_RequestLayoutList` (0x43d620), `LayoutSet_LoadSlotBitmap`
(0x43d6c0), `DPlaySessionMgr::LayoutSet_InitFromConfigFileMaybe` (0x43d820, PARKED DIFF
724/992), `ApplSetupWndPartial::LoadIndexFileMaybe` (0x409e70, PARKED DIFF 548/699),
`ApplSetupWndPartial::RebuildAndNotifyMaybe`
(0x40a150, EXACT)/
`SendSelectRequestMaybe` (0x40ac50, EFFECTIVE MATCH), plus a "layout sync queue" class around
`0x409e70`/`0x40a150`/`0x40ac50` (shared fields +0xec/+0xf0/+0xf4/+0x110) — see the
`ApplSetupWnd` writeup above for the full cluster status.

**Naming-promotion sweep (v286), `GameNetThreadState`/wire messages:** `FileTransferNode`/
`FileRequestWireMsg`'s `wAttId`/`wXferId` (was `idWordAMaybe`/`idWordBMaybe` — attachment id /
transfer-match key, mirrored onto `FileBlockWireMsg`'s own `idWordBMaybe` for consistency),
`bOwnerByteA` (`FileTransferNode` +0x8, was `bUnk0x8Maybe`), `wTrainId` (+0xa, was
`wUnk0xaMaybe`), `bBlockStage` (+0x10, was `bFlag0x10Maybe` — a 3-value 0/1/2 stage, not a bool,
per `NetFile_PumpPendingTransferSend`'s own switch), `bCooldownTicks` (+0x14, was
`bFlag0x14Maybe` — a per-node rate-limit countdown reset to 0x14 after each service),
`wBlockSeq` (`FileBlockWireMsg` +0xa). `TrainStateWireMsg`'s `bOwnerByteA`/`bOwnerByteB` (was
`bOwnerAMaybe`/`bOwnerBMaybe`) and `TrainStateAckWireMsg::bOwnerByteB` (was
`bSenderProviderIndexMaybe`, +0x7 — confirmed the ack aliases the same wire bytes as the sync
message, `+0x7` being the 2nd owner byte from OUR OWN perspective). `TrainSyncCarRecord`/
`TrainSyncCarRecordSend`: `nCarTypeId`/`nCarCategory` (was `carTypeIdMaybe`/`carSubIdMaybe`) and
`bHasDetail` (was `bHasDetailFlagMaybe` — ⚠ renamed by EXACT LINE ONLY, not identifier search:
`PeerTrainNode` has its own unrelated field of the identical name used ~30× elsewhere in the same
2 files). `UnkTrailingMaybe` (+0x3a4) reconfirmed genuinely dead (write-only both ends, mirrors
`CarNetState::Unk0x398`). `PlayerRosterWireMsg`'s `sessionId` (was `dwSessionIdMaybe`, renamed to
match the ALREADY-established un-prefixed convention on sibling `SessionWelcomeWireMsg`/
`WelcomeReplyMsg`) and `dwCarCountDup` (already-understood sic/duplicate field, just dropped
Maybe). `GameNetThreadState` itself: `hInstance`/`hwndOwner` (was `unk04Maybe`/`unk08Maybe` —
traced through `GameNetThread_InitState`'s ctor-arg chain to `SplashWnd`'s own embedded
`WindowBase` fields, confirmed by `GameNetThread_ResetNetManager`'s own
`g_pNetManager->hWndParent = this->hwndOwner`), `dpidCurrentPlayer`, `pTrainListActive`/
`pTrainListAwaitingAck`/`pTrainListRehomed`, `nTickCounter`/`nTrainAdvanceInterval`,
`pOutboundTransfers`/`pInboundTransfers`, `nPendingFileReceiveCount` (all straightforward
Maybe-drops, already well-described). **Two real corrections that swap which field means what:**
`bSkipConnectMaybe` (+0xc, was `bStopRequestedMaybe`) — its only writer is
`DPlay_UiConnectHandler`'s URL-launch branch (user chose to launch an external URL instead of
connecting), its only reader skips the real DirectPlay connect attempt; it does NOT gate thread
shutdown. `bShutdownRequestedMaybe` (+0xd, was `bDispatchBusyMaybe`) — its only writer is the
type-8 shutdown command (`GameNet_ProcessLocalCommand` case 8), and once set the thread flushes
its queues and exits; there's no reentrancy scenario anywhere in the transcribed code. I.e. the
PRIOR session's comments on these two offsets had the roles swapped — `+0xc` is "skip connect",
`+0xd` is "shut down", not the reverse. `bSessionStateFlagMaybe` (+0x30, was `bStateFlag30Maybe`)
stays hedged — only the setter side (`GameNet_DispatchMessage` case 0, from
`SessionWelcomeWireMsg::bStateFlag`) is confirmed, no reader found yet.

## Train/car network objects and the decal editor

- **`CarNetObj`** (**0x450 bytes — the class is COMPLETE in `src/CarNetObj.h` as of v475**;
  ctor 0x40d500): the per-car network/identity object hanging off a `PeerTrainNode`'s car slots.
  Layout: `AnimDescRefObj0x477488` base embedded at +0x00 (0x88 bytes, a genuine base — the ctor
  calls its ctor directly), the car's own `CarNetState` card embedded BY VALUE at +0x88 (0x39c
  bytes, running to +0x424), `bStateAppliedMaybe`@+0x424, `nCarTypeIdMaybe`@+0x428,
  `nCarCategory`@+0x42c, then the anchor/mode tail: `pNameAMaybe`/`pNameBMaybe`@+0x430/+0x434
  (the car's two `NameAnchorMaybe` track anchors), `wHeadingMaybe`@+0x438 (0/0x20/0x40/0x60),
  `wUnk0x43a`, `bUnk0x43c`, `dwModeAMaybe`/`dwModeBMaybe`@+0x440/+0x444, `wUnk0x448`, and the
  `pOwnerTrainNodeMaybe`@+0x44c back-pointer. `0x44c + 4 = 0x450` closes the class against
  `PeerTrainNode_AllocCarSlot`'s own `operator new(0x450)` sizeof oracle.
  ⭐ **Until v475 that tail lived on TWO separate TU-local views** (`CarNetObjAnchorPartial` in
  `src/PeerTrainNode.cpp`, `CarNetObjModePartial` in `src/NameAnchorMaybe.cpp`) because the shared
  class stopped at +0x430 — a genuinely duplicated layout. The promotion retired
  `CarNetObjModePartial` outright and reduced `CarNetObjAnchorPartial` to methods-only (its
  methods take a still-TU-local `PeerTrainNodeTickPartial *`, which is what still blocks folding
  it away entirely). It cost **−294 B / −2 EXACT** in `/Og` TU-state rotation and was immediately
  repaid: the ctor **matched EXACT on the first compile at 351 B**, which independently confirms
  every offset in the promoted tail. See `docs/CODEGEN.md`'s "a constructor is the other half of
  that oracle" bullet. ⭐ **v477 got the −294 B back in full**, without touching either victim's
  source, on two further `src/CarNetObj.h` edits — see docs/PARKED.md's v475 section, now a
  resolved worked example rather than a live park.

  **`wUnk0x448` is a DRAW-PLANE selector** (resolved v477, having been "written but never
  observed read" since v475): `HitTestTileMaybe` below compares it against a caller-supplied
  plane number as its first test, and `PeerTrainSlotQueueMaybe::FUN_0044e2e0` drives that with 1
  (the plane it is repainting) and then 0, so a car draws on exactly one of two planes.

  **Every function in Ghidra's `CarNetObj` namespace is now transcribed** (`src/CarNetObj.cpp`,
  9 markers): ctor **0x40d500** (351 B, EXACT); the dtor pair **0x40d660**/**0x40d680** (30 + 201
  B, both EXACT first compile — releases both anchors through `NameAnchorVtblProbe`, drops the
  owner back-pointer, and repaints the car's last rect via `g_worldBoard.MarkRectDirty` unless
  the owning train's `bHasDetailFlagMaybe` says the whole train is already being torn down);
  `CarNetObj_GetAppliedState` **0x40d750** (20 B, EXACT — returns `&pCar->stateMaybe` only while
  the latch is set); `CarNetObj_ApplyNetState` **0x40d770** (275 B, EFFECTIVE — the card-latch
  three-way, whose body is the inlined `CarNetState::operator=` that served as v474's layout
  oracle); `ResolveBothAnchorsToPointMaybe` **0x40d890** (79 B, EXACT — seats the A anchor on the
  tile under a pixel point and the B anchor 0x16 px to the right of where A actually landed, read
  back off A rather than recomputed, then re-centers the sprite); `CarNetObj_GetCarTypeId`
  **0x40e0d0** (18 B, EXACT — answers -1 when the base never resolved a kind descriptor);
  **`SetCarTypeAndCategory` 0x40e0f0** (57 B, EXACT — **this IS vtable slot 15**, see below);

  ⚠ **`RetagKind` never existed.** Until v477 the class modeled slot 15 as a declared-only
  `RetagKind(unsigned short, int)` PLUS an inline `SetCarTypeAndCategory` wrapper dispatching to
