  0x40e0f0, which is Ghidra's own `SetCarTypeAndCategory`. It byte-matched throughout (an inline
  wrapper around a virtual emits the same `call [reg+0x3c]`), which is why it survived so long;
  see CLAUDE.md's struct-discipline rule on checking the vtable before naming a slot. The real
  body stamps `nCarTypeIdMaybe`, reloads the base descriptor via a CLASS-QUALIFIED
  `AnimDescRefObj0x477488::SetDescriptor` (a direct call, not a slot-6 dispatch), and refreshes
  `nCarCategory` from `MapCarTypeIdToCategoryMaybe` only if that reload succeeded.
  **`MapCarTypeIdToCategoryMaybe` (0x40eb60, 206 B COMDAT incl. both switch tables, EXACT)** is
  the id→category map: 1 = the locomotive kinds 0x1804/0x1806/0x1808, 2 = 0x1866/0x1868/0x186a,
  3 = 0x186c/0x186e, 4 = the 0x1870/0x1871 hand-off pair, 0 = everything else. Its home TU is
  `src/CarKindDesc.cpp` (it is the last COMDAT of that .obj's address range), declared in
  `src/CarKindDesc.h`; its other two callers are the `PeerTrainRoster` train-spawn sites. ⚠ The two accessors are deliberately kept as free `__fastcall` taking `void *`
  rather than real methods: that matches their declarations in `src/CarNetState.h` and their ~20
  call sites across `src/DPlaySessionMgr.cpp`/`src/GameNet.cpp`, which reach cars through
  `PeerTrainNode::carSlots` (typed `TilePlacedObjPartial *`). fastcall-with-one-pointer and
  thiscall are the same call shape, so the two forms are byte-identical; promoting them means a
  cast at every call site in two codegen-sensitive TUs and should be priced as its own change.
  The ctor populates the whole +0x430 tail ONLY when the base's `bValid` came back true (i.e. the
  kind id resolved); the four stores above the guard — both anchor pointers, the owner
  back-pointer and `nCarTypeIdMaybe` — happen unconditionally, so a rejected car has NULL anchors
  rather than garbage, which is exactly the state `PeerTrainNode`'s own ctor tests for.

- **`PeerTrainNode`** (0x94 bytes, ctor 0x44be50; full Ghidra struct): one per remote train,
  keyed by `trainId`@+0x7a / `ownerByte`@+0x78, linked via next@+0x70. **Genuinely
  polymorphic** — `pVtbl`@+0x00 (its `vtbl[0](1)` release is the idiom the queue-teardown
  paths call on unconsumed type-0xe/0x10 payloads, see GameNet section). `+0x4` is
  `nDiscardFlag` (renamed 2026-07-20, ex-`dwUnk0x04`): `==1` means "release/delete this node
  now" (checked by `TrainNet_HandleMoveRequest`, `GameNet_ConnectOrJoinSession`,
  `HandleQueuedTrainConnect`, `RemovePeerTrainsAndSlot`); the ctor's `mode` arg is sometimes
  `2`, a distinct transient spawn state some consumers fold into "discard" and others don't —
  not fully resolved. `wHeading`@+0x74 (renamed from `dwUnk0x74`/`dwHeadingMaybe` — was a
  WORD, not a dword; see below) is a countdown/heading-reuse field: `GameNetThread_TickLoop`
  decrements it per-tick on `GameNetThreadState.pPeerListHeadMaybe`'s chain (same struct —
  that field IS this one) and tears the peer down at 0, while `TrainNet_PostMoveRequestForNode`/
  `GameNet_ConnectOrJoinSession` both stamp it with a heading value or a long sentinel
  (32000) respectively — same storage, different producer's meaning. **CORRECTED
  2026-07-20:** the adjacent word at `+0x76`, `wLocalHeading`, was previously documented/
  commented as "high half of the old dword, zeroed with `wHeading`" (implying it's basically
  padding/unused) — this is WRONG. `TrainNet_AdvanceLocalTrainSteps` (0x43bb00) and
  `TrainNet_TryBoardEdgeHandoffMaybe` (0x43c160) actively read/write `+0x76` as a genuine SECOND,
  independent heading field driving LOCAL track-junction-following, on code paths that never
  touch `+0x74` (the NETWORK hand-off heading, touched only by the network hand-off/blocked-
  queue reversal logic). `wHeading`/`wLocalHeading` are two adjacent shorts from a legacy
  merged dword that share only a zero-init call site — both are load-bearing, distinct
  fields, not padding. `bHasDetailFlagMaybe`@
  +0x88 is set by both `TrainNet`/`GameNet` producers when queuing a command for this node;
  purpose beyond "command pending" not yet pinned. **4** car-slot
  pointers (+0x10/+0x14/+0x18/+0x1c) — `PeerTrainNode_AllocCarSlot` (0x44c220) allocates up
  to 3 via its own counter@+0xc. **Read in full v353** (`src/PeerTrainNode.cpp`, EFFECTIVE):
  it refuses once the counter reaches 3 OR the slot ONE PAST the current end is occupied (the
  counter doubles as the highest live index, so the +1 probe is the real "is there room" test),
  bumps the counter BEFORE constructing, `new`s a **0x450-byte** `CarNetObj` under `/GX` — that
  literal is the authoritative `sizeof(CarNetObj)` oracle — stamps the car's
  `pOwnerTrainNodeMaybe`@+0x44c back-pointer, and on a car whose ctor left `bValid` clear
  rolls the whole thing back (`delete`, slot cleared, counter decremented). Returns
  `unsigned char`, not int (both failure exits `xor al,al` over the hoisted success value). `PeerTrainNode_UpdateSelectedCar` (0x44d6c0) switches
  between 2 remembered car ids (+0x24/+0x26) into +0x58. A local movement/stall-detection
  block at `+0x7e..+0x86`, driven every tick by `TrainNet_AdvanceLocalTrainSteps`: signed
  `wPosX`/`wPosY`@+0x7e/+0x80 (current tile x/y, read via `movsx` with `0xffff`/-1 as an
  "unset" sentinel), `bStallStepCounter`@+0x82 (ticks since the last stall checkpoint
  re-check; incremented each tick position changes, compared against a randomized threshold
  `rand()/6553+3`, reset to 0 when the threshold fires), and signed `wCheckpointPosX`/
  `wCheckpointPosY`@+0x84/+0x86 (tile x/y at the last stall checkpoint, compared against
  `wPosX`/`wPosY` when the threshold fires to detect the train hasn't actually progressed —
  triggers a random-reroute).
  `PeerTrainSlotQueueMaybe::SpawnOrAssignRandomTrain` (0x44dc10, transcribed v492,
  `src/PeerTrainSlotQueueMaybe.cpp`) — the roster's own train FACTORY, and the best oracle for
  what the game's random traffic is made of. Refuses outright once `nActiveCount >= 4` or
  `nOwnedCountMaybe >= 3`, scans for the first free slot, then builds the node one of two ways:
    * **`pTrainRecord == NULL`** (idle traffic / screen-saver): the locomotive kind is drawn from
      the three 0x1804/0x1806/0x1808 kinds (`rand() % 3 * 2 + 0x1804`), then 0..4 extra cars, each
      independently drawn from one of three families — **category 2** passenger (0x1866/0x1868/
      0x186a), **category 3** freight (0x186c/0x186e), **category 4** the single caboose 0x1870.
      The family selector is `rand() % 3 + 2` and IS the category number the arm then passes to
      `PeerTrainNode_AllocCarSlot` (see `docs/CODEGEN.md` #55 — the source's `+ 2` is recoverable
      from the emitted `add`/`sub` pair).
    * **`pTrainRecord != NULL`** (a loaded layout, or the train-config menu's selection): entry
      [0] is the locomotive kind and [1..3] the towed slots, 0 meaning "leave empty" — the same
      `anSelection` layout `RebuildCarSlotsFromSelectionMaybe` consumes, with a
      `SetCarsReady(false)` after the lead and after every car added.
  Either way the node is then NAMED `"<g_pLocalPlayerIdentity->name> <wTrainId>"` (format
  `"%s %lu"` at 0x47f030, `_snprintf` into a 12-byte local capped at 10) through car 0's own
  vtable slot 0xd, and REJECTED — destroyed via slot 0, slot re-cleared — if car 0 did not come
  up with `bValid == 1`, i.e. if the kind's descriptor never loaded. On success it bumps BOTH
  counters and calls `ClaimDecorObjMaybe(pTile, 1)`. Both parameters stay `void *`: the two call
  sites disagree on their real types (`src/NetSessionEventQueue.cpp` passes a
  `TrainPlacementRecord *` whose leading four ints are the consist, `src/WorldActionCursor.cpp` a
  plain `int[4]`). ⚠ `// sic:` when all four slots are occupied the scan falls out with `i == 4`
  and the shared exit returns `aSlots[4]` — one past the array, byte-aliasing
  `aSortScratchMaybe[0]`. Latent, not live: the roster-full guard above already refused that case.
  **The dtor (0x44c0d0, 118 B, transcribed EXACT v532, `src/PeerTrainNode.cpp`)** mirrors the ctor
  and is short: re-stamp vtable `0x47836c`, then — unless the app never had a session
  (`g_pDPlaySessionMgr == NULL`) or this node is a detail-flagged peer node that was never
  announced (`bHasDetailFlagMaybe != 0`) — tell the session the train's origin slot is free again
  via `GameNet_BroadcastLocalOrigin(wTrainId, bOwnerByteA, bOwnerByteB)`; then `delete` every
  occupied car slot and finally the lead `pNameMaybe` anchor. The car loop runs
  `0..wCarSlotCount` INCLUSIVE — the count doubles as the highest live index here exactly as it
  does in `PeerTrainNode_AllocCarSlot`, so a lone-locomotive train (count 0) still releases slot 0.
  Its vtable slot 0 is the `??_G` scalar-deleting thunk at 0x44c0b0 (30 B, left unclaimed per the
  ICF convention); consumers reach that through `PeerTrainNodeVtblProbe`.
  **`SetModeBMaybe` (0x44c150, 32 B, transcribed EXACT v532)** — was `FUN_0044c150`. Moves the
  train into mode-B state `mode` and re-derives the cars' ready flag from it: every state EXCEPT 2

  `TrackDepotTileObj::TryClaimForTrainMaybe`.
  **The ctor (0x44be50, transcribed v354, `src/PeerTrainNode.cpp`)** is the class's best
  field-name oracle. Signature `(int nKindId, int nDiscard, char bPeerOwned, char bHasDetail)`.

  top of the board (`ResolveTileAnchorMaybe(-1,-1,0)`, then

- **RESOLVED v432 (`TryMatchSocketMaybe`, 0x40b880 — TRANSCRIBED into
  `src/NameAnchorMaybe.cpp`, PARTIAL/PARKED; autopsy in `docs/PARKED.md`). Two corrections to
  earlier readings, both from the transcribed body:**
  - **It is a `NameAnchorMaybe` method, not a `BigObj` one.** Ghidra had it as
    `BigObj::BigObj_TryMatchSocketPointMaybe` with `this = BigObj*` (the v75-era reading, and the
    name it carried through v431). `this` is the ANCHOR: `+0x14`/`+0x08`/`+0x04` are
    `pTileMaybe`/`nSocketIndexMaybe`/`dwUnk0x04`, and the only `BigObj` in the body is
    `pTileMaybe->pKindDesc`. Renamed + this-typed + return-typed `TrackTileObj *` in Ghidra and
    `save_program`'d.
  - **⚠ Its RETURN POLARITY IS INVERTED from what the name suggests, and every caller depends on
    it.** NULL means the hand-over SUCCEEDED (the anchor now sits on the neighbour); a non-NULL
    tile means it did NOT, and is the tile that BLOCKED it — either the neighbour that refused
    (the two extended-chain ends) or this anchor's own unchanged `pTileMaybe` (no cell there,
    wrong category, or a closed-loop points piece that refused). So
    `AdvanceAlongTrackMaybe`'s `matched != 0` arm is the BLOCKED path, which is exactly why it
    goes on to inspect that tile's `dwTrackState` for 8/2/7/3 (dead / points / level crossing /
    reverse) rather than treating it as a success.
  What the body does: takes the world-pixel position of socket `nSocketIndexMaybe` on the
  anchor's own tile, converts it to a board cell, asks that cell's occupant for its ORIGIN
  (`WorldBoardMaybe::GetPlaneASlotGridPosMaybe`, 0x4557c0, ex-`FUN_004557c0` — renamed v432;
  returns the occupying object's own anchor tile position by value, or (-1,-1) for an
  empty/off-board cell, so a multi-tile object answers the same origin from every cell it
  covers), and then tests the point against FOUR of that neighbour's sockets: `1`,
  `wSocketCount - 1`, `wSocketCount + 2` and `wSocketCountExt - 1` — precisely the four indices
  `BigObj::IsEndSocketIndexMaybe` accepts, i.e. the two ENDS of each of the kind's two socket
  chains. On a hit it re-seats the anchor: old tile's `nOccupantRefCount--`, `pTileMaybe` =
  neighbour, `dwUnk0x04` = the step direction that walks AWAY from the matched end,
  `nSocketIndexMaybe` = that end's index, new tile's `nOccupantRefCount++`. The two
  `m_type0x63a == 0xb` guards on the extended-chain ends compare socket 0 against the chain's
  own far end and refuse when they coincide — a closed loop must not hand the train straight
  back onto the chain it just left. See `docs/engine-bugs.md` for its deref-before-null-check.

Not yet determined whether this identifies a specific board/world session vs. a plain connection sequence number — behaviorally clear, semantics still a "Maybe".
  - **`+0x1c` renamed `nextPostSeqId`** (dword) and **`+0x20` `postSeqIdString`** (`char[16]`, conservatively sized — real content is at most 8 chars + NUL) — found via `FUN_00453320`, retyped+renamed `AllocNextPostSeqIdString` (its lone param retyped `LocalPlayerIdentity*`, per the "plain param, not `this`" recipe since it's `__fastcall` not `__thiscall`). Body: formats `wsprintfA(postSeqIdString, "%03d %04d", clientId, nextPostSeqId)`, then increments+wraps `nextPostSeqId` at 9999→0, then re-persists the WHOLE identity via the same `.usr`-file body `Profile_SavePlayerUserFile` has (duplicated logic, not a shared call). The returned formatted string is used by callers (e.g. `CarNetStateAlt::FUN_00442a70`, hashed via `DPlay_ParsePortNumber`) to build unique per-postcard `PostBag\...\<id>.crd` filenames — i.e. a monotonic sequence number for generating unique postbag/card ids, persisted across sessions so ids stay unique run-to-run.
  - **The `+0x30`–`+0x120` span (240 bytes) — RESOLVED 2026-07-14 (v65), merged into one field
    `abRawProfileTail` (`byte[240]`).** Not missing fields: it's an opaque region that only
    ever moves as raw bytes inside the same `ReadFile`/`WriteFile(this+4/&kindTag, 0x120)`
    blob that also covers every already-named field from `kindTag` through
    `hasIdFlag` — no code anywhere (full `.text` sweep) gives it typed field semantics.
    `Config_LoadPlayerIdentityFileMaybe` (0x4530c0, was `FUN_004530c0`, this-typed) is the
    loader; for a brand-new player (no `.usr` file yet) its `CreateFileA` fails and the
    `ReadFile` never runs, so these 240 bytes are literal **uninitialized heap garbage** from
    `operator new(0x124)` at allocation, written verbatim to disk by the very next save
    (`Profile_SavePlayerUserFile`/0x4532a0 or `AllocNextPostSeqIdString`/0x453320's own
    duplicate save), then round-tripped unchanged on every later load/save. Ruled out lead:
    `EditCardWnd`'s cached `this+0x298/0x29c/0x2a0` color bytes belong to a wholly separate,
    freshly-allocated `0x39c`-byte `CarNetState` object whose own ctor zero-inits them —
    no read from `LocalPlayerIdentity` beyond the already-mapped `clientId`. Open
    only in the sense of "what was this originally *for*" (likely vestigial/cut-feature
    reserved space in the on-disk format) — not chasing further, no live readers exist. |
  | 0x0c | 4 | `nPostSeqId` (renamed 2026-07-20, ex-`Unk0x0c`) | post-sequence id: `atoi`'d from `AllocNextPostSeqIdString`, used as the `.crd`/`.att` filename and `PostBagAlbumIndexRecord::nId` — was previously folded into the tail of the old 7-byte `Unk0x09[3..6]`; now split out as its own dword. |

  | 0x3a | 2 | `wAttachmentId` (renamed 2026-07-20, ex-`Unk0x3a`/`Unk0x46`) | attachment file id (`PostBag_BuildAttFilePath`/`PostBag_DeleteAttachmentFiles`); nonzero gates the "has attachment" badge + an outbound appearance request; roster-checked, mismatch → "missing appearance" request |
  | 0x3c | 4 | `bAttachmentSoundPlayedMaybe` (renamed 2026-07-20, ex-`Unk0x3c`/`Unk0x48`, still hedged/uint not bool) | ctor default 1; `DPlaySessionMgr.cpp`'s arrival-sound check reads it as "already announced" when `0 && wAttachmentId != 0` |

  Additional construction paths: `CreateFromWireRecordMaybe` (0x442fa0),
  `CreateFromFileMaybe` (0x444c70), `InitFromWireRecordMaybe` (0x4428e0, shared init body).
  `SaveCardFile` (0x442a70, transcribed `src/EditCardWnd.cpp` v150, **EXACT match**) — see
  the PostBag family entry above for its full write-up; NOT a `CarNetStateAlt` method
  despite a prior session's namespace-boxing (corrected 2026-07-17).
  Sibling class **`CarNetStateAlt`** (`CreateAndFill`/`InitMaybe` 0x442a10/0x442ec0, own
  vtable `0x478268`, 0x390 bytes — a compact/alternate variant; struct not modeled yet).
- **`DecalSlot`** (6 bytes) — **the car sticker/decal system**: the game networks each
  car's decal placements so peers see the same stickers (car customization, not track
  telemetry). Field order is `packedKind` (byte 0: `(dirOrKind << 3) | (subIndex-1)`),
  `placementSeq` (byte 1: nonzero = occupied; an incrementing per-editor counter
  doubling as placement order), `xHalf` (byte 2: local X halved), `width` (byte 3:
  hit-rect width, from the thumbnail cache), `yHalf` (byte 4), `height` (byte 5) —
  a non-obvious x/width/y/height interleave. Methods: `AddDecalMaybe` (0x442c90 —
  fixed-128 FIFO, drop-oldest-when-full; the array base is struct-relative 0x96 in-memory,
  0xa2 on the wire — the 12-byte delta is the in-memory vtable+locals), `HitTestDecalMaybe`
  (0x442d30 — back-to-front `PtInRect` (center = stored×2), click-to-remove),
  `CompactDecalsMaybe` (0x442e00). Callers live in `EditCardWnd`'s mouse handlers
  (`GetCursorPos` → `ScreenToClient` → subtract car-art origin +0x1a0/+0x1a4).
  **Reader side confirmed 2026-07-17 (v159), transcribed `src/EditCardWnd.cpp`:**
  `PostBagCacheBundle::DrawPlacedClipartItem` (0x4440a0, PARKED) and `DrawLastPlacedItem`
  (0x4436c0, PARKED) both read the array via `CarNetState::decalSlots[128]` (`+0x96`).
  `placementSeq` doubles as `ClipartBitmapCache_GetOrLoad`'s own `slotIndex` arg (which
  numbered decal bitmap file to load, e.g. `"S0%03d.bmp"`) — the writer-side "incrementing counter"
  and the reader-side "which graphic" are the same value, not two separate roles. `xHalf`/
  `yHalf` confirmed *2 (a half-grid-cell dest offset) by the reader side too;
  `width`/`height` unread by either reader function transcribed so far. A duplicate
  Ghidra struct (`PlacedItemRecordMaybe`, created without checking for this pre-existing model)
  was found and merged onto this one, not the other way around — see the `PostBag.cpp` cluster
  catalog above for the merge writeup.

## Small object families and utilities

- **`TimeOfDayMaybe`** (byte-matched ctor/dtor 0x412620/0x412660) — small list-node/value
  class, embedded by `Obj0x4779e0` and used in pairs by the ScriptEventLoader. Field semantics
  PROVEN 2026-07-29 (v494, [TimeEvents] sscanf argument order): `m_8` = hour, `m_4` = minute,
  `m_c` = day-of-month, `m_10` = month (-1 = any). Three sibling window predicates exist, all
  `__cdecl (tm *pNow, TimeOfDayMaybe *pOpen, TimeOfDayMaybe *pClose)`: `0x412670`
  `TimeOfDay_IsDateInWindowMaybe` (day-of-year window over m_c/m_10, wraps New Year),
  `0x412710` `TimeOfDay_IsTimeInWindowMaybe` (minute-of-day only, in src/TimeOfDayMaybe.h),
  `0x412790` `TimeOfDay_IsDateTimeInWindowMaybe` (both; TRANSCRIBED EXACT v515,
  src/TimeOfDayMaybe.cpp). All three are renamed in Ghidra.

## ScriptEventLoader (the world-session manager, DAT_004a99b0)

RESOLVED AS A WHOLE 2026-07-29 (v494): the entire 0x41f4e0..0x4202b0 .obj is transcribed in
`src/ScriptEventLoader.cpp` — 12 of 15 functions EXACT (2074 B), the rest parked
(docs/PARKED.md v494). The class was previously known in pieces: the address-based
`EasterEggMgrAppView0x406ba0` methods-only view (src/EasterEggMgr.h, still the consumer-facing
declaration for AppWindow.cpp/LoadingScreen.cpp/Main.cpp), the `ScopedTimestampMaybe` orphan
class (src/ScopedTimestampMaybe.cpp — its ctor/dtor/??_G 0x41f480/0x41f4b0/0x41f4d0 ARE this
class's, and the "orphan code block" 0x45c655..0x45c675 is exactly its static-init + atexit
thunk pair), and the `g_easterEggMgrMaybe` singleton.

**Layout (size 0x14):** `+0x0` vptr (vtable 0x4779f4 — one dword ahead of SplashWnd_Vtbl
0x4779f8, sharing its ENTIRE slot run; provenance unexplained), `+0x4` = **g_dwGameTick**
(DAT_004a99b4 — the address every other TU knows as the game tick is really this class's
wall-clock field: the ctor `_time()`s it and the timer proc at 0x45c3c0 re-`_time()`s it on
every fire, so "tick" values are wall-clock SECONDS), `+0x8` [LoadEvents] list head,
`+0xc` [TimeEvents] list head, `+0x10` unlocked-easter-egg count (also the next ini key index).

**ee.ini** (`<install prefix>ee.ini`, ships in the RF archive; `loco/extract/ee.ini`):
- `[LoadEvents]`: `startDay,startMon,endDay,endMon,kindSlotId,remapTargetId` — date-windowed
  kind-slot remaps (seasonal art swaps). `LoadEventScriptsMaybe` (0x41f5e0) loads them into
  `LoadEventRecordMaybe` nodes (0x34 B, singly-linked at +0x30); `ApplySeasonalDateWindowsMaybe`
  (0x41f970) applies each in-window record via `UIResources::SetKindSlotPtrMaybe` + runs the
  easter-egg unlock on the target, and on October 31 sets `dwRenderFlags = 0x400` on every kind
  in 0x1800..0x198e (the Halloween reskin) then dirty-marks the board. `g_forcedSeason`
  (1=Apr 1, 2=Jun 11, 3=Oct 31, 4=Dec 2, 5=Dec 25) overrides the date first.
- `[TimeEvents]`: `startDay,startMon,endDay,endMon,startHr,startMin,endHr,endMin,effectKindId,
  effectMobility,period,type,x,y` — scheduled effect spawns. `LoadTimeEventScriptsMaybe`
  (0x41f6e0) loads them into `TimedEventRecordMaybe` nodes (0x48 B, +0x44 link) with a jittered
  first-fire tick; `ProcessTimedEventsMaybe` (0x41ff20) fires the first due one per call through
  the EffectSpawner and re-arms it (`rand() % period + 1`, or `rand() % (2 - period) + period`
  for period <= 0). The jitter guards carry the swapped-constants engine bug
  (docs/engine-bugs.md).
- `[EasterEggs]`: unlocked kind ids, keyed 1..N. ⚠ Read/written through `g_pIniFile`
  (LOCO.INI), NOT ee.ini — `LoadEasterEggsMaybe` (0x41f7e0) points a local IniFile at ee.ini
  and never reads from it. `RecordEasterEggUnlockMaybe` (0x41f8e0) bumps the count, appends the
  key, and only latches the descriptor's `Unk0x163Maybe` when the ini write reports success.

**The idle pump** `TickWorldIdleMaybe` (0x41fd00, called from the SelectedObjWidgetMaybe idle
path at 0x42ccb6): on 10-second multiples processes due time events, then posts every
game-window widget a 0x403 + 0x408 pair (Sleep 25 between) and a random sample (count/12, min
2, +1) a 0x402; on 20-second multiples posts each category-7/8 actor a 0x404 (Sleep 1); on
60-second multiples posts 0x406 with the tick. AppWndProc's matching cases: 0x402 = widget
slot 0x3c, 0x403 = `DecorObjMgrMaybe::TickObjSeqGoalsMaybe`, 0x404 =
`RestoreExpiredActorDescMaybe` (0x4202b0 — restores an actor's original descriptor when its
seq-reward claim window +0x68 expires), 0x406 = `UIResources::TickStationClockChimeMaybe`,
0x408 = widget slot 0x48.

**`ProcessInsertSeqSpawnsMaybe` (0x420000)** — the InsertSeq spawn pump (called from
FUN_004086f0_BigSwitch at 0x408908; `this` loaded, never read). Walks the game-window widget
list under the DAT_004fd3dc placement-eviction gate (saved/raised/restored); for each object
whose InsertSeq record's precondition ring holds (0x456d90), performs the record's spawn
payload (see src/CursorDesc.h's +0x568..+0x58f block): kind A pokes the object through slot 7
when it is 0 or the descriptor's own resourceId, else is placed at the front-row tile
(restarting the whole walk on success) with arg5 = 0 for the 0x3010-0x301b scenery kinds;
kind B spawns as a 'W'-code effect when category 0xe (position mode 'S' scroll-relative / 'W'
absolute / else object-rect-relative) else is placed likewise.

  at 0x434500 calls the ctor directly on its own `lockAMaybe`/`lockBMaybe` fields at `+4`/
  `+0x20` — see `DecorObjMgrMaybe` above). `Lock0x449410`/`FUN_00449420` (IAT-indirect
  `EnterCriticalSection`/`LeaveCriticalSection(this+4)` wrappers, widely used across
  `GameNet`/`DecorObjMgrMaybe`/world-idle-pump call sites) are the actual Lock/Unlock API —
  free functions, not virtual methods, despite operating on a polymorphic object.
